items.title: Evaluating Parallel Sampling Depth and Reconstruction Thresholds in Planned Decoders
items.summary: Masked diffusion models typically sample token rounds independently, whereas planned decoders generate a coarse plan before filling in tokens in parallel. Researchers investigated when and how effectively plans save computational rounds by studying broadcast trees where token dependencies are dictated by edge correlations. Findings indicate that decoders lacking a plan require significantly more rounds below the reconstruction threshold, while planned decoders can achieve logarithmic depth. Analysis reveals that a plan provides the greatest advantage near the reconstruction threshold, provided its structural units are kept small. Exact divergence calculations within a Gaussian model further confirm these theoretical lower bounds and exponents.
items.author: Chuling Wen, Weijie Liang, Jian Lu
items.original_title: The Price of Not Planning: Parallel Sampling Depth Peaks at the Reconstruction Threshold
items.original_summary: Masked diffusion models sample the tokens of one round independently. Planned decoders first generate a coarse plan, then fill in the tokens in parallel. We ask when a plan saves rounds, how many it saves, and how fine it must be. We study this on broadcast trees: the leaves are the tokens, the internal nodes are the plan, and the edge correlation $θ$ sets how strongly tokens depend on the plan. Errors are measured by the forward Kullback-Leibler divergence $\varepsilon$, and the lower bounds hold for every deterministic value-adaptive rule, also with learned conditionals. We show that a decoder without the plan needs of order $\min\{n,(n/\varepsilon)^α\}$ rounds below the reconstruction threshold, where $α=\log b/(4\log(1/θ))$ rises to $1/2$ at the threshold, and that the exponent stays below $1/2$ above it (binary channel: $0.02\leθ\le0.98$).

items.title: A database of optical and thermal-radiative behaviour of materials under solar radiation
items.summary: Solar-matter interactions are important in many scientific and engineering applications. Modeling them needs consistent optical and thermal-radiative properties over the full solar spectrum. Here we present SpaderOptics, a database for 21 materials: metals, oxides, semiconductors, polymers, ceramics, and carbon. It compiles wavelength-dependent refractive indices and extinction coefficients from the literature. Each literature source is kept separate, together with its original conditions. One physics-based calculation chain turns these data into reflectivity, transmissivity, absorptivity, and emissivity for different incidence angles, slab thicknesses, and temperatures. Combined with the Air Mass Zero (AM0) solar spectrum, the properties give absorbed, reflected, and transmitted solar flux for concentrated sunlight.
items.author: Vasiliki E. Alexopoulou, Nikolaos Karalis, Konstantinos Asimakopoulos et al.

items.title: Pulsar Timing Correlations Induced by Stochastic Spin-2 Ultralight Dark Matter
items.summary: Ultralight dark matter (ULDM) can generate time-dependent gravitational perturbations, providing a potential signal for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs). In Galactic halos, the velocity dispersion of ULDM gives rise to finite spatial coherence, which influences the correlations between pulsar timing signals. In this work, we derive the timing-residual cross-correlations induced by rapid metric oscillations of spin-2 ULDM, allowing for general polarization statistics. Under equipartition among the five polarization modes, the intrinsic angular kernel contains monopole and quadrupole components and exhibits an angular profile closely resembling that of spin-1 ULDM, suggesting a potential degeneracy between the two ULDM candidates in PTA observations.
items.author: Hao-Xuan Shi, Yu-Mei Wu, Chang Liu

items.title: Mono-Z Signatures of Vector Dark Matter Detection at Future Electron-Positron Colliders: FCC-ee and ILC
items.summary: We investigate the mono-$Z$ signature of a vector dark matter (VDM) model at future electron-positron colliders. In this model, a stable vector boson, arising from an extended $U(1)$ gauge symmetry, serves as a viable DM candidate that interacts with the Standard Model (SM) through a Higgs portal. We perform a detailed cut-based analysis for the mono-$Z$ channel at the FCC-ee (with $\sqrt{s}=240$ and $365$ GeV) and the ILC (with $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV), considering both leptonic and hadronic decays of the $Z$ boson. Signal significances are evaluated for benchmark points using fast event simulation with MadGraph5, PYTHIA8, and Delphes3. Our results demonstrate that future $e^+e^-$ colliders provide excellent sensitivity to Higgs-portal VDM, with the ILC's beam polarization offering an additional handle to suppress SM backgrounds.
items.author: Seyed Yaser Ayazi, Saeid Paktinat Mehdiabadi, Rouzbeh Rouzbehi

items.title: Hybrid Optimization-Generative Motion Planning for Multiagent Affine Formations
items.summary: Formation maneuver control enables a multiagent system to cooperatively navigate through constrained environments in collective motion. While various formation controllers exist, they rely heavily on high-quality and dynamically feasible reference trajectories provided a priori, making formation motion planning (FMP) essential. To address the computational challenges for high-dimensional joint trajectories faced by conventional constrained optimization-based solutions, this paper introduces a hybrid optimization-generative framework with a focus on affine formations, which provide the necessary spatial flexibility. By formulating the planning task as a constrained Maximum-a-Posteriori estimation, we decouple multiagent objectives to leverage pre-trained single-agent diffusion priors for dynamic feasibility, obstacle avoidance, and smoothness.
items.author: Zhonggang Li, Hongyu Zhou, Raj Thilak Rajan

items.title: A Density Functional Tight Binding Model for Rapid Screening of Spin-Orbit-Coupling-Driven Topological Properties in Bismuth
items.summary: We present a transferable Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) model for bismuth with explicit spin-orbit coupling that enables exploration of the structural degrees of freedom governing topological properties with minimal computational resources. We have used our DFTB model to run high-throughput calculations at a scale that would be significantly more expensive with standard Kohn-Sham Density Functional Theory (DFT) to determine a strain-buckling map of electronic and topological properties for bismuthene, where we identify regions of band gap closure and band inversion as a function of structural parameters. We show that our approach yields an accurate band structure for the rhombohedral phase, where small band gaps exist at or near time-reversal-invariant momentum (TRIM) points.
items.author: Nir Goldman, Ben Hourahine

items.title: A boson representation of the electronic structure calculation based on the quantum Krylov subspace algorithm
items.summary: Quantum calculations are expected to broaden the range of strongly correlated phenomena in solids accessible to first-principles calculations. The quantum Krylov diagonalization method, or in a broader sense, the quantum subspace expansion method (QSE) offers an advantage over other variational methods in terms of numerical stability. In this work, we propose a boson representation of electronic systems with the aim of reducing QSE quantum circuit depth, where electron-hole pair bosons serve as the fundamental degrees of freedom. We benchmark the boson representation in comparison with a corresponding fermionic QSE and CCSD for an equidistant and a dimerized configuration of a periodic hydrogen chain \ce{(H2)_n}.
items.author: Hiroki Katow, Hisao Nakamura

items.title: Jim Mirandy Transitions from Contractor to Civil Servant at NASA Stennis
items.summary: Jim Mirandy has transitioned from a long-term contractor to a civil servant at NASA's Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. Hired under a workforce directive to restore core competencies, Mirandy serves as a quality assurance specialist and close call investigator. Growing up with a father who worked in the aerospace industry, Mirandy developed an early interest in fixing things and problem-solving. After starting his career hands-on as a mechanic working on the Space Shuttle External Tank, he shifted his focus toward safety and quality operations. At NASA Stennis, he contributes to institutional safety through employee committees, training programs, and rigorous testing oversight that supports missions like the Artemis program.

items.title: Immersive virtual reality in learning physics: a systematic review of opportunities and challenges
items.summary: Immersive virtual reality (IVR) can heighten presence and enable active, embodied interaction in realistic 3D environments, which has been associated with potential benefits in physics education. This article presents a comprehensive review of IVR implementation in physics education at both school and university levels. The analysis included 34 studies indexed in Scopus and ERIC, published between 1 January 2018 and 1 June 2025. Methodologically, this review followed a preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses approach. IVR implementations for physics learning were assessed, topic-aligned activity types were summarized, and associated opportunities and challenges were documented. Findings indicate that IVR can support physics learning by providing complementary visualizations, optimizing cognitive load, enabling haptic learning, saving time, and fostering collaborative inquiry.
items.author: Andrej Vidak, Iva Movre Šapić, Vjeran Gomzi et al.

items.title: Deterministic nonlinear domain engineering algorithm with variable sub-coherence-length domains
items.summary: We present a new and improved deterministic algorithm that calculates the poling domains for the implementation of arbitrary phase-matching functions (PMF) in quasi-phase-matched nonlinear crystals for parametric down-conversion photon sources. In contrast to previous work, the algorithm presented here makes full use of the limits of the fabrication process, such as the minimum feature size and resolution of the lithographic process underpinning the poling procedure. This minimizes the tracking error to the target electric field and improves the accuracy in reaching the desired PMF. We give a tutorial on how to calculate the target function for arbitrary PMFs and run the algorithm.
items.author: Michael Schlosser, Tommaso Faleo, Gregor Weihs et al.

items.title: Allosteric Inhibition Reverses Hydrocephalus Caused by Shp2 Mutation in Mice
items.summary: Researchers discovered that the catalytically inactive Shp2 C459S mutation leads to communicating hydrocephalus in mice by impairing ciliary development and motility, differing from mutations that alter neurogenesis. Brain tissues from mutant mice exhibited elevated GAB1 and AKT phosphorylation, pointing to dysregulated PI3K-AKT signaling as the underlying cause. The study revealed that pharmacological inhibition of PI3K successfully rescues ciliogenesis defects and alleviates hydrocephalus. Furthermore, using the allosteric SHP2 inhibitor SHP099 increased the thermal stability of the mutant protein and reduced hydrocephalus symptoms. These insights demonstrate that the condition is driven by structural conformational changes rather than catalytic activity, highlighting the therapeutic potential of conformation-specific allosteric inhibitors.
items.author: Neoklis Makrides, Emily Sun, Hilal Mir et al.
items.original_title: Allosteric inhibition rescues hydrocephalus caused by catalytically inactive Shp2 in mice
items.original_summary: by Neoklis Makrides, Emily Sun, Hilal Mir, Jen-Zen Chuang, Ziyuan Jiang, Yihua Wu, Carlos Serra, John Peregrin, Qian Wang, Wellington V. Cardoso, Ching-Hwa Sung, Neel H. Shah, Xin Zhang SHP2, a protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) crucial in Ras-MAPK signaling, is associated with various human congenital diseases and cancers. Here, we show that the catalytically inactive Shp2 C459S mutation results in communicating hydrocephalus, similar to the catalytically activating Shp2 E76K and Mek1 DD mutants. Unlike previous mutants, however, Shp2 C459S/+ mutation uniquely affects ciliary development rather than neurogenesis, leading to structural abnormalities in cilia and impaired ciliary motility. Differential scanning fluorimetry suggested that SHP2 C459S , SHP2 E76K , and SHP2 C459S/E76K mutations all induce an open SHP2 conformation, but only SHP2 C459S leads to aberrant GAB1 phosphorylation in cells expressing wild-type SHP2.

items.title: Dendritic Depolarization Block Enables Single Neurons to Perform XOR Computation
items.summary: Using biologically realistic modeling, researchers demonstrated that single neurons can perform complex exclusive-or logic computations through dendritic depolarization block rather than relying solely on multilayer networks. Voltage-gated calcium channels facilitate a non-monotonic input-output relationship where moderate asynchronous drive generates spikes, but excessive drive causes a sustained plateau that suppresses output. This XOR-like computation is strictly governed by the temporal distribution of synaptic inputs rather than their spatial arrangement. The process remains robust across various dendritic configurations but fails under synchronous activation. Cross-morphological validation confirms that this frequency-synapse-count trade-off serves as a generalized biophysical mechanism for neural information processing.
items.author: Yanheng Li, Xiaojuan Sun, Yunliang Zang
items.original_title: Neuronal XOR computation requires temporally activated synaptic information
items.original_summary: by Yanheng Li, Xiaojuan Sun, Yunliang Zang Single neurons can perform complex exclusive-or (XOR) computation which is conventionally thought to need multilayer networks, yet the biophysical mechanisms and the robustness of such computations under stochastic synaptic drive remain unclear. Using biologically realistic modeling, we demonstrate that dendritic depolarization block provides a universal and robust mechanism for XOR-like computation. Voltage-gated calcium channels enable a non-monotonic input-output relationship: moderate asynchronous drive evokes spiking, whereas excessive drive induces a sustained plateau that suppresses output, naturally implementing XOR logic computation. This computation is strictly gated by temporal distribution of synaptic inputs rather than spatial distribution; the XOR-like response is robust across diverse dendritic configurations but collapses under synchronous activation.

items.title: New Framework Improves Epidemic Control Despite Incomplete Observation Data
items.summary: Incomplete reporting, testing limits, and asymptomatic infections often distort epidemic-control policies. To address this, researchers developed a three-stage computational epidemiology framework combining observation modeling, state reconstruction, and policy optimization. The approach extends a metapopulation SEIQR model and introduces ODE-DynNet, a hybrid model that uses mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics and graph-temporal learning to infer hidden infection states. Coordinated testing and isolation are then framed as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem. Testing the pipeline with community mobility data from Shenzhen, China, demonstrated an 88% reduction in infection costs compared to decoupled policies using raw proxy data, showing that explicit state reconstruction effectively supports epidemic control under surveillance gaps.
items.author: Shang Wang, Yuxiao Luo, Yunduan Cui et al.
items.original_title: Epidemic control under incomplete observations through mechanistic state reconstruction and multi-agent learning
items.original_summary: by Shang Wang, Yuxiao Luo, Yunduan Cui, Meng Zhang, Min Kang, Ling Yin Epidemic-control policies are usually optimized from reported infection states, but these reports are often incomplete because testing capacity, reporting behavior, delays, and asymptomatic infections vary across regions and time. Such observation gaps can distort the state used by the controller and lead to suboptimal testing and isolation decisions. We develop a three-stage computational epidemiology framework that links observation modeling, state reconstruction, and policy optimization. First, we extend a metapopulation SEIQR model to represent fully observable, steady partially observable, and non-steady partially observable surveillance regimes. Second, we introduce ODE-DynNet, a hybrid reconstruction model that combines mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics with graph-temporal learning to infer hidden infection states from distorted observations.

items.title: New Agent-Based Framework Evaluates Pneumococcal Vaccine Strategies
items.summary: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a major global pathogen responsible for severe pneumonia and invasive bacterial diseases. Although pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been widely deployed, their long-term effectiveness has often been undermined by serotype replacement, prompting the development of broader-coverage vaccines with lower individual immunogenicity. To assess the long-term effects of these newer formulations, researchers have introduced a flexible agent-based modeling framework that incorporates immunity, carriage, and clinical models. Unlike older paradigms that group serotypes strictly by vaccine type, this novel approach tracks individual serotype dynamics over time. The model's versatility was validated through a retrospective analysis tracking the sequential introduction of 7- and 13-valent pneumococcal vaccines in Australia.
items.author: Nefel Tellioglu, David J. Price, Xinghui Chen et al.
items.original_title: A flexible agent-based modelling framework of multi-serotype pneumococcal carriage to evaluate vaccine strategies in large populations
items.original_summary: by Nefel Tellioglu, David J. Price, Xinghui Chen, Violeta Spirkoska, Cyan Yingying Wang, Robert Moss, Natalie Carvalho, Kylie S. Carville, Patricia Therese Campbell, Jodie McVernon Streptococcus pneumoniae is a multi-serotype pathogen causing a substantial global burden of pneumonia and invasive bacterial disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been implemented worldwide, protecting against colonisation and disease from selected high-burden serotypes, but in many settings short-term effectiveness has been eroded by serotype replacement. Vaccines with broader serotype coverage have been developed, at the cost of immunogenicity against single serotypes. To determine the longer-term impact of these new formulations, we propose a novel modelling framework that evaluates the relationship between serotype-specific vaccine immunogenicity and effectiveness, comprising immunity, carriage and clinical models.
items.ai_title: New Agent-Based Framework Evaluates Pneumococcal Vaccine Strategies
items.ai_summary: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a major global pathogen responsible for severe pneumonia and invasive bacterial diseases. Although pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been widely deployed, their long-term effectiveness has often been undermined by serotype replacement, prompting the development of broader-coverage vaccines with lower individual immunogenicity. To assess the long-term effects of these newer formulations, researchers have introduced a flexible agent-based modeling framework that incorporates immunity, carriage, and clinical models. Unlike older paradigms that group serotypes strictly by vaccine type, this novel approach tracks individual serotype dynamics over time. The model's versatility was validated through a retrospective analysis tracking the sequential introduction of 7- and 13-valent pneumococcal vaccines in Australia.

items.title: Robust parametric estimation of avian cranial morphology
items.summary: by Kaikwan Lau, Gary P. T. Choi Quantifying morphology from 3D scans is increasingly central to comparative biology, yet many existing pipelines require labor-intensive manual landmarking and impose strict assumptions on the data quality, hindering the high-throughput analysis of large and often imperfect digitized collections. In this work, we develop a fully unsupervised geometric framework that extracts robust parametric descriptors of cranial morphology directly from imperfect 3D skull meshes. Specifically, utilizing tools in computational geometry, differential geometry, and numerical optimization, the framework automatically aligns each specimen, measures the primary skull dimensions, and fits geometric primitives to the orbit and the neurocranium via robust iterative schemes, yielding stable estimates even for topologically noisy or damaged meshes.
items.author: Kaikwan Lau, Gary P. T. Choi

items.title: Ten simple rules for creating and maintaining FAIR competency frameworks
items.summary: by Denise Bianco, Daria Sokolova, Matthew Forshaw, Clementina Ramirez Marengo, Emma Karoune, Kim T. Gurwitz, Vera Matser In a modern skills-based economy, competency frameworks are essential tools for workforce planning, career progression, and professional development. However, traditional frameworks often exist as static, isolated documents that lack digital connectivity and machine-readability. This article introduces a strategic roadmap to modernise professional standards by applying the FAIR principles: making competency frameworks Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. We present the FAIR competency framework lifecycle, an iterative model centred on end-user engagement, and outline 10 simple rules to guide creators through every stage of development.
items.author: Denise Bianco, Daria Sokolova, Matthew Forshaw et al.

items.title: Proteogenomic analysis of 5,411 plasma proteins in sickle cell disease patients
items.summary: by Cristian Groza, Arnaud Chignon, Ken Sin Lo, Vanessa Bellegarde, Pablo Bartolucci, Guillaume Lettre There are few therapeutic options to treat patients with sickle cell disease (SCD), a blood disorder caused by mutations in the β-globin gene that affects > 7M individuals worldwide. Combining human genetics and high-throughput proteomics can help identify new drug targets. Here, we present results from a proteogenomic analysis of the plasma proteome in SCD patients. We measured the levels of 5,411 plasma proteins and tested their associations with common genetic variation in 343 SCD patients. After conditional analyses, we identified 560 protein quantitative trait loci (pQTL), including 58 (10%) that are novel.
items.author: Cristian Groza, Arnaud Chignon, Ken Sin Lo et al.

items.title: Accessory regions shape genome evolution in the cereal pathogen Fusarium poae
items.summary: by Thomas E. Witte, Mohamed Elian, Jakob Bruggink, Chris Blackman, Linda J. Harris, Anne Johnston, Carmen Hicks, Anne Hermans, Whynn Bosnich, Xiben Wang, David P. Overy Fusarium poae is a widespread component of Fusarium head blight (FHB) pathosystems, frequently detected in cereal crops despite limited symptom development during infection. Populations of F. poae comprise closely related lineages with limited evidence of sexual recombination, raising questions about the genomic variation present within this comparatively cryptic pathogen and how it is organized. Here, a genomic analysis of 84 F. poae isolates, including 12 long-read assemblies, was used to characterize population structure and genomic variation within a predominantly contemporary Canadian collection supplemented by isolates from diverse international origins.
items.author: Thomas E. Witte, Mohamed Elian, Jakob Bruggink et al.

items.title: Experimental evolution of yeast reveals trade-offs between early and late stationary phase
items.summary: by Jason Tarkington, Aditya Mahadevan, Angelina G. Chan, Gavin Sherlock Stationary phase in yeast and other microorganisms begins when a limiting nutrient in the environment is exhausted and cell division ceases. Most cells subsequently enter quiescence and then lose viability. However, even in spent media, metabolism continues, and the environment can change over time, causing the relative fitnesses of genotypes to differ over the course of stationary phase. For yeast, how such fitness varies and what genotypes might be favored at what points in stationary phase is largely unknown. In this work we experimentally evolve S. cerevisiae in batch culture, varying the time spent in stationary phase between growth cycles, and we isolate adaptive clones.
items.author: Jason Tarkington, Aditya Mahadevan, Angelina G. Chan et al.

items.title: NF-κB/Dif-driven miR-1000 feedback restrains toll signaling via targeting Myd88 to restore Drosophila immune homeostasis
items.summary: by Chaolong Jia, Ju Li, Ning Li, Shangmin Yang, Linxian Sun, Shengjie Li, Fei Ma, Ping Jin Innate immune homeostasis is vital for animal survival and requires precise control of both the intensity and duration of immune signaling. Although microRNAs (miRNAs) are known to fine-tune immune responses, their transcriptional regulation mechanisms during infection remain poorly characterized. Here, we identify an NF-κB-dependent miRNA feedback loop essential for Drosophila Toll pathway. Through dynamic expression profiling and functional genetics, we demonstrate that the NF-κB transcription factor Dif directly activates miR-1000 transcription upon Gram-positive bacterial infection, while miR-1000 in turn targets the adaptor Myd88 mRNA for degradation.
items.author: Chaolong Jia, Ju Li, Ning Li et al.

items.title: Liquid–liquid phase separation: An emerging paradigm orchestrating the pathogenicity of plant pathogenic fungi
items.summary: by Yi Lou, Shiqi Ji, Lin Yu, Yakubu Saddeeq Abubakar, Wenhui Zheng The battle between plants and fungal pathogens plays out as a molecular arms race, shaped by constant and complex exchanges at the infection interface. Liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) is emerging as a biophysical organizing principle that operates alongside genetic and protein-interaction networks to govern fungal pathogenicity. LLPS enables cells to form dynamic, membrane-free compartments that are recognized as a critical driver of infection. In this review, we summarize recent advances showing how LLPS contributes to fungal pathogenicity by coordinating three core processes: the development of infection structures, the organization of virulence effectors, and rapid transcriptional reprogramming in response to host stress.
items.author: Yi Lou, Shiqi Ji, Lin Yu et al.

items.title: TXNIP contributes to HIV-1 transcriptional competence and inducible reactivation through an EZH2-ETV1 regulatory pathway
items.summary: by Ziyao Wu, Han Zhang, Taizhen Liang, Yuzai Zhang, Muye Xia, Chenliang Zhou, Yibin Li, Jie Peng, Shuwen Liu, Lin Li Persistent human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) latency remains a major barrier to durable remission, yet the host pathways that regulate proviral transcriptional competence and inducible reactivation remain incompletely defined. Thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP) is a glucose-responsive host factor, but its role in HIV-1 transcription and latency regulation has not been established. Here, we provide evidence that TXNIP supports HIV-1 long terminal repeat (LTR)-driven transcription, productive replication, and latency reversal. Genetic depletion of TXNIP reduced LTR reporter activity, nascent viral transcripts, virus production, and latency-reversing agent (LRA)-induced reactivation across reporter-based, productive-infection, chronically infected, latency, primary-cell, and ex vivo models, whereas TXNIP overexpression enhanced viral transcriptional output.
items.author: Ziyao Wu, Han Zhang, Taizhen Liang et al.

items.title: Evaluation of Lassa fever surveillance system in Edo State, Nigeria (2024–2025)
items.summary: by Paul Waliaula Wekunda, Oladipo Ogunbode, Zainab Dambazau, Oyeladun Okunromade, Musonda Chikwanda Introduction Lassa fever is a priority disease in Nigeria. Periodic evaluation of its surveillance systems is essential to strengthen performance and ensure efficient use of limited public health resources. This study evaluated the Lassa fever surveillance system in Edo State, Nigeria. Methods The evaluation followed the 2001 CDC guidelines and used a cross-sectional mixed-methods design. We reviewed statewide surveillance data from 2024–2025 and selected respondents from 26 health facilities across 15 of the 18 (83.3%) local government areas (LGAs), as well as from the state surveillance unit and WHO.
items.author: Paul Waliaula Wekunda, Oladipo Ogunbode, Zainab Dambazau et al.

items.title: Child marriage before and after the 2019 ban in Brazil: An interrupted time series analysis
items.summary: by Marcelo Luis Urquia, Maria Paula Godoy, Carolina Fonseca Leal de Araújo, Carla Adriane Leal de Araújo, José Roberto da Silva Junior, João Guilherme Bezerra Alves Background Child marriage, defined as a legal marriage or informal union of a minor, is considered a violation to human rights and is associated with adverse developmental and health outcomes. Brazil is one of the countries with the highest number of child marriages worldwide. In 2019, Brazil enacted legislation banning child marriage for Methods We accessed public-use anonymized marriage and birth registrations nationwide data in the period 2014–2024, with complete information on age and marital status.
items.author: Marcelo Luis Urquia, Maria Paula Godoy, Carolina Fonseca Leal de Araújo et al.

items.title: Burden and impact of infections among adult liver transplantation-related hospitalizations: A nationwide analysis
items.summary: by Sahiljot Singh Bhupal, Joseph Solomon, Saniya Jiwani, Carol Singh, Aalam Sohal, Mohanad Al-Qaisi, Nilofar Najafian Introduction The presence of infections in patients undergoing liver transplantation (LT) has been associated with worsened clinical outcomes. We aimed to examine the current burden and impact of infections during index LT hospitalization using a large national cohort. Methods We analyzed data from the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) Database (2016–2022) to identify all hospitalizations for LT aged >18. Hospitalizations were stratified into two groups based on infection status. Data collected included patient demographics, liver disease etiology, liver-related decompensations, comorbidities, and clinical outcomes. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate categorical outcomes, and survey-weighted generalized linear models with a gamma distribution and log link were used to evaluate length of stay and hospitalization costs.
items.author: Sahiljot Singh Bhupal, Joseph Solomon, Saniya Jiwani et al.

items.title: Informal help-seeking among Peruvian women exposed to intimate partner violence: A cross-sectional analysis of violence characteristics in the 2023 Demographic and Health Survey
items.summary: by Yordanis Enriquez Canto, Giovani Díaz Gervasi, Luis Menacho Alvirio Background Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major public health problem in Peru, yet many women who experience it do not seek help. We examined how the characteristics of IPV and individual and sociocultural factors are associated with help-seeking among Peruvian women exposed to physical and/or sexual IPV. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 Peruvian Demographic and Health Survey (ENDES). The analytic sample comprised 5,584 women aged 15–49 years who reported lifetime physical and/or sexual violence by a current or former partner and were asked whether they had ever sought help.
items.author: Yordanis Enriquez Canto, Giovani Díaz Gervasi, Luis Menacho Alvirio

items.title: Detectability of controlled leaks in an Andean water transmission main: A field evaluation of changepoint methods on flow and pressure signals
items.summary: by Holger Manuel Benavides-Muñoz, Peter Cheung Leak detection on pumped transmission mains that cross steep terrain relies on hydraulic signals whose response to a small leak may be comparable to sensor noise. We evaluated five unsupervised methods (PELT with Bayesian and Akaike penalties, Bayesian online changepoint detection [BOCD], an OLS-CUSUM structural-break procedure and a moving-average ±3σ chart) on flow and pressure series recorded every 30 s during seven controlled leak trials (valve setting 3–5% of nominal flow) in two field campaigns on an Andean transmission main in Loja, Ecuador. Detections were compared with a chance-level reference obtained by placing the same number of changepoints at random.
items.author: Holger Manuel Benavides-Muñoz, Peter Cheung

items.title: Succession of coast pine barrens to northern hardwoods in a lacustrine sand dune system
items.summary: by Grace W. Auckley, Jordan M. Marshall The Grand Sable Dunes is a perched lacustrine dune system within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore, USA, on Lake Superior. Wind provides disturbance which has continually influenced the successional pathways of these dunes. The objectives of this study were to identify the relationships between forest stand age, successional processes, and overall forest development by categorizing forest type and regeneration patterns, mapping the dendrochronological sequence, and quantifying coarse woody debris (CWD) accumulation in the Grand Sable Dunes. We surveyed the understory, midstory, and overstory woody vegetation across 43 plots. Cores from the four largest trees were collected and CWD volume was measured within each plot.
items.author: Grace W. Auckley, Jordan M. Marshall

items.title: Communication-aware dynamic graph learning for V2X misbehavior detection using GAT–BiLSTM and bagged trees
items.summary: by Yuee Zhang, Ping Wang, Xinyu Wang, Xiao Zheng Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication supports cooperative driving, which also makes the malicious vehicle-state reports influence nearby vehicles. Due to the isolated use of physical state and cross-time communication context, existing methods struggle to detect malicious reports that are physically self-consistent and only reveal inconsistencies at the temporal communication level. Thus, this paper proposes a sequence-level misbehavior detection framework based on graph attention networks (GAT) and bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM). Recorded sender–receiver interactions define a directed communication graph for each one-second window. The GAT can learn the neighboring information contributes to detection.
items.author: Yuee Zhang, Ping Wang, Xinyu Wang et al.

items.title: Intelligent classification of medically and veterinary important mosquito vectors using self-distillation-enhanced supervised learning
items.summary: by Santhad Chuwongin, Morakot Kaewthamasorn, Tanawat Chaiphongpachara, Sedthapong Laojun, Tawee Saiwichai, Naruchit Soiphet, Siridech Boonsang, Veerayuth Kittichai Mosquito-borne diseases remain a persistent global public health burden, with effective control strategies depending on the accurate and timely identification of mosquito species and estimation of their population density. The current gold standard, morphological identification via microscopic examination, is limited by inter-observer variability and a scarcity of local taxonomic expertise. While highly accurate, molecular techniques like polymerase chain reaction and DNA barcoding are often impractical for widespread field use due to their cost, procedural complexity, and reliance on specialized equipment and technicians. In response to these challenges, this study harnesses the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to develop a robust, accessible diagnostic tool.
items.author: Santhad Chuwongin, Morakot Kaewthamasorn, Tanawat Chaiphongpachara et al.

items.title: Enabling vs. directive: How performance management affects innovative performance through thriving at work
items.summary: by Vincent Goossens, Adelien Decramer, Mieke Audenaert Rapid changes in the business landscape push organizations to innovate. Scholars, practitioners and policymakers have emphasized the importance of innovative performance to remain competitive. This study investigates how directive and enabling performance management (PM) affect employee innovative performance. Drawing on the socially-embedded model of thriving, we propose thriving at work, the joint experience of vitality and learning, as mediating mechanism. Using three-wave, multi-source data from 461 employees and their supervisors, Structural Equation Modeling results indicate that: (1) enabling PM is positively related to innovative performance through both vitality and learning, whereas for directive PM only learning mediates the negative indirect relationship; (2) both vitality and learning are individually positively associated with innovative performance; and (3) learning only enhances innovative performance when vitality is high.
items.author: Vincent Goossens, Adelien Decramer, Mieke Audenaert

items.title: RGDfC-functionalized gold nanoclusters versus the clinical radiosensitizer sodium glycididazole in triple-negative breast cancer radiotherapy
items.summary: by Xiangchao Song, Lingwei Wang, Chunyin Li, Chengbin Qu, Jianyu Xiao Radiotherapy for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is often limited by intrinsic tumor radioresistance. The clinically approved radiosensitizer sodium glycididazole (CMNa) is restricted by its hypoxia-dependent activity and lack of tumor targeting. Integrin-targeted gold nanoclusters have been extensively investigated as radiosensitizers, yet direct head-to-head comparisons with CMNa are lacking. We synthesized RGDfC-gold nanoclusters (RGDfC-AuNCs) via one-step biomineralization and compared them with CMNa in 4T1 murine TNBC cells and tumor-bearing mice. The nanoclusters showed ultrasmall size, good stability, and exhibited enhanced cellular uptake relative to non-targeted controls. In vitro, radiosensitization performance was assessed by CCK‑8 assays under normoxic and CoCl 2 ‑mimicked pseudo‑hypoxic conditions.
items.author: Xiangchao Song, Lingwei Wang, Chunyin Li et al.

items.title: Exploring the associations of physical activity, social anxiety, perceived stress, and quality of life in Chinese college students: A network analysis
items.summary: by Fumei Yuan, Hong Wang, Wentao Qiu, Chaoliang Mao College students face complex interactions among physical activity, quality of life, social anxiety, and perceived stress. This study employed network analysis to explore these associations. A cross-sectional sample of 699 Chinese undergraduates (427 males, 272 females) completed the PARS-3, WHOQOL-BREF, PSS-10, and LSAS. A Gaussian graphical model was estimated using EBICglasso; strength, expected influence, and bridge expected influence (BEI) were calculated. Social anxiety and perceived stress were moderately to strongly positively correlated (r = 0.42–0.51), and both were substantially negatively correlated with quality of life, whereas after accounting for conditional dependencies, physical activity occupied a peripheral position, showing only weak partial associations with the psychological variables.
items.author: Fumei Yuan, Hong Wang, Wentao Qiu et al.

items.title: Development and internal validation of VA-BLED for 1-year esophageal variceal bleeding risk in cirrhosis
items.summary: by Dominic Denk, Silja Schröder, Mireen Friedrich-Rust, Stefan Zeuzem, Alexander Queck Background and Aims Esophageal variceal bleeding is a life-threatening complication of cirrhosis, yet current risk stratification targets portal hypertension stage and endoscopic stigmata instead of short-term bleeding probability. We evaluated whether a simple score built from routinely available variables could stratify 1-year esophageal variceal bleeding risk. Methods We developed and internally validated two multivariable logistic models in a retrospective outcome-balanced cohort of 108 patients with esophageal varices (54 variceal bleeding, 54 no bleeding). VA-BLED BASE incorporated Child-Pugh score, normalized alanine aminotransferase, and current alcohol use. VA-BLED HISTORY additionally incorporated previous bleeding.
items.author: Dominic Denk, Silja Schröder, Mireen Friedrich-Rust et al.

items.title: Prevalence of intimate partner violence against women in East Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: by Zekarias Markos, Esubalew Muluneh Aligaz, Sitotaw Tesfa Zegeye, Rahel Dinkneh, Temesgen Mamo, Sintayehu Samuel Lorato Background Intimate partner violence (IPV) remains a pervasive public health and human rights issue worldwide, with sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) bearing a disproportionately high burden. However, synthesized evidence specifically from the East African region is limited. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Forty-one cross-sectional studies reporting IPV among women in East Africa were identified from seven electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online [AJOL], CINAHL, and Google Scholar). Databases were searched from August 1 to September 30, 2025.Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal checklist for prevalence studies.
items.author: Zekarias Markos, Esubalew Muluneh Aligaz, Sitotaw Tesfa Zegeye et al.

items.title: Trends in Lyme disease incidence in England, 2013 to 2024
items.summary: by Janie Olver, Mark Gideon Burdon, Eva Emanuel, Ali Datoo, Verena FermorDunman, Miranda Ferguson, Jessica I’Anson, Roberto Vivancos, Christina Petridou, Amanda Semper Official Lyme disease incidence figures for England are based on the number of cases with a laboratory-confirmed diagnosis from the national reference laboratory. However, these figures underestimate the true incidence of acute cases since patients can also be diagnosed clinically without the need for laboratory testing. The use of a multiplication factor has been proposed to estimate total Lyme disease incidence from the number of laboratory-confirmed cases. The current multiplication factor is derived from data spanning 1998–2016 and is thought to be outdated, in part due to the introduction of new national Lyme disease management guidance in 2018.
items.author: Janie Olver, Mark Gideon Burdon, Eva Emanuel et al.

items.title: Development of a diagnostic biomarker panel for early-stage lung adenocarcinoma using serum-derived small RNAs
items.summary: by Daisuke Ueda, Ryou-u Takahashi, Yasuhiro Tsutani, Yukie Nishiyama, Yumiko Koi, Yuta Ibuki, Yoshihiro Miyata, Tomoyuki Akita, Junko Tanaka, Morihito Okada, Hidetoshi Tahara Objective Circulating small RNAs, such as microRNAs (miRNAs) and transfer RNA fragments (tRFs), reportedly reflect the physiological and pathological conditions in various diseases. Herein, we aimed to identify circulating small RNAs for the early diagnosis of lung adenocarcinoma. Methods This study included 40 healthy controls and 43 patients with lung adenocarcinoma. We analyzed their serum using small RNA sequencing and identified differentially expressed small RNAs between healthy controls and patients with lung adenocarcinoma. We verified the expression profiles of these small RNAs in 29 patients with lung adenocarcinoma and 27 healthy controls.
items.author: Daisuke Ueda, Ryou-u Takahashi, Yasuhiro Tsutani et al.

items.title: Performing the unspoken: Protocol for an ethnodrama study of caregiver burden among Arab migrant women caring for older adults at home in the Greater Toronto Area
items.summary: by Areej Al-Hamad, Yasin M. Yasin, Kateryna Metersky, Kristina Kokorelias, Cole Lewis Informal caregiving enables many older adults to remain at home, yet the work of family caregivers is often poorly recognized and unevenly supported. Among Arab migrant women, caregiving may be shaped by strong traditions of family responsibility, gendered expectations, migration and settlement pressures, language barriers, employment and childcare responsibilities, and limited access to culturally responsive services. This protocol describes a one-year, three-phase, arts-based community-engaged study developed in partnership with the Arab Community Centre of Toronto (ACCT). The study is guided by Ethics of Care and Intersectionality frameworks and aims to understand the caregiving realities of Arab migrant women who support older adults at home in the Greater Toronto Area (GTA), Canada, translate their narratives into ethnodrama, and co-generate actionable recommendations for community and service systems.
items.author: Areej Al-Hamad, Yasin M. Yasin, Kateryna Metersky et al.

items.title: Effective practice within day service centres for people with intellectual disabilities: a systematic review of quantitative research
items.summary: by James Belsey, Rachel Harrison Background This review aimed to identify areas of consensus, contention, and any gaps in the literature that may exist with regard to what constitutes best practice and effective provision for people with intellectual disabilities within day service centres. Materials and Methods The review was prospectively registered on the PROSPERO registry (ID: CRD42024585737) and conducted according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis guidelines. The International Bibliography of the Social Sciences, Scopus, and PsycInfo databases were searched in April 2026 for peer-reviewed research that investigated the effectiveness of day service provision in non-residential settings.
items.author: James Belsey, Rachel Harrison

items.title: Calculation of sequence space coverage in a mutagenesis library
items.summary: by Alberto Florez Prada, Guido Uguzzoni, Darren J. Hart Directed evolution requires screening of large mutagenesis libraries, but accurate calculation of library sizes needed to discover functional variants remains challenging. Existing models provide baseline estimates, yet current computational approaches for finding the best variants scale poorly with library complexity. Here, we introduce a scalable computational framework that overcomes the combinatorial scaling bottlenecks of previous top- k models. By aggregating variants into a composition log–sum distribution and applying log-space convolution across randomisation blocks, we extend coverage estimation to massive sequence spaces and mixed codon schemes. By inverting these calculations, we establish conservative screening upper bounds and practical ceilings on the maximum randomisable positions for experimental design.
items.author: Alberto Florez Prada, Guido Uguzzoni, Darren J. Hart

items.title: Integrative transcriptomic and single-nucleus analyses identify microbiota–metabolite-associated immune signatures of fibrosis severity in MASLD
items.summary: by Zhi-yun Liu, Jing Feng, Wen-qiao Lu, Lin Wang, Qian-yu Bi, Jie Gao, Chun-lei Liu, Te-jin Ba, Li Kong, Fei-hu Zhang Objective To identify microbiota–metabolite-associated immune features associated with fibrosis severity and evaluate their cross-cohort expression, discrimination and cellular context in human liver. Methods Discovery used 206 NAFLD cases from GSE135251, comparing F0–F2 with F3–F4. Human gutMGene host genes were intersected with ImmPort immune genes, followed by transcriptome-wide FDR filtering, LASSO and balanced Random Forest selection. Complete-pipeline five-fold cross-validation assessed internal performance. Fixed features and coefficients were evaluated in GSE130970, including age- and sex-adjusted sensitivity analyses. GSE244832 provided single-nucleus localization and descriptive CellChat context.
items.author: Zhi-yun Liu, Jing Feng, Wen-qiao Lu et al.

items.title: Intergenerational transmission of depression and anxiety among diverse immigrant populations in Sweden
items.summary: by Kenta Okuyama, Sara Larsson Lönn, Tsuyoshi Hamano, Ardavan M. Khoshnood, Jan Sundquist, Kristina Sundquist Background Little is known about the intergenerational transmission of depression and anxiety among children to immigrants. Our study aimed to investigate the association between parental depression/anxiety and offspring depression/anxiety among non-immigrants and second-generation immigrants, and whether the association differs by sex and immigrants’ regions of origin. Methods We used nationwide longitudinal registers that cover the entire population in Sweden. The study individuals were categorized as non-immigrants (n = 744,089) and second-generation immigrants (n = 210,868) from six regions of origin. Parental and offspring depression and anxiety were assessed by registered diagnosis from the National Patient Register, and the association was examined by Cox proportional hazard models, adjusted for potential confounders.
items.author: Kenta Okuyama, Sara Larsson Lönn, Tsuyoshi Hamano et al.

items.title: Temporal trends in the incidence of chronic kidney disease from 1992 to 2021: An age-period-cohort analysis using GBD 2021 data and projections until 2031
items.summary: by Yu Zheng, Muhong Wei, Daibing Lu, Yuxin Liu, Xue Chen, Jing Mi, Wenjia Peng, Yuyuan Zhang Background This study analyzed the temporal trends in the incidence of Chronic kidney disease (CKD) globally and across various regions over the past 30 years, as well as projected incidence for the next 10 years. These findings may help identify regions and age groups where intensified CKD surveillance, prevention, and health-system planning should be prioritized. Methods Data on the number of CKD cases and age-standardized incidence rates (ASIR) were obtained from the GBD 2021 dataset. The age, period, and cohort effects were assessed using the age-period-cohort (APC) model.
items.author: Yu Zheng, Muhong Wei, Daibing Lu et al.

items.title: State-triggered cooperative mandatory merging at temporary lane closures in mixed traffic flow
items.summary: by Jie Yu, Tao Chen, Qiang Wen, Mingyuan Bai Cooperation can create space at a temporary lane closure, but unnecessary intervention can increase traffic disturbance and fuel use. We develop ECO, a state-triggered strategy that links selective gap creation to mandatory merge execution. Initial target-lane density, remaining distance and controllable-neighbor availability govern activation. Longitudinal model predictive control shapes the gap, while predictive admission, lateral tracking and bounded safety filtering govern execution. Paired simulations assume that all vehicles, including those with nominal human-driving behavior, permit final safety intervention. Across 20 conditions with nonzero target-lane connected and automated vehicle penetration, ECO reduces fuel intensity by 0.80%–7.20% relative to the specified continuous-cooperation controller and completes all 500 main runs.
items.author: Jie Yu, Tao Chen, Qiang Wen et al.

items.title: Implementation of mental health screening tools among women refugees and asylum seekers in the United States: A systematic review
items.summary: by Pierre J. Amiel, Shalini Suresh, Abdulaziz Almuhanna, Pratik Chhetri, John Pateña, Joyce Gyamfi, Dorice Vieira, Chukwuemeka Iloegbu, Emmanuel Peprah Globally, displaced populations face significant mental health challenges, with women refugees and asylum seekers experiencing greater risks of anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder. Despite the widespread use of mental health screening tools such as the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), the Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7), and the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist (PCL-5), their implementation among refugee women remains underexplored. This systematic review examines the adoption, appropriateness, acceptability, and fidelity of use of mental health screening tools for adult women refugees and asylum seekers in the United States.
items.author: Pierre J. Amiel, Shalini Suresh, Abdulaziz Almuhanna et al.

items.title: Baicalein and Baicalein-loaded liposomes attenuate manganese-induced injury in the rat substantia nigra
items.summary: by Wesam Nofal, Ayat B. Al-Ghafari, Huda A. Al Doghaither, Ahmad Najem Alshammari, Manal S. Fawzy, Ekramy M. Elmorsy, Gehad E. Elshopakey, Wayne G. Carter Background/objectives Manganese (Mn) can accumulate in the brain, damage the basal ganglia and cause Parkinsonian phenotypes. Baicalein (BA), a natural flavonoid, shows therapeutic promise driven by its antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. This study aimed to evaluate whether BA and baicalein-loaded liposomes (BA-LPs) reduce Mn-induced injury to the substantia nigra. Methods Sixty male Wistar rats were allocated into six groups: control, Mn (50 mg/kg), BA (30 mg/kg), BA-LPs, and Mn combined with either BA or BA-LPs.
items.author: Wesam Nofal, Ayat B. Al-Ghafari, Huda A. Al Doghaither et al.

items.title: Dynamic regulation of the podocyte phosphatase PTPRO by stress and glucocorticoids
items.summary: by Nina Sopel, Carmen Popanda, Alexandra Ohs, Janina Müller-Deile Protein tyrosine phosphorylation is a critical regulator of podocyte function, controlling cell adhesion, signaling, and cytoskeletal architecture. The receptor-type protein tyrosine phosphatase PTPRO (GLEPP1) is highly expressed in podocytes, and its dysregulation contributes to podocytopathies. However, the mechanisms controlling PTPRO expression under stress remain incompletely understood. Here, we demonstrate that PTPRO is expressed in conditionally immortalized human podocytes and is dynamically regulated. Exposure to the pro-fibrotic cytokine TGF-β induced an upregulation of PTPRO, accompanied by a concomitant downregulation of microRNA-26b (miR-26b), which we identified as a post-transcriptional regulator of PTPRO. Furthermore, the podocyte stressor puromycin aminonucleoside markedly suppressed PTPRO expression, whereas glucocorticoids induced PTPRO, highlighting context-dependent regulation.
items.author: Nina Sopel, Carmen Popanda, Alexandra Ohs et al.

items.title: Functional performance and 12-month change in effusion-synovitis in knees at risk of osteoarthritis: A longitudinal analysis using the osteoarthritis initiative
items.summary: by Yang Wang, Hao Liu, Hang Zhang, Wenbo Zhao, Xin Miao, Qifeng Tao, Tiemei Wang, Jinxin Jiang, Xing Wang, Xianchun Yang, Xueyong Qiu, Lan Chen, Lili Chen, Ruyu Liao, Yang Yang, Di Liu, Shanhong Liu, Bin Yu, Shanshan Yang, Ting Wang, Shengfa Li Background Effusion-synovitis is a key marker of synovial inflammation and is linked to the progression of knee osteoarthritis (KOA). However, the determinants of short-term changes in synovial inflammation remain unclear. This study examined the associations of baseline demographic, clinical, functional, and cardiometabolic factors with 12-month changes in effusion-synovitis volume in knees at risk of osteoarthritis (OA). Methods We performed a longitudinal analysis using data from the POMA incident OA cohort of the Osteoarthritis Initiative.
items.author: Yang Wang, Hao Liu, Hang Zhang et al.

items.title: Neuromuscular performance, physiological recovery, and maturation-referenced reference values in youth athletes: A cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Souhail Bchini, Dhouha Moussaoui, Anissa Bouassida, Nouf H. Alkhamees, Nadhir Hammami, Fatma Hilal Yagin This cross-sectional study characterized neuromuscular performance and acute physiological responses across age, sex, and biological maturation in 140 youth athletes (74 boys, 66 girls; 10–16 years), and described maturation-stratified distributions of two field measures. Participants completed 30-m sprint, countermovement jump (CMJ), standing long jump (SLJ), and handgrip testing; post-sprint heart-rate recovery (HRrec-30s) and a testing-battery perceived-exertion index (PEI) served as co-primary physiological/perceptual outcomes; maturity offset (Mirwald method) classified Pre-, Circa-, and Post-PHV subgroups; allometric scaling was used to account for body size; and a Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction was applied across a pre-specified family of 58 pairwise comparisons and correlations (Tables 2–6).
items.author: Souhail Bchini, Dhouha Moussaoui, Anissa Bouassida et al.

items.title: Depressive symptoms among adult patients with systemic lupus erythematosus in the Jazan Region, Saudi Arabia: An analytical cross-sectional study
items.summary: by Aliyah Mansour Alhamoud, Siham Elamin Habeeballah Mental disorders, including depression, are common among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Depressive symptoms can significantly impair quality of life and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Studies investigating depressive symptoms and their associated factors in individuals with SLE have yielded inconsistent findings. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the prevalence of depressive symptoms among patients with SLE and to identify the associated factors in patients from the Jazan Region of Saudi Arabia. An analytical cross-sectional study of 112 patients with SLE in Jazan, Saudi Arabia was conducted in 2023. A convenience sampling technique was used to recruit all eligible adult patients with SLE who attended rheumatology clinics and day-care units at the referral hospitals in the region.
items.author: Aliyah Mansour Alhamoud, Siham Elamin Habeeballah

items.title: Reversal of dynamical backaction and cooling below the quantum backaction limit in Floquet-driven multimode optomechanical resonators
items.summary: Dynamical backaction describes how a driven cavity field responds with delay to mechanical motion, and can be used to cool that motion toward its quantum ground state or amplify it into self-oscillation. Control over this interaction underpins laser cooling, high-fidelity state preparation, quantum transduction, and phonon lasing. In conventional cavity optomechanics, both the sign and the magnitude of the optical damping are dictated by the laser detuning, and cooling is bounded by quantum backaction (QBA), the optomechanical analogue of the Doppler limit in cold atoms. We show, in theory and experiment, that dynamical backaction can be strongly enhanced in multimode optomechanical resonators driven by time-varying (Floquet) optical fields.
items.author: Menno H. Jansen, Roel Burgwal, Ewold Verhagen

items.title: Subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic waves for enhancing Brillouin gain in a planar waveguide structure
items.summary: We propose a planar waveguide structure consisting of two layers separated by a gap that provides subwavelength confinement of optical and acoustic modes and a large overlap integral between them. This, in turn, leads to an increase in Brillouin gain. Using the structure of two Si$_3$N$_4$ layers with a subwavelength gap from SiO$_2$ as an example, we demonstrate that a hybridized transverse-magnetic (TM) optical mode exhibits strong field confinement in the SiO$_2$ gap. Simultaneously, a high-frequency acoustic mode can be confined in the same gap, providing a high spatial overlap between the optical and acoustic fields. This provides a high opto-acoustic interaction with a Brillouin gain up to $5$ W$^{-1}$m$^{-1}$.
items.author: A. R. Mukhamedyanov, E. A. Tereshchenkov, E. S. Andrianov et al.
