items.title: Laser Processing for Energy Applications
items.summary: Laser processing has emerged as a transformative technology in the energy sector, enabling precise, efficient, and scalable solutions for energy generation, storage, and sustainability. This chapter explores the diverse applications of laser technology in energy applications. It begins with an overview of laser-driven inertial confinement fusion for energy production, highlighting key experimental facilities and crucial laser parameters. The role of lasers in solar energy harvesting is examined, including photovoltaic cell optimization, concentrated solar power, and laser-assisted recycling of solar modules. The chapter further reviews recent developments into laser-based techniques for enhancing electrochemical performance through surface texturing at various scales. Advancements in lithium-ion battery technology are also discussed, focusing on next-generation materials, battery manufacturing processes, and the impact of laser techniques on performance, safety, and scalability.
items.author: Marcos Soldera, Robert Baumann, Bogdan Voisiat et al.

items.title: How Elasticity and Chiral Damping Shape Domain-Wall Creep
items.summary: Asymmetric domain-wall expansion in the creep regime provides an experimentally accessible probe of the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (iDMI) and, in principle, chiral damping. However, severe discrepancies with complementary measurement techniques and the lack of a model describing the full experimental phenomenology of the creep of chiral domain walls, limits the application of these measurements. Here, using a symmetry decomposition of the velocity curve, we derive an analytical model describing the coupled influence of domain-wall stiffness and chiral damping in the creep regime. Their interplay generates the antisymmetric distortion that shifts the velocity minimum away from the DMI field. Applied to Co-based magnetic multilayers, the model yields iDMI values consistent with BLS and flow-regime benchmarks and identifies the reasons for the longstanding discrepancy.
items.author: Adriano Di Pietro, Alessandro Magni, Stefania Pizzini et al.

items.title: ThermoSight: From Appearance to Internal Thermofluid Fields via Physics-Guided Neural Reconstruction
items.summary: Most neural reconstruction methods focus on reproducing scene appearance, yet inferring physical states from visual observations is essential for machine understanding of the physical world. Reconstructing the internal temperature and soot fields of radiating thermofluids such as flames is challenging yet essential for improving energy efficiency and assessing heat exposure and fire spread. In flames, temperature and soot concentration jointly govern visible emission, and soot self-absorption alters the light that reaches each camera. With limited views, changes in the two fields can offset one another in the recorded RGB images, making temperature and soot difficult to disentangle. ThermoSight, a physics-guided neural framework for scientific imaging, jointly reconstructs continuous three-dimensional temperature and soot volume fraction fields from limited calibrated flame images without field-level ground truth during optimization.
items.author: Yuhao Fang, Chenglin Lu, Hefei Ling et al.

items.title: STA: A Split Temporal Adversary Method for Evaluating Robustness of Multimodal RL-based Driving Policies
items.summary: Multimodal reinforcement learning (MRL) offers a promising paradigm for autonomous driving by jointly leveraging complementary sensor observations to learn effective decision-making policies. However, its effectiveness critically depends on temporal alignment across modalities, making temporal inconsistency a fundamental vulnerability. Even subtle misalignment or latency can corrupt fused representations and ultimately lead to decision failures. Existing studies have explored adversarial attacks to induce cross-modal temporal inconsistencies, thereby enabling systematic evaluation of the temporal robustness of MRL policies. However, existing methods remain limited in generality, realism, and adaptivity. To address these limitations, we propose the Split Temporal Adversary (STA), which formulates multimodal temporal attacks as a unified decision process that jointly optimizes attack timing and modality selection under realistic policy-aware and budget-constrained settings.
items.author: Shenghao Xiong, Xiaolin Chang

items.title: Cavity Control of Emission Dynamics from Spin Defects in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
items.summary: Optically addressable negatively charged boron vacancy ($\mathrm{V_B^-}$) defects in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are promising for quantum sensing at room temperature. The two-dimensional structure of hBN allows direct access to the local environment, enabling proximal sensing of target materials. However, its broadband emission and low quantum yield hinder efficient light-matter interaction, and the coupling of $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ optical dipoles to confined cavity fields remains poorly understood. In this study, we integrate $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ defects with a tunable plano-concave microcavity, achieving three-dimensional optical confinement. This approach yields photoluminescence (PL) enhancement and cavity-modified optical decay dynamics, providing insights into the orientation of the $\mathrm{V_B^-}$ defect dipole.
items.author: Anuj Kumar Singh, Atanu Patra, Paul Konrad et al.

items.title: Robotic Reward Models in the Foundation-Model Era
items.summary: Robotic reward models (RRMs) use foundation models to replace per-task reward engineering with reusable, task-conditioned evaluation. Yet under one name, their outputs answer different questions, from whether a task succeeded to which execution is better. This survey organizes 114 methods into five semantic families by the question their native outputs answer: Outcome, Absolute Progress, Relative, Temporal Value, and Hybrid. Within this taxonomy, we review how model design determines what an evaluator can judge, how raw experience becomes supervision, and how existing evaluation practice tests the result. The review exposes a gap: agreement with demonstration order and downstream policy gains do not show whether a reward tracks task fulfillment.
items.author: Guoqiang Liang, Yiqi Lin, Shangchen Zhou et al.

items.title: High-quality intrinsic circular dichroism in silicon-based bound states in the continuum metasurfaces via strong coupling
items.summary: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) can significantly enhance spin-selective light-matter interactions. However, current BIC metasurfaces generally rely on single or multiple chiral BIC modes to enhance circular dichroism (CD), limiting their application in functional integrated devices. This paper proposes a method that utilizes the strong coupling effect in BIC metasurfaces to achieve intrinsic CD with both a high quality factor (Q-factor) and high efficiency. The metasurface is designed as a silicon-based cross-shaped nanohole array, which can simultaneously support a TM-like BIC mode and a TE-like guided-mode resonance (GMR) mode. By introducing under-etching to break the out-of-plane symmetry and tuning the in-plane asymmetry parameter, strong coupling between the quasi-BIC (QBIC) mode and the GMR mode can be induced, thereby achieving near-perfect intrinsic CD with a high Q-factor.
items.author: Leyi Zhu, Tian Sang, Guanhua Yang et al.

items.title: GainCtrl: Predicting Remaining Gains for Efficient LLM Agent Execution
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to power agents that interact with tools and environments to solve complex tasks. Repeated attempts improve the quality of tool-using agents, but continued execution incurs additional costs even when it is unlikely to improve the best result ultimately returned. This raises the question of when to stop an attempt to reduce execution cost while preserving task-level Best-of-N quality. To address this question, we introduce GainCtrl, a gain-based execution controller for LLMs. In GainCtrl, a lightweight CPU predictor uses interaction histories to estimate expected positive gains over retained scores, which are then used to guide stopping decisions with calibrated thresholds to limit the loss in mean Best-of-N task quality.
items.author: Kangwen Zhao, Jianfeng Cai, Ruopei Sun et al.

items.title: Material Tailored Multispectral Magnetization via the Inverse Faraday Effect in Tunable Coaxial Nanoantenna
items.summary: All-optical control of magnetization via the Inverse Faraday Effect presents a transformative pathway for ultrafast high-density data storage and nanoscale spintronics. However, unlocking its full potential requires moving beyond traditional gold-centric, narrowband constraints. In this study, we present a comprehensive theoretical framework evaluating IFE-driven static magnetic field generation across a diverse library of plasmonic materials, including gold, silver, copper, aluminum, and titanium nitride. Using a dimensionally tunable coaxial nanoantenna, we map the optomagnetic response across the deep-ultraviolet to near-infrared spectrum. Our findings reveal highly distinct, material-dependent behaviors: aluminum uniquely sustains robust magnetization in the deep-UV, whereas silver, copper, and gold exhibit superior efficiency at longer wavelengths.
items.author: Roméo Zapata, Bleuenn Belz, Xingyu Yang et al.

items.title: MemEmo: Evaluating Emotion in Memory Systems
items.summary: Memory systems address the challenge of context loss in Large Language Models during prolonged interactions. However, as an essential tool for warm companionship and personalized services, the effectiveness of memory systems in processing affective information remains underexamined. To bridge this gap, we propose an emotion-enhanced memory evaluation benchmark to assess the performance of mainstream and state-of-the-art memory systems in integrating and harnessing emotional information. First, we design a benchmark called \textbf{MemEmo} to assess the affective reasoning and tracking capabilities of memory systems across four dimensions: emotional information extraction, emotional memory updating, emotional memory question-answering, and emotional conflict detection. Second, we construct the \textbf{H}uman-\textbf{L}ike \textbf{M}emory \textbf{E}motion (\textbf{HLME}) dataset to provide an empirical foundation for scrutinizing memory systems.
items.author: Peng Liu, Zhen Tao, Jihao Zhao et al.

items.title: Routing Beyond Task Categories: A Cost-Aware LAB-Bench Study
items.summary: We tested whether features of biology questions or of a model's first answer can improve accuracy within an inference budget. In a LAB-Bench pilot, we compared a category router with one that adds six structural features. Neither reached the primary 80% accuracy target on development. At the 50% and 60% secondary targets, both chose Haiku for all 120 held-out questions and scored 71/120. We then froze a new comparison before collecting responses on 144 additional questions. Semantic routing scored 86/144. A policy that could defer after reading Haiku's answer scored 87/144. Both stayed within the inference budget of USD 0.678 per 1,000 queries.
items.author: Ahmed Tariq, Leo Guinan

items.title: Selective Sensor Acquisition for Multimodal Place Recognition
items.summary: Multimodal Place Recognition (PR) can improve robustness, but most systems rigidly read and process every sensor for every query, even when the primary sensor is sufficient, with implications for energy consumption, second sensor update rate, and domain-specific considerations such as passive stealth. We introduce selective, controllable sensor acquisition, where a user specifies a desired second sensor usage rate and the system acquires the additional sensor only when the primary sensor's estimated performance is sufficiently poor. An online threshold adjustment achieves the requested usage rate by adapting to recent primary sensor performance, directing additional sensing towards queries where fusion is most likely to help without calibration specific to sensor modality, PR method, or environment.
items.author: Margaux Edwards, Tobias Fischer, Michael Milford

items.title: PEETS: Preference-aware Embeddings with Explicit Tree Structure for Auxiliary Product Bundling
items.summary: Auxiliary products such as flight protection and flexible-change services are recommended alongside primary travel purchases. This setting creates a granularity ambiguity: SKUs within one product type share semantics but differ in price and coverage, while rejecting one offer does not imply disinterest in the entire type. We present \textbf{PEETS} (\textbf{P}reference-aware \textbf{E}mbeddings with \textbf{E}xplicit \textbf{T}ree \textbf{S}tructure), a training-time framework for auxiliary product bundling. PEETS regularizes an existing click--conversion predictor through two conditional comparisons. Hierarchical Contrastive Loss uses the pair's common ancestor as a reference; Negative Contrastive Loss conditions structural sampling and comparison shifts on logged rejection events. Both act on shared SKU representations during training.
items.author: Maolei Huang, Jing Tian, Dexuan Duan et al.

items.title: AVD: A Multi-Sensor Teleoperated Wheelchair Platform with Safety-Aware Control
items.summary: Electric wheelchairs predominantly rely on manual joystick interfaces, which present critical barriers to independent mobility for individuals with severe motor and visual impairments. This paper presents AVD (Autonomous Vehicle Drive), a dependable teleoperation architecture for assistive mobility that unifies perception, communication, embedded control, and remote supervision in a single low-cost platform built entirely from commercially available hardware. The central engineering contribution is a safety-oriented design framework: control authority follows a static hierarchy, a manual emergency stop and the occupant's joystick pre-empt remote commands, and the on-board sensing layer has stop-only authority. The compute design partitions primary and safety functions and specifies a heartbeat-driven safe-state transition for the fault cases considered.
items.author: Namai Chandra, Madhur Thareja, Boby George

items.title: ACiT: Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers
items.summary: Visuomotor policies condition action prediction on visual and proprioceptive observations. While historical proprioceptive sequences carry rich dynamic priors, current methods treat them as equal to high-dimensional vision, causing the proprioceptive signal to be overwhelmed. To identify what is lost in equal-conditioning fusion, we analyze proprioceptive data and find that strong inter-joint coupling is the key action-determining structure. This finding aligns with the neural sensorimotor loop, in which proprioception first forms a body-centered prior and vision is later calibrated via parietal remapping. Inspired by this, we propose ACiT, Proprioceptive-Prior Action Chunking with Inverted Transformers, which reinforces historical joint-coupling as the primary condition with vision as a later calibration.
items.author: Haixiang Wu, Zhihao Guan, Yang Yang

items.title: TaF-Foundation: Wrench-Grounded Cross-Sensor Tactile Representations
items.summary: Tactile sensing is essential for contact-rich manipulation, yet heterogeneous sensing mechanisms and observation formats hinder cross-hardware transfer. Since physical contact is governed by Newtonian mechanics, we ground tactile representations in six-dimensional wrenches, establishing a common physical reference across sensing mechanisms. Specifically, we pair tactile observations from all sensors with wrench measurements, enabling shared physical supervision without requiring direct tactile-to-tactile pairing between sensors. To support learning at scale, we develop a dedicated acquisition platform and collect over 100 million paired tactile observations and wrench measurements from 24 sensors spanning four families of sensing principles. Building on this dataset, our framework combines sensor-specific input adaptation with a shared tactile encoder.
items.author: Jiaming Jiang, Yuzhe Huang, Baokun Yang et al.

items.title: AgentFaultBench: State-Verified Evaluation of Tool-Fault Recovery
items.summary: Does recovery advice help an agent finish a task after a tool fails? AgentFaultBench evaluates LangGraph and CrewAI agents performing specified tasks in an isolated GitLab installation. We inject tool errors and check both the resulting files and issues and the required reads, verification and final response. The prompt supplies the expected issue and report text, so the task tests execution rather than content generation. In the primary comparison of 1,944 planned runs, advice changes success by -8.33, 0.00 and +1.06 percentage points relative to a neutral reminder; missing outcomes leave the latter two comparisons inconclusive. Later experiments test a revised recovery policy.
items.author: Sachin Gupta

items.title: SG-ODOM: Event-Driven Proprioceptive State Estimation with Stability-Gated Contact Updates for Legged Robots
items.summary: Reliable proprioceptive state estimation for legged robots fuses inertial sensing with kinematic sensing from leg encoders. The latter assumes a foot is stationary during the stance phase; however, physical foot touchdown does not necessarily provide a stationary reference for odometry, particularly during impact and load transfer. Repeatedly applying kinematic corrections throughout the same contact phase can introduce redundant or unreliable information. We present SG-ODOM, a proprioceptive odometry framework that uses stability-gated contact selection to schedule kinematic updates. Following physical touchdown, a stability gate accepts the contact for state estimation only after the foot reaches a sufficiently stable support condition. The resulting validated touchdown event triggers an estimator correction, while additional timeout updates bound the maximum duration of uninterrupted IMU propagation.
items.author: Francesco Iotti, Chiyun Noh, Franco Angelini et al.

items.title: Design of the Secure Smart Scooter with Automatic Lane Detection
items.summary: The authors present a prototype of an electric scooter that uses computer vision to determine driving lanes and automatically modify vehicle configuration. Scooters steer on sidewalks, bike paths, or car lanes. The government imposes speed limits on the lanes in which electric scooters drive. Featuring computer vision, electric scooters can determine driving lanes and automatically modify vehicle configuration. However, such systems' safety is still a concern, and research into such vehicle systems' safety and security aspects is proceeding. First, we will present our vehicular setup. Then, we will present our implemented scooter with safety constraints. Finally, we present our security prototype for such an electric scooter.
items.author: Hamid Reza Ghaeini, Nils Ole Tippenhauer

items.title: A First Look at System One Decision Models for Malware Detection
items.summary: Malware detection needs scores calibrated at a fixed false positive rate (FPR) and decisions an analyst can read: feature-based detectors give the first, large language models (LLMs) on decompiled code the second, through generated text of uncalibrated confidence. System One decision models answer a typed question about a text with a probability over its declared answers in one forward pass. We present the first evaluation of these models for Windows Portable Executable malware detection, analyze how they decide, and propose S1Mal, an ensemble on the typed answers and the embedding of CLM-8B. In an isolated virtual machine, Ghidra and capa decompose each binary, and the host renders the records into a canonical textual state, a digest of headers, imports, MITRE ATT&CK capabilities and strings, optionally with decompiled functions, without class shortcuts.
items.author: Pier Mattia Basciano, Giovanni Farina, Salvatore Monteleone

items.title: Unconventional Magneto-Optical Kerr Effect beyond Magnetization Scaling Driven by Pulse-Field-Induced Metamagnetism in Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
items.summary: First-order phase transitions often proceed through metastable states and complicated phase coexistence, yet such nonequilibrium processes are obscured in bulk measurements. The magneto-optical Kerr effect (MOKE) probes the local off-diagonal optical response, offering access to local magnetic dynamics beyond bulk measurements. Here, we investigate the magnetic-field-induced antiferromagnetic (AFM)-ferrimagnetic (FRM) transition in the polar insulator Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ using pulsed-field MOKE measurements extended for the first time up to 60 T and down to 1.4 K. The MOKE response exhibits unexpected and huge nonmonotonic transient behavior across the metamagnetic phase transition. The MOKE behavior does not show any scaling with the bulk magnetization, pointing to an MOKE analogue of the unconventional anomalous Hall effect.
items.author: Soichiro Yamane, Sota Nakamura, Shuya Suzuki et al.

items.title: IndustrialKnowEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-Level Industrial Knowledge in LLMs
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly explored for industrial tasks, yet few benchmarks evaluate their mastery of industrial knowledge across different types of cognitive demand. We introduce IndustrialKnowEval (IndKnow), a benchmark for industrial knowledge and engineering question answering. It contains 43,282 samples covering 21 task types across seven industrial sectors, including aerospace, electric power, and metallurgy, organized into four levels of cognitive demand: memory, comprehension, reasoning, and engineering application. Enterprise-based domain specialists and experienced researchers participate in all stages of dataset construction and quality control. We conduct a series of experiments on 18 representative LLMs, with domain experts deeply involved in the evaluation.
items.author: Haiteng Wang, Haoze Li, Jingwei Guo et al.

items.title: Breaking the Fixed-Substrate Limitation of Deep Learning Ellipsometry with Pseudo-Substrate Spectra
items.summary: A machine learning method, deep learning ellipsometry (DLE), enables direct and rapid estimation of the optical constants and structures of thin films from spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) spectra. However, conventional neural-network-based DLE models are restricted to the specific substrate used during training, and applying them to a different substrate requires ~100 h of retraining. Here, we propose a framework that overcomes this fixed-substrate limitation by introducing a two-input feature-wise linear modulation DLE (FiLM-DLE). In this model, the SE spectra of a thin-film structure are input together with those of the substrate measured before film deposition, which we term the pseudo-substrate spectra.
items.author: Yuki Ikarashi, Naoki Kurokawa, James N. Hilfiker et al.

items.title: SpeCal: Spectral Calibration for Unsupervised RLVR
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has substantially improved the reasoning abilities of large language models, but its dependence on ground-truth answers or external verifiers limits its ability to exploit abundant unlabeled reasoning data. Unsupervised RLVR alleviates this bottleneck by deriving scalar rewards from the model's own rollouts. However, the reliability of such self-generated supervision varies substantially across rollout groups and individual responses, while existing methods construct or refine their rewards mainly from decoded outcomes and reward statistics. These endpoint signals reveal what answers the model produces, but provide limited information about whether the underlying rollout representations form a reliable structure for learning.
items.author: Kai Tang, Xing Zheng, Haobo Wang et al.

items.title: Spatiotemporal beam stirring of femtosecond pulses in a multicore fiber driven by spectral decorrelation
items.summary: Multicore fibers (MCFs) are promising for ultrafast laser systems, but random coupling between their cores makes the output power distribution unstable. Previously, we observed spatiotemporal beam stirring of narrowband sub-nanosecond pulses in a 7-core fiber, where Kerr nonlinearity equalizes the core powers. Here, we study the propagation of 150-fs pulses at 1052 nm in the same fiber. As the fiber length increases up to 20 m, the output core powers become equalized with a spread $<7\%$, and the far-field speckle pattern transforms into a bell-shaped total beam. In contrast to the sub-nanosecond case, the effect does not depend on the input peak power (0.2--15 kW) and originates from the spectral decorrelation of the random coupling between the cores, whereas a narrowband CW source yields an unstable output with a $\sim 40\%$ spread.
items.author: Nikita V. Bochkarev, Alena Y. Kolesnikova, Mikhail D. Gervaziev et al.

items.title: Lock-in phase evidence for the electro-optic effect of interfacial water on ITO electrodes
items.summary: Attribution to the Pockels effect of interfacial water, reported at interfaces between transparent electrodes and aqueous solutions, has relied on using an optical model to estimate the contribution of changes in the electrode's own carrier density to the electromodulation spectrum and subtracting this contribution. In this study, we test this attribution using the phase, without subtracting the electrode contribution with an optical model. Because the carrier response of the electrode follows charge modulation at several hundred hertz without delay, it has a common phase at all wavelengths apart from sign reversals of the response. However, the measured transmission modulation spectra at the interface between indium tin oxide (ITO) and 0.1 mol L$^{-1}$ aqueous NaCl show a phase peak near 420 nm, where the ITO response becomes small.
items.author: Soichiro Ashikaga, Kazuaki Nakata, Takayoshi Kobayashi et al.

items.title: Magnitude 5 Earthquake Strikes Near Sarangani, Philippines
items.summary: A magnitude 5.0 earthquake struck 68 kilometers south of Sarangani, Philippines, at a depth of about 10 kilometers on November 16, 2026. Data remains subject to agency review.

items.ai_summary: A magnitude 5.0 earthquake struck 68 kilometers south of Sarangani, Philippines, at a depth of about 10 kilometers on November 16, 2026. Data remains subject to agency review.

items.title: Telecom-band optical parametric oscillation in a passive silicon microring resonator at cryogenic temperatures
items.summary: At telecommunications wavelengths, free carriers generated by two-photon absorption limit optical parametric oscillation (OPO) in silicon. Here, we demonstrate telecom-band OPO in a passive silicon microring resonator without electrical carrier sweep-out, driven by a single continuous-wave (CW) pump at 4.5 K. We achieve an on-chip OPO onset power of 2.25 mW and a total conversion efficiency of 1.9% into all parametric sidebands at a pump power of 4.8 mW. Despite CW pumping, the parametric output emerges as a train of pulses synchronized with microsecond-scale self-pulsing. At higher pump powers, OPO emission is absent during intervals of sustained sub-GHz oscillations in the pump transmission, narrowing the temporal window for OPO.
items.author: Shoichiro Yasui, Xuejun Xu, Hidetaka Nishi et al.

items.title: Webb Telescope Captures Star Formation and Jets in NGC 7129
items.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has captured a detailed infrared image of the star-forming region NGC 7129 to help researchers understand how stars develop. Gravity initially pulls together large amounts of gas to form stars, but the process becomes complex as growing stars emit powerful winds and jets, and some eventually explode. Cool stellar atmospheres can also generate opaque dust that blocks visible light when dispersed. In the captured image, younger and more mature stars appear across different colored gas regions, highlighting the physical processes at work during early stellar development.

items.ai_title: Webb Telescope Captures Star Formation and Jets in NGC 7129
items.ai_summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has captured a detailed infrared image of the star-forming region NGC 7129 to help researchers understand how stars develop. Gravity initially pulls together large amounts of gas to form stars, but the process becomes complex as growing stars emit powerful winds and jets, and some eventually explode. Cool stellar atmospheres can also generate opaque dust that blocks visible light when dispersed. In the captured image, younger and more mature stars appear across different colored gas regions, highlighting the physical processes at work during early stellar development.

items.title: Indonesian Tropical Glaciers Shrink to Near Disappearance
items.summary: Glaciers on Puncak Jaya in Indonesia have shrunk drastically since 1988, dwindling to about two percent of their former area by late 2025. Comparisons between historical and recent satellite imagery reveal that the ice has thinned significantly, broken apart, and lost its ability to flow like a glacier. Climate conditions and intense El Niño events, which bring warm air and rain instead of protective snow, have severely accelerated the melting process. Scientists warn that these high-altitude tropical ice remnants could disappear completely around 2030 or even sooner.

items.title: E2F4 gene therapy reverses established synaptic and cognitive deficits and remodels learning-associated signaling in Alzheimer's disease mice
items.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes progressive synaptic dysfunction, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline, yet strategies capable of reversing established deficits remain limited. Here, we show that neuronal expression of a p38MAPK phosphorylation-resistant human E2F4 variant (hE2F4DN), delivered by adeno-associated virus, restores hippocampal long-term potentiation and memory in homozygous 5xFAD mice after functional impairment is established. Treatment also reduces amyloid-{beta} and phospho-tau pathology and prevents hippocampal neuronal loss. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses reveal remodeling of metabolic, redox, neuroimmune, synaptic-vesicle, and GSK3{beta}-associated signaling pathways. Following contextual fear conditioning, hE2F4DN-treated mice exhibit broader learning-associated synaptic proteomic signatures and distinct phosphoregulatory responses involving synaptic machinery.
items.author: Sanchez-Puelles, C., Hernandez-Vivanco, A., Grieco, A. et al.

items.title: Magnetic nanoparticle enrichment reveals conserved nitric oxide burst responses in Arabidopsis and wheat
items.summary: Rapid nitric oxide bursts are a conserved response to environmental stimuli, but their effects on cellular S-nitrosylation remain poorly understood. We developed a fluorinated magnetic nanoparticle method for rapid, efficient profiling of S-nitrosylation. Using Arabidopsis and wheat, we treated plant tissues with S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO) to simulate a rapid nitric oxide surge. The method was then employed to capture S-nitrosylation dynamics within 24 h after treatment. Our analysis revealed sequence-dependent preferences for cysteines near basic or hydrophobic residues. Proteins showing rapid S-nitrosylation increases were predominantly associated with oxidative stress responses and energy metabolism, consistent with our metabolomic data. Functional studies using wheat TaGR1 mutants identified glutathione reductase 1 as a key regulated target.
items.author: Ji, R., Yang, N., Yu, L. et al.

items.title: N-Hydroxypipecolic Acid Triggers Systemic Acquired Resistance Against Leaf Rust (Puccinia triticina) in Wheat
items.summary: Systemic acquired resistance (SAR) represents a conserved immune strategy enabling plants to mount long-lasting, whole-plant protection following localized pathogen challenge. In Arabidopsis thaliana, SAR is orchestrated by the mobile immune regulator N-hydroxypipecolic acid (NHP); however, the extent to which NHP defines systemic immune states in polyploid crops remains unclear. Here, we establish NHP as an inducer of systemic immunity in hexaploid wheat (Triticum aestivum) during infection by the obligate biotrophic fungus Puccinia triticina. Local NHP application conferred robust disease suppression in distal leaves and elicited a temporally structured oxidative response characterized by a distal, biphasic reactive oxygen species (ROS) wave linking local and systemic tissues.
items.author: Sun, S., Formby, S., Craven, C. et al.

items.title: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
items.summary: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank. Because the published benchmark did not identify its test sets, we reran GBLUP, RKHS and elastic-net models on the same splits as TabPFN-3.5.
items.author: Flagel, L.

items.title: Endogenous Osteoblast-Osteocyte-Osteoclast Signaling Enables Bone Remodeling, Drug Response, and Cancer Invasion in a Nanoscale Calcified Bone-on-a-Chip
items.summary: Bone homeostasis depends on spatially orchestrated interactions among osteoclasts, osteoblasts, and osteocytes within a unique microenvironment characterized by an extracellular matrix that is mineralized on the nanoscale. Reconstructing these interactions to enable autonomous cell differentiation and tissue remodeling remains a significant challenge in faithfully modeling bone physiology and disease in-vitro. Here, we present an engineered bone-on-a-chip platform that recapitulates the spatial organization of bone-resident cells, the differentiation of immune cells into osteoclasts, and calcified tissue resorption. We demonstrate that nanoscale mineralization of cell-laden collagen hydrogels is associated with ossification- and matrix-associated transcriptional changes and an osteocyte-like phenotype in osteoblast-lineage cells, while establishing a multicellular microenvironment associated with pro-osteoclastogenic RANKL/OPG signaling and supporting osteoclastogenesis and remodeling without the need for exogenous growth factors.
items.author: Sousa, M. G. C., Athirasala, A., Hosseini, M. et al.

items.title: Engineering the Lr67-associated G144R substitution by prime editing enhances leaf rust resistance in wheat
items.summary: Wheat rust diseases threaten global wheat production, highlighting the need for durable sources of resistance. The Lr67-associated G144R substitution in the sugar transport protein gene TaSTP13-D1 confers broad-spectrum resistance to multiple fungal pathogens. Here, we used an enhanced prime-editing system (ePPEplus) to introduce this resistance-associated substitution into the three TaSTP13 homoeologs in hexaploid wheat. Using the wheat-compatible JWPE1 vector, we achieved editing frequencies of 84 to 92% across the A, B, and D genomes in regenerated T0 plants. Homozygous edits were recovered in all three homoeologs, including one line carrying homozygous edits across all three genomes. Disease assays showed that edited lines had reduced leaf rust severity and fungal biomass compared with susceptible controls.
items.author: Waites, J., Venado, R. E., Syombua, E. D. et al.

items.title: Primate Saccade Rhythmicity
items.summary: Rhythmic sampling is a hallmark of many sensory systems across diverse organisms. In primate vision, rapid foveating eye movements repetitively sample the visual environment at a rate of approximately 4 Hz. Yet, the observed inter-saccadic interval distributions might equally well be produced by a non-rhythmic stochastic process as by a - putatively variable- rhythmic generator. This raises the fundamental question whether primate visual sampling differs from the numerous examples of rhythmic sampling strategies exhibited across sensory modalities and species. Here, using experiments in humans, macaques, and a marmoset, as well as statistical approaches adopted from studies of temporal structure in neuronal spiking patterns, we show that primate saccade generation is unambiguously rooted in a rhythmic source.
items.author: Näher, T., Zhang, Y., Spadacenta, S. et al.

items.title: EPHB2 promotes long-range axon extension and its variants cause callosal dysgenesis
items.summary: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres, essential for integrating neural activity across large-scale brain networks. Accordingly, abnormal CC development is associated with diverse neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Callosal projection neurons (CPNs) of the cortex form the CC by extending long-range axons to the contralateral hemisphere; however, the mechanisms that sustain axon elongation over such remarkable distances remain poorly understood. Here we show that variants in the human gene EPHB2, which encodes a tyrosine kinase receptor regulating nervous system development and implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, cause CC dysgenesis. We characterise variant- specific effects on EPHB2 signalling and demonstrate that variants identified in individuals with distinct CC morphologies differentially alter CPN axon outgrowth and integration in vivo.
items.author: Park, S. S., Nagy, G. N., Perez Ferrer, I. et al.

items.title: Do altered neural responses during self-reflection converge across psychiatric disorders? A systematic review and meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies
items.summary: Altered neural responses during self-reflection have been reported across psychiatric disorders, but it is unknown whether there exist common brain regions across studies. To fill the gap, we conducted a systematic review and coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis of task-based neuroimaging studies. Through systematic literature search and article screening, we identified 36 studies across 8 diagnostic categories, of which 25 studies were eligible for the ALE meta-analysis. Qualitatively, these studies revealed altered neural response among psychiatric disorders in brain regions include cortical midline and lateral association regions. ALE analyses were conducted separately for self-versus other and self-versus control contrasts, the former identified convergence in the right anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and the latter found converged activation in the left middle frontal gyrus (MFG).
items.author: Zhu, S., Yan, W.-J., Chuan-Peng, H.

items.title: Mathematical model for visual cortical development based on molecular mechanisms underlying the generation and elimination of dendritic spines
items.summary: In the developing brain, neural circuits are elaborated by the activity-dependent rewiring of synaptic connections. The current view of synaptic rewiring in early development is that filopodia spontaneously generated along dendrites transform into spines by establishing contacts with neighboring axonal boutons to form synapses whereas spines of inappropriate synapses are eliminated in an activity-dependent manner. In this theoretical study, we mainly focus on the processes of spine generation, maturation, and elimination to build a mathematical model of synaptic rewiring, incorporating experimental findings on actin polymerization and depolymerization under the activation of Rho-GTPases mediated by the binding of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) to neurotrophin receptors such as tropomyosin kinase receptor B (TrkB) and the low-affinity-nerve growth factor receptor (p75NTR).
items.author: Tanaka, S., Miyashita, M.

items.title: GradeBins: quality control of bins from synthetic and real metagenomes
items.summary: Genomes reconstructed from metagenomes support studies of microbial diversity and function, but their interpretation depends on how much DNA is recovered and whether foreign sequence is included. Quality can be measured in benchmarks, where contig origins are known, but must be estimated in routine analyses. Here we present GradeBins, which assesses individual bins (contigs assigned to one candidate genome) and summarizes the complete bin set from an assembly. For 6,374 simulated bins, its measurements agreed with AMBER and independent calculations within rounding. In control bins built from 20 kb fragments of reference genomes, GradeBins had lower observed completeness error than CheckM1 and CheckM2 and the highest observed F1 (the harmonic mean of precision and recall) for bin selection.
items.author: Bushnell, B., Bowers, R. M., Villada, J. C.

items.title: Unravelling the hidden diversity of the monkfish Lophius gastrophysus using integrative taxonomy
items.summary: The monkfish Lophius gastrophysus is a commercially exploited demersal species distributed along the continental shelf and slope of the western Atlantic Ocean. Like other anglerfish species, L. gastrophysus has a pelagic larval stage that can facilitate dispersal by oceanic currents (Farina et al., 2008). It is considered the most widely distributed species in the genus, spanning more than 10,000 km of the western Atlantic Coast, from North Carolina to Argentina. Previous morphological analyses based on a limited set of traits suggested that L. gastrophysus may comprise two distinct species. We tested this hypothesis by combining molecular and morphometric data. Sequence data were obtained from 38 L.
items.author: D'Elia, A. K. P., Soares, L. M. M., Henning, F. et al.

items.title: Centromere divergence and allopolyploidy reshape carnivorous sundew genomes
items.summary: Centromeres are essential for chromosome function, yet how contrasting centromere architectures shape polyploid genome evolution and plant diversification remains unresolved. In monocentric chromosomes, centromeric activity is restricted to one chromosomal region; in holocentric chromosomes, it is distributed along the chromosome length. Hybridization followed by genome doubling can place chromosome sets with different centromeres, repeat complements, and rearrangement histories in the same nucleus. We examined whether such genomic mergers are associated with later chromosome restructuring in carnivorous Caryophyllales, focusing on chromosome-scale assemblies of putatively holocentric Drosera regia and monocentric D. capensis. The two sundews retain broad syntenic continuity and related polyploid ancestry, but their present genomes differ sharply.
items.author: Avila Robledillo, L., Fukushima, K., Salojarvi, J. et al.

items.title: CLASSIFICATION OF PROKARYOTIC DNA METHYLTRANSFERASES BY CATALYTIC DOMAIN TOPOLOGY
items.summary: Prokaryotic DNA methyltransferases (MTases) are essential enzymes that play a crucial role in restriction-modification systems, preventing the degradation of self DNA by restriction enzymes. In addition, they contribute to the regulation of gene expression, DNA repair, DNA replication, and other processes. Here, we propose a novel classification of prokaryotic MTases based on the 3D topology of the catalytic domain, which addresses the limitations of the previous scheme developed by Malone and Bujnicki. The latter, which grouped MTases into categories such as , {beta}, {gamma}, etc., has been in use for over 20 years. We identified seven structural classes (A-G) of MTases by analyzing 38 experimentally determined 3D structures and several AlphaFold-predicted models, and validated the classification against all reviewed DNA MTases from Swiss-Prot.
items.author: Samokhina, M.

items.title: Restriction Enzyme activity under Force determined with autonomous DNA Origami Force Clamps via Gel Electrophoresis
items.summary: Investigating force-depending behaviour in biological systems is a challenging task, with most techniques requiring complex experimental equipment while also often being limited in scalability. We designed a facile force spectroscopy technique using DNA origami-based force clamps that apply forces up to ~40 pN. We validated the approach by using type II endonucleases that have been previously studied quantitatively by single-molecule measurements. Using ensemble measurements based on ubiquitously used agarose gel electrophoresis, we qualitatively observed force-dependent behaviour for EcoRV and force-independent behaviour for BamHI, replicating previous data for these enzymes. Interestingly, we also observed force-dependent behaviour for EcoRI, whose restriction behaviour has been previously described as force-independent.
items.author: Ermatov, A., Matthies, M., Sulc, P. et al.

items.title: Biomolecular design through latent reasoning with RFD4-Proteina
items.summary: Biomolecular design requires finding chemically and geometrically compatible arrangements of interacting atoms and molecules. The complexity of problems which can be tackled by deep learning design models is limited by both the molecular landscape they encompass and their ability to explore that landscape effectively. Here we introduce RFD4-Proteina, which addresses these limitations through intrinsic and extrinsic reasoning within a shared chemical and conformational latent space. The latent space encompasses standard and modified amino acids, sugars, DNA, and RNA, with force-field supervision favoring physically plausible atomic reconstructions. Within this space, intrinsic reasoning uses recurrent refinement to adaptively allocate computation, while extrinsic reasoning guides search with arbitrary constraints such as energetic or geometric criteria.
items.author: Corley, N., Didi, K., Kazman, M. W. et al.

items.title: ISdetector: precise mapping of insertion sequences and associated structural variations from short-read sequencing data
items.summary: Motivation. Repetitive insertion sequences (ISs) and adjacent structural variants (SVs) complicate precise mapping from bacte-rial short reads. Accurate insertion coordinates are important for studying genome evolution and tracking transmission. Results. ISdetector constructs IS-specific references with target copies removed and clusters soft-clipped reads to pinpoint insertion sites. On simulated genomes, it had higher recall and F1 score than ISMapper and MGEFinder. On 19 Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes, it achieved the highest high-confidence F1 score (0.86). On five Shigella sonnei genomes, it performed comparably to ISMapper (F1 score 0.85). It detected 81 of 105 IS6110 copies with associated SVs or complex events, versus 41 (ISMapper) and 12 (MGEFinder).
items.author: Zhou, Y., Lu, B., Zhao, Y.

items.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
items.summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important challenge. To address this challenge, we propose st2sc (Spatial Transcriptomics to Single-Cell), an end-to-end framework for inferring single-cell gene profiles from multicellular ST data. st2sc introduces a novel Attention Gradient Flow Tracking (AGFT) algorithm that extracts attention maps from a Vision-Gene Transformer to identify candidate cell instances without predefined background constraints.
items.author: Lee, Y. J., Shah, S., Mantrala, S. et al.

items.title: DNA methylation assigns sequencing reads to closely related bacterial strains when their sequence cannot
items.summary: Clinical and public-health questions often concern strains rather than species, yet co-resident strains of one species can be so closely related that a single long read carries no sequence difference between them. We measured how often this happens in 639 pairs of isolates of Enterococcus faecium, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus sequenced on one nanopore platform. Among the 297 pairs above 99% average nucleotide identity (ANI), 40.37% of read placements (a read counted against one strain's genome) carried no sequence difference between the two strains, and above 99.9% ANI about three quarters did. Strains of one species also differ in the DNA motifs they methylate.
items.author: Kakabra, K., Claesson, M. J.

items.title: Point mutations in the FimH lectin domain: predicted folding stability versus conformational dynamics for R60P, Q133K and Y137A
items.summary: Background. The adhesin FimH attaches uropathogenic Escherichia coli to the urinary epithelium through a force-regulated catch-bond that single lectin-domain substitutions can modulate. How such substitutions reshape the dynamics of the isolated lectin domain, and whether stability predictors anticipate them, is unclear. Methods. We compared the wild-type (WT) lectin domain (PDB 4XO8, apo) with R60P, Y137A and Q133K, using three 500 ns molecular dynamics (MD) replicates per system (6 microseconds total) and three folding-stability predictors (FoldX, a Cartesian-ddG-type Rosetta protocol, ERIS-2). The replicate was the unit of analysis (n = 3), with 95% confidence intervals and a WT replicate-to-replicate control. Results.
items.author: Navas Passos, J. A., Pereira Tapia, A., Velez Duncan, C. et al.

items.title: A Rare Constitutional Centromeric Expansion of Chromosome 1 in a Phenotypically Normal Individual: A Comprehensive Cytogenetic Study
items.summary: Constitutional centromeric heteromorphisms are uncommon chromosomal variants that may complicate cytogenetic interpretation. We report a constitutional enlargement of the centromeric region of one chromosome 1 homologue identified incidentally during biological dose estimation in a suspected occupationally exposed individual. Conventional cytogenetics, pancentromeric fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and multiplex FISH confirmed the variant and excluded cryptic chromosomal rearrangements. Analysis of 500 metaphases revealed no dicentric chromosomes. Quantitative assessment demonstrated a centromere to chromosome length ratio of 0.314 plus/minus 0.019 for the enlarged homologue compared with 0.169 plus/minus 0.019 for the unaffected homologue and 0.161 to 0.186 in controls, representing an approximately 1.86 fold increase (t = 28.4, p < 0.0001).
items.author: Shirsath, K. B., Desai, U. N., Notnani, A. et al.

items.title: Fast and background-suppressed DNA-PAINT
items.summary: The speed and resolution of DNA-PAINT imaging is partly limited by the background fluorescence at high imager-strand concentrations. Here, we combine the photoactivatable fluorophore-quencher-DNA probes with the photoactivation, diffusion, and excitation strategy on a spinning disk confocal microscope, decoupling background fluorescence from the imager-strand concentration. This method yields >7-fold faster DNA-PAINT imaging in cells, a ~15 nm localization precision in hydrogels, without using specialized or speed-optimized imager strands.
items.author: Sun, T., Liu, S., Zhang, X. et al.

items.title: Tycholyzer: NanoTemper NT.6 Tycho Analysis Tool
items.summary: NanoTemper Tycho NT.6 is a nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nanoDSF) instrument that enables rapid measurement of apparent protein melting temperatures. Thermal shift assays are widely used to assess protein stability under different conditions, including screening for protein-ligand interactions. These experiments often involve multiple samples, conditions, and replicates collected across several instrument runs, generating datasets that can be cumbersome to organize, compare, and analyze quantitatively. Here, we introduce Tycholyzer, a user-friendly software application that streamlines processing and analysis of Tycho nanoDSF data. Tycholyzer allows users to combine data from multiple runs, inspect and select individual fluorescence traces, and normalize and group replicate profiles for comparison across experimental conditions.
items.author: Ghani, V. G., Boudker, O.

items.title: Minor intron splicing restricts E2F transcription factor activity in RB-deregulated prostate cancer
items.summary: Castration-resistant prostate cancer with neuroendocrine differentiation (CRPC-NE) arises in RB1-mutated lineage plastic cells in response to androgen receptor (AR)-targeted therapies. RB1 loss leads to constitutive E2F activation and cylin-dependent kinase (CDK) inhibitor resistance, making it challenging to restrict E2F activity. A post-transcriptional node is that typical E2Fs contain a rare but highly conserved minor intron, processed by the minor spliceosome (MiS). In an in vivo CRISPR screen, we nominate the MiS as the strongest dependency, and U6atac correlates strongest with E2F transcriptional programs in a clinical CRPC cohort. U6atac depletion led to mis-splicing of typical E2Fs, cell cycle arrest, and translation of a minor intron-containing E2F1 isoform (E2F1-MIRI) as a pharmacodynamic biomarker.
items.author: Thienger, P., Paassen, I., Maier, B. et al.

items.title: EcoToxFred: A knowledge-graph-grounded conversational agent for exploring ecotoxicological monitoring and hazard data
items.summary: Assessing chemical risks to aquatic ecosystems requires the joint interpretation of monitoring data, ecotoxicity data, and derived risk indicators, yet such integrated data are rarely accessible to users without database expertise. We present EcoToxFred, an open-source conversational agent that provides natural language access to a curated knowledge graph of chemical monitoring and hazard data for European surface waters. EcoToxFred couples a large language model (LLM) with a Neo4j graph database in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture. An agent interprets user questions, selects tools, translates questions into graph queries, and returns answers as text, tables, or interactive maps, together with the executed query for reproducibility.
items.author: Scheibe, P., Schmid, T. S., Schor, J.

items.title: Ultrasensitive Regulation in the Tryptophan System in Escherichia coli Provides Effective Noise Mitigation
items.summary: The tryptophan system in Escherichia coli maintains intracellular concentration of tryptophan in a narrow band regardless of the nutritional status and uncertainty in its environment. The system is characterized by three distinct regulations namely, genetic regulation, mRNA attenuation and enzyme inhibition, that use the tryptophan concentration as a feedback signal. It has been shown previously, that the multiple feedback loop design is responsible for rapid synthesis of tryptophan when faced with starvation. It is well known that a design with rapid response to external signals also implies poorer noise mitigation properties. This work investigates the design elements that limit the adverse impact of the multiple feedback loop architecture on noise propagation in the tryptophan system using a frequency response analysis.
items.author: Bavdekar, V., Bhartiya, S., Venkatesh, K. V.

items.title: Combination of in vitro and ex vivo infection models highlights the role of NAD-dependent ADP-ribosylation in Influenza A virus infection.
items.summary: Influenza A viruses (IAV) remain a major public health concern, causing an estimated 650 000 deaths annually. Although vaccines are available, vaccination coverage is limited and must be repeated annually due to the genetic variability of these viruses. Furthermore, although direct acting antivirals are available, they must be administered as early as possible after infection to be effective. In this context, understanding the metabolic alterations associated with the replication and pathogenesis of IAV could contribute to the development of treatments that promote virus clearance and patient recovery. In this study, we identified the intracellular level of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) as a key factor in the replication of IAV.
items.author: Jacolin, F., Aublin-Gex, A., Vellet, M. et al.

items.title: Azospirillum brasilense and cytidine as combination treatment to enhance drought resilience of peas
items.summary: Aims: This study tested the efficacy of two combination treatments on drought resilience of peas; Azospirillum brasilense Sp7 with the chemoattractant seedling exudate compound cytidine or pea seedling exudate. Methods and Results: Phenotypic characterization revealed that drought tolerance of peas treated with ACyt was 68.9% higher than that of peas treated with the inoculant alone (A). Dry shoot weight of ACyt Drought plants was 30.7% higher than that of plants from the untreated control group NB Drought, drought recovery of ACyt plants was 21.6% better. The treatment with seedling exudate (AEx) was less effective. 16S rDNA analysis revealed that increase in drought tolerance was accompanied by modulation of the rhizosphere.
items.author: Ojha, B., Tagoe, J., Horne, S. M. et al.
