items.title: Three-dimensional parton structure in QCD with CP-violation
items.summary: The Energy-Momentum tensor encodes the mechanical properties of a system such as the internal distributions energy, momentum, forces, and particle fluxes. The QCD energy momentum tensor respects CP symmetry even when QCD is modified with a CP-violating $θ$-term. In this theory, there are 5 unique generalized form factors in the Lorentz decomposition of the total Energy Momentum tensor and 3 more which only vanish when summing over all flavors. We introduce two new lightcone GPDs whose Mellin moments give the electromagnetic and gravitational form factors. These generalize the observables for QCD-based CP violation such as the neutron electric dipole moment to three dimensional light cone structure.
items.author: Alexandru-Mihail Sturzu, Joe Karpie

items.title: Pressure and Magnetic Field Control of Topology in Antiferromagnetic Bilayers
items.summary: Controlling band topology in magnetic semiconductors requires strategies that couple electronic structure to experimentally accessible degrees of freedom. Here we propose a cooperative approach based on pressure and magnetic reorientation in A-type antiferromagnetic bilayers. Antiparallel layer magnetizations suppress hybridization between exchange-polarized band-edge states, limiting their response to interlayer compression. A magnetic field that aligns the layer moments removes this spin mismatch, enabling pressure-enhanced hybridization to drive a band inversion. The magnetization direction then controls the symmetries of the inverted bands and whether spin--orbit coupling produces a Chern-insulating gap or symmetry-protected nodal crossings. First-principles calculations for bilayer CrSBr illustrate this mechanism within a compressed orthorhombic structural model.
items.author: Narsimha Rao Elaprolu, Marco Gibertini

items.title: The Spectral Anatomy of Complex-Time Singularities
items.summary: The properties of the bulk spacetime in a holographic theory may be probed by the analytic structure of the boundary correlator $G(t,x)$. In this letter, we analyse the singularities of $G(t,x)$ by deriving them from Fourier space. We show that the quasinormal modes are characterised by two distinct momentum scaling regimes. The first regime is defined by a finite $k/ω^γ$ for some characteristic exponent $γ$ which is extracted from the singularity, and probes $G(t,0)$, reproducing the bouncing geodesic analysis. The second regime is defined by a finite $k/ω$, and probes the complexified bulk away from the singularity, which allows us to study the singularities of $G(t,x\neq 0)$.
items.author: Samuel Valach, Mile Vrbica

items.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
items.summary: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order $\mathcal{H}/k$ of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation.
items.author: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca et al.

items.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
items.summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. This paper examines the challenges MI tools face when applied to realistic agentic failures. We focus on one such failure: web agents hallucinating actions that are not available on a website. We apply a series of mechanistic analyzes to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as it interacts with live websites. We find that a linear probe trained on the last prompt token can predict hallucinations before generation begins (0.80 AUC) and steering along a probe direction corrects 85\% of hallucinations, but disrupts 7\% of valid actions.
items.author: Mohamed Aghzal, Mor Geva, Gregory J. Stein et al.

items.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
items.summary: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architecture, combining vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings, to ensure high fidelity to the reader's current context. We evaluate the system across classical English books using both quantitative comprehension metrics and qualitative LLM-based independent judging.
items.author: Mohammed Efaz, Udo Bub, Itilekha Podder

items.title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys
items.summary: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. With next-generation FRB surveys the number of bursts will drastically increase and measurements of the baryon distribution will be possible on the Mpc scales most relevant to Stage IV weak lensing surveys. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales.
items.author: Haruki Ebina, Martin White

items.title: Complex fluid flow dynamics by bright scattershot boson sampling
items.summary: Boson sampling machines have become a fruitful tool for establishing new concepts, which connect fundamental physics with computer science applications. Here, we exploit the intrinsically high-dimensional correlations generated by the measurement outcomes of a multiphoton boson sampling machine and demonstrate how a reconfigurable architecture can be programmed to autonomously model the time evolution of nonlinear dynamical systems that describe complex fluid flows. By extending on the original scattershot boson sampling (SBS) scheme to include higher photon number components -- a scheme which we label bright scattershot boson sampling (BSBS) --- this scheme overcomes scaling issues inherent to SBS-based schemes by utilizing all randomly generated input photon number distributions.
items.author: Robert Schade, Shailendra K. Rathor, Tim J. Bartley et al.

items.title: Disturbance-Aware Informative Planning in Spatiotemporal Environments
items.summary: Autonomous robots are widely used for persistent monitoring of spatiotemporal environments, where quantities of interest (QoI) change across space and time and require repeated measurements. In practice, robot motion can be affected by external disturbances that vary across the environment. When such external disturbances are not considered in trajectory optimization, it can lead to inaccurate predictions of robot motion and, consequently, the information acquired about the QoI during execution. However, estimating disturbances throughout the environment can be inefficient, as disturbances in regions with little overlap with monitoring trajectories have limited impact on monitoring performance. We therefore propose a two-stage informative planning framework for unknown, spatially varying but time-invariant disturbances, combining informed disturbance sampling with disturbance-aware trajectory optimization.
items.author: Kaleb Ben Naveed, Haejoon Lee, Anouck Girard et al.

items.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. The full stack of quantum computing encompasses several tasks: preparation of logical code states, implementation of logical gates, logical routines on encoded qubits, etc. Yet, these circuits are largely designed by hand for individual cases, with some recent works incorporating machine learning for certain aspects. We formulate this problem as agentic evolutionary program synthesis, wherein a large language model, leveraging its pretraining knowledge and tool-use proficiency, and guided by a circuit verifier, evolves a program that defines a Clifford circuit for a wide range of curated tasks such as logical state preparation, logical gate design, and logical routines such as code-switching, code growth, etc.
items.author: Aritra Lahiri, Florian Marquardt

items.title: Solution of the Qubit Marginal Problem from Fermionic Representability
items.summary: Whether local reduced states are compatible with a global quantum state---the quantum marginal problem---is central to quantum information and simulation. Here we present a solution to the ensemble marginal problem for qubits based on the representability theory of fermions. Encoding each qubit as one fermion in two orbitals, we prove that the representable qubit marginals form an exposed face of the set of $N$-representable fermionic reduced density matrices, selected by the vanishing of every site-occupation variance. Complete hierarchies of fermionic representability conditions therefore transfer exactly to qubits. Applications to frustrated Heisenberg and transverse-field Ising rings show that the $(2,3)$-positivity conditions are exact at the Majumdar--Ghosh point and accurate to about 0.5% at criticality.
items.author: David A. Mazziotti

items.title: In Situ Monitoring and Predictive Modeling of Harmful Algal Blooms with Autonomous Surface Vehicles
items.summary: Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs) pose significant environmental, economic, and public-health challenges in coastal and inland water bodies, creating a need for scalable methods to collect spatially distributed water-quality data. This paper presents an autonomous surface vessel-based sensing system for in-situ water-quality monitoring related to harmful algal bloom detection. The system integrates a BlueBoat Autonomous Surface Vessel (ASV), a motorized winch for depth-controlled sonde deployment, a multiparameter water-quality sonde, side-scan sonar, and an event-camera payload. Autonomous waypoint missions were used to collect measurements across selected sampling regions and multiple depths, enabling both horizontal and vertical characterization of environmental conditions. Field deployments were conducted in Lake Pontchartrain, Louisiana, with additional measurements collected in False River, Louisiana to increase dataset diversity.
items.author: Nenyi Kweku Nkensen Dadson, Jean Paul Gonzalez, Daniel P. Arabie et al.

items.title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions
items.summary: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) accelerate scientific research by integrating robotics, automated experimentation, and machine learning to execute experiments autonomously. Biology and chemistry have adopted these systems. However, increasing SDL complexity heightens susceptibility to unexpected faults in automated workflows, highlighting the need for efficient recovery mechanisms. In this study, we investigate telerobotic interventions to enhance SDL resilience against unexpected failures. We developed a teleoperation interface enabling human operators to resolve disruptions during automated tasks. The interface enables precise control of a six-degree-of-freedom (DOF) robotic arm (UR3e) using a 3D mouse (3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Pro). Two velocity-based controller strategies were evaluated: (i) a coupled mode mapping all six DOFs to the 3D mouse's central knob and (ii) a decoupled mode separating translational and rotational motions.
items.author: Ziheng Wu, Adrian Vecina Tercero, Andre A. Fatehi et al.

items.title: Blind in-memory arithmetic with confined skyrmions: doubling and successor functions on a skyrmion byte
items.summary: We present a skyrmionic-based computation platform, able to perform fully in-memory computing by collectively manipulating the skyrmions that serve as bits of the binary memory. The computation protocols are implemented through driving currents and adequately located anisotropy defects that modify the dynamics of the skyrmions along a magnetic track. Simulations demonstrating the feasibility of such an in-memory computing system are shown for several basic and simple mathematical operations with natural numbers, such as doubling and adding one (the successor function). We also discuss how further optimization of the geometry, barrier profiles, current amplitudes, and timing parameters could improve both the robustness and the overall practical feasibility of the system.
items.author: Joan Reverté, Nuria Del-Valle, Jaume Cunill-Subiranas et al.

items.title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners
items.summary: Cooperative self-play can teach a humanoid to receive an object without any human data, but the partner it meets after training is never the one it trained with; we show that a fluent self-play handover policy breaks with unfamiliar partners, identify the main cause, and repair it. In a physics-based parcel handover between a Unitree G1 and a learned giver, both trained by alternating PPO self-play, the receiver completes 95% and 90% of handovers with its own partner (two training seeds) but only 31% with scripted partners it has never met. Paired interventions isolate the cause: under a shared reward the learned giver always starts its offer at once, so the receiver learns a single rendezvous, and delaying its own partner by one second cuts success from 95% to 6% (87% to 34% in the second seed).
items.author: Mohammad Khoshnazar, Mike Degany, Deyuan Qu et al.

items.title: Fine-tuned atomistic foundation model for accurate sodium-carbon chemistry in Na-ion batteries
items.summary: Atomistic foundation models have emerged as a promising route to DFT-level accuracy for materials simulation with complex chemical environments. However, their reliability across competing bonding regimes and, more importantly, how complex bonding affects predictions of material properties remain unclear. Among materials with competing bonding regimes, sodium storage in hard carbon poses a substantial challenge. Hard carbon features diverse local structural motifs, including defective and curved graphitic regions, amorphous regions, and closed/open pores. Motivated by its importance for Na-ion batteries, we systematically evaluate existing pretrained foundation models based on the MACE architecture across different local Na/C motifs. We find that the pretrained models fail to accurately capture Na-Na and Na-C interactions for metallic Na clusters on graphene.
items.author: Andres Felipe Usuga, Ihor Radchenko, Yuxin Tang et al.

items.title: Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
items.summary: We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin ($S=5/2$) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself, $\mathrm{Tr}[ρ_M^2]\approx0.8$. Modeling this channel with rates fixed by the measured optical pumping of a single Mn spin, we find that the entanglement it enables is not monotonic in the pump strength: it peaks at a finite rate and then decreases, since the same channel leaks decoherence to the qubits through the coupling that mediates their entanglement.
items.author: Ellen Martins Fernandes, Fabricio Macedo de Souza

items.title: A charge-dependent electron emission yield from electron irradiated dielectrics
items.summary: The total electron emission yield (TEEY) of dielectric surfaces may vary during electron irradiation owing to charge accumulation within the material. In the present work, the generation, transport, and escape formulation of Dionne is extended by introducing an additional attenuation of secondary electrons that depends on trapped positive charge. The resulting emission law is coupled to a charge-balance equation, allowing the TEEY to be calculated as a function of incident energy and injected charge. The model is examined using measurements on polycrystalline Al2O3, from which effective cross sections describing interactions between trapped charge and secondary electrons are determined. Their mean value is then used to predict the evolution of the TEEY curves without further adjustment.
items.author: M. Belhaj, A. M. Cavalca de Almeida, N. Fil

items.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
items.summary: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. Healthcare robotics makes the transition from monitoring to action especially visible by translating AI-generated recommendations and decisions into speech, movement, prompting, physical assistance, escalation, and care coordination, making embodiment, clinical integration, human oversight, and governance fundamental design requirements. Further progress requires safe and interoperable care architectures in which intelligent components operate through clinically validated and accountable workflows.
items.author: Ivana Ragusa, Lorenzo Guiducci, Filippo Cavallo

items.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
items.summary: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $μ$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $μ$s per round.
items.author: Jiayu Fu, Zirong Shen, Lin Gan et al.

items.title: Machine learning of strength surfaces enables high regularization length phase-field fracture
items.summary: Classical phase-field models of brittle fracture capture toughness-controlled crack growth but not the material's strength surface, which governs crack nucleation. The theory of Kumar et al. (2020) incorporates the strength surface through a nucleation driving force, and Chockalingam (2025) derived this driving force for arbitrary strength surfaces described by $n$ material parameters, with which the phase-field strength surface (PFSS) converges to the material strength surface as the regularization length $\varepsilon \to 0$ and matches it exactly at $n$ chosen states for any $\varepsilon$. In practice, however, the strength surface must be supplied as an analytic form chosen and calibrated case by case, and for the widely used analytic surfaces ($n=2$) accurate strength reproduction requires $\varepsilon$ commensurate with the Irwin characteristic length $l_{ch}$, imposing prohibitive mesh requirements for large structures.
items.author: S Chockalingam, Aditya Kumar, Adrian Buganza Tepole

items.title: Exploring M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$: Mellin amplitudes with composite operators
items.summary: We bootstrap mixed correlators in M-theory on AdS$_7\times$S$^4$, focusing on tree-level correlation functions involving one double-particle operator and three single-particle operators. Combining inputs from AdS/CFT, the chiral algebra, and the OPE at large central charge, we uniquely determine the Mellin amplitude for $\langle [{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{q}]{\cal O}_{2}{\cal O}_{p}{\cal O}_{p+q-2}\rangle$ for generic $p$ and $q$. While our main focus is the $\mathcal{N}=(2,0)$ SCFT in six dimensions, we also derive the analogous result in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, applying the same bootstrap approach to $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM. Despite their different dynamics, the resulting Mellin amplitudes exhibit a strikingly similar structure, with non-trivial OPE predictions for low-twist protected operators providing a key input.
items.author: Francesco Aprile, Hector Puerta-Ramisa, Mitchell Woolley

items.title: Symmetry-Controlled Quantum State Transfer in Poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene: From Heisenberg to Hubbard Dynamics
items.summary: We investigate quantum state transfer in the poly-bi-[8]-annulenylene lattice using isotropic Heisenberg and Hubbard models. For a 16-site lattice, reflection symmetry separates the single-excitation Hamiltonian into independent triplet and singlet sectors, allowing analytical determination of the energy spectra. Although perfect state transfer is forbidden for positive couplings, appropriately chosen coupling ratios enable pretty-good transfer with arbitrarily high fidelity. Remarkably, the triplet transfer probability is independent of the interchain rung coupling, while singlet transfer can be selectively enhanced or suppressed, enabling symmetry-selective quantum transport without time-dependent control. Extending the analysis to the Hubbard model, we show that the Heisenberg transfer dynamics emerge in the strong-interaction limit, while finite interactions delay all high-fidelity transfer peaks of a symmetry sector by the same fraction of their transfer time, set by the spectrum, and reduce the peak fidelity, even at the corrected time, by an amount that grows with the transfer time.
items.author: Adnan Jaljuli, Pablo Serra, Ammar Ali et al.

items.title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
items.summary: Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector $k=0$, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes. We identify seven regions in this lane, with four distinct topological phases, characterized by different Zak phases of the three bands.
items.author: P. A. Grizzi, P. Roura-Bas, A. A. Aligia

items.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
items.summary: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems.
items.author: Yuehaw Khoo, Bowen Li, Yuguan Wang et al.

items.title: High Entropy Oxides as Room Temperature Anderson Insulators with Colossal Soft Gaps
items.summary: The Anderson effect, arising from destructive quantum interference of electron wave packets in disordered potentials, is usually observed at cryogenic temperatures and typically arises from extrinsic defects in conventional materials such as phosphorus dopants in silicon or oxygen vacancies in transition metal oxides. Here we demonstrate that a multication lattice of transition metals in a high-entropy oxide (HEO) natively establishes an interacting Anderson insulator that extends up to $500\,\mathrm{K}$. By controlling the population of transition metal cations in $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1-x}(\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Ni})_{x/4}\mathrm{O}_3$ (LS5B), we tune the system from the prototypical correlated metal $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{O}_3$ at $x=0.00$ to a localized insulator at $x=0.80$, where the disorder length contracts to near the unit cell (3.85 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$) and drives the electron mean free path to the Ioffe-Regel limit.
items.author: Elena Salagre, Heather Hare, Eli Rotenberg et al.

items.title: Validating Graph Neural Network Feature Attribution Through Local Perturbations: A Study on CoMoFeNiCu Decomposition Enthalpy
items.summary: Graph neural networks (GNNs) show promise for predicting materials properties, but interpretability remains a challenge, particularly understanding whether attributed feature importance reflects physical reality or statistical artifacts. Here, we present a methods validation study that deliberately overfits a physics-aware GNN ensemble to probe the robustness of feature-ranking approaches. Using the CoMoFeNiCu high-entropy alloy system with three stoichiometries, we train GNNs to predict decomposition enthalpies from DFT-calculated structures while explicitly constraining output weights to encode feature importance. By design, our dataset is limited (approximately 900 binary and 4,500 ternary decomposition pathways) to control compositional complexity and enable precise interrogation of local chemistry effects.
items.author: Miguel Tenorio, James Chapman

items.title: Tunable Hybridization of Whispering Gallery Modes in High-Index Photonic Molecules
items.summary: Photonic molecules formed by coupled dielectric microresonators provide a platform for controlling collective optical modes, yet the interplay between molecular topology, resonator detuning, and dielectric environment in determining their spectral response remains insufficiently quantified. Here, we systematically quantify the evolution of Whispering Gallery Mode (WGM) hybridization in high-index TiO$_2$ and perovskite coated TiO$_2$ microresonators with molecular topology, and establish the corresponding effective inter-cavity coupling using a combined numerical and analytical analysis. We further show that perovskite-shell incorporation provides a diameter and thickness-dependent modification of the effective coupling, producing a non-monotonic response rather than a uniform suppression of coupling. Despite the resulting closely spaced hybridized resonances in the high-index perovskite environment, the supermodes remain spectrally resolvable, with $Q$-factor of order \(10^3\) for representative modes.

items.title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
items.summary: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total.
items.author: Cong Xu, Ravi Sankar

items.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
items.summary: Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design. Here we introduce Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer (GaDiT), a generative model that combines dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution. GaDiT generates high-quality disordered structures while accelerating sampling by two orders of magnitude compared with existing corrector-based approaches, as demonstrated across two-dimensional amorphous carbon and three-dimensional amorphous silicon and silica. Moreover, GaDiT supports conditional generation under single or combined structural features, physical properties and preparation conditions in a unified model, and enables inverse design that expands accessible structure-property ranges beyond the training distribution.

items.title: Gravitational Corrections to OPE Coefficients
items.summary: The short-distance singular behavior of correlation functions of quantum field theories in curved spacetime is a universal property shared by all well-behaved states (known as Hadamard states). For two-point functions this takes the form of the Hadamard tail of free scalars and its generalizations to spinning fields and interacting theories. In this work, we compute similar universal curvature corrections to curved-space OPE coefficients in a short-distance expansion for interacting quantum field theories in general dimensions. We work at leading order in the curvature but for arbitrary backgrounds. Examples include weakly coupled scalar field theories with cubic and quartic interactions as well as strongly coupled conformal field theories.
items.author: Ameya Chavda, Alessandro Podo, John Staunton

items.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
items.summary: Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay $t_{\mathrm{SR}}$ and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number $N$. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss. Here we extend the analytical treatment of superradiance to variable emitter numbers using the Schwinger-boson mapping of the collective spin onto two bosonic modes. In this formulation, collective decay annihilates an atom in the excited-state mode and creates one in the ground-state mode.
items.author: Christian Niehof, Nico S. Bassler, Claudiu Genes

items.title: Uniaxial strain induces $d$-wave phonon chirality in ferroelectric BaTiO$_3$
items.summary: Circularly dichroic resonant inelastic x-ray scattering has revealed electrically switchable $g$-wave phonon chirality in freestanding BaTiO$_3$ membranes. Here, we show from first principles that uniaxial strain changes the angular class of this texture. Lowering $C_{4v}$ to $C_{2v}$ adds a $d$-wave helicity that is bilinear in the orthorhombic strain $η$ and the polarization, with nodal lines along the stress axis. For the 38~meV branches at $η=1\%$, we find that (i) along the diagonal, where the helicity vanishes by symmetry without strain, it reaches about 60\% of the unstrained maximum, and (ii) at the measured wave vectors off the mirror it is reduced by more than half.

items.title: Enhanced Hyperspectral Nano-FTIR Imaging by Neural-Network-Based Processing of Multiple Signal Harmonics
items.summary: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy combines infrared spectroscopy with nanometer-scale spatial resolution and enables hyperspectral nanoimaging. However, quantitative measurements typically rely on higher-harmonic near-field signals, which are largely background-free but suffer from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Lower harmonics provide substantially higher SNR but contain significant background contributions that distort the near-field response and hinder quantitative analysis. Here, we introduce a cross-harmonic neural network (CHNN) that exploits the complementary information encoded in multiple harmonic channels to denoise third-harmonic hyperspectral data. Trained directly on experimental nano-FTIR datasets, the CHNN uses first- and second-harmonic spectra to improve the SNR of the third-harmonic response. Applied to a PMMA/PS polymer blend, it substantially reduces noise while preserving spectral features and nanoscale spatial contrast.
items.author: Pablo Calvo-Barlés, Sergio G. Rodrigo, Luis Martín-Moreno et al.

items.title: On the origin and geometry of anomaly-related poles in Double Deeply Virtual Compton Scattering
items.summary: Anomaly-related poles have been reported in one-loop box amplitudes for the gluon-initiated channel of double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS). The residues of these poles carry the gluonic operator structures associated with the chiral and trace anomalies. The origin of the poles within the box amplitude has remained unclear. In this work, we trace both poles to a subleading Landau singularity on the boundary of the box's Feynman-parameter domain, where one parameter vanishes and the remaining three propagators form a triangle subdiagram. We examine the same boundary using dimensional regularization (DR), nonzero momentum transfer $t$, and a finite quark mass $m$.

items.title: Gemini Space Photos Sparked Earth Observation Programs
items.summary: During the final Gemini XII mission in November 1966, astronauts James A. Lovell Jr. and Edwin E. “Buzz” Aldrin Jr. captured photographs of Earth's surface from space. These images demonstrated the scientific value of orbital imagery and helped researchers make a strong case for dedicated Earth observation satellite programs. William T. Pecora, director of the United States Geological Survey, later noted that this Mercury and Gemini photography directly inspired the creation of the Earth Resources Observation Satellite program. That initiative ultimately paved the way for the Landsat program, which has spent over five decades providing essential global data for monitoring agriculture, wildfires, flooding, and other environmental changes.

items.title: Gravitational production of dark QED by the trace anomaly
items.summary: We revisit the production of fermionic dark matter $χ$ through the graviton portal, sourced by inflaton annihilation at the end of inflation. Because the production rate is helicity-suppressed, $\propto m_χ^2$, the dark fermion must be very heavy to account for the observed relic abundance, $m_χ\gtrsim 10^{10}$ GeV, with the exact bound set by the reheating temperature $T_{\rm RH}$. Here we examine how interactions within the dark sector could modify this result. As a toy model, we consider dark QED, in which $χ$ couples to a light dark photon. We first show that, as a consequence of classical conformal invariance, bremsstrahlung of a dark photon does not lift the helicity suppression for light fermions.
items.author: Simon Cléry, Aliaksei Kachanovich, Michel HG Tytgat

items.title: Connecting High-Twist Expansion and Color Glass Condensate Dynamics
items.summary: The high-twist (HT) expansion and the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) describe nuclear multiple scattering in complementary kinematic regimes. For direct-photon production in proton-nucleus collisions, we formulate an arbitrary-order multiple-scattering master expression that includes photon emission before, between, or after the ordered quark scatterings in the amplitude and its conjugate. In the high-energy limit, resumming multiple scatterings to all orders recovers the CGC Wilson-line dipole result. However, the naive power expansion of the eikonal CGC result reproduces the leading twist but only part of the twist-four contribution obtained in the HT expansion. Including longitudinal sub-eikonal phases and Landau-Pomeranchuk-Migdal interference restores the CGC-HT correspondence through twist-4.
items.author: Yu Fu, Zhong-Bo Kang, Farid Salazar et al.

items.title: Bond Anharmonicity in a Caged Molecule Probed by Vibronic Core Spectroscopy
items.summary: X-ray absorption spectroscopy and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at the nitrogen K-edge show that the N$\equiv$N bond in N$_2$@C$_{60}$ is substantially more anharmonic than in free N$_2$, with the ground-state ($X^1Σ_g^+$) anharmonic constant $\hbarω_e x_e$ a factor of two larger ($3.8\pm0.3$~meV versus $\sim 1.8$~meV) despite an essentially unchanged harmonic frequency. The same enhancement is found across all three vibronic potentials accessible to the experiment---the electronic ground state, the core-excited intermediate state, and the spectator-decay final state---pointing to a common origin rather than an effect specific to one electronic configuration. High-level coupled-cluster calculations of the N$_2$@C$_{60}$ potential energy surface, however, find no significant change in anharmonicity upon encapsulation, ruling out a simple static distortion of the N$\equiv$N bonding potential by the fullerene cage.
items.author: Connor J. B. Fields, Bang Huynh, Filipe Junqueira et al.

items.title: Towards an improved understanding of $a_1$ and $a_2$ transition form factors
items.summary: The isovector axial-vector and tensor meson states $a_1$ and $a_2$ have garnered interest in the last years since they appear as intermediate states in the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution to $(g-2)_μ$. Their dynamical behaviour including their transition form factors is poorly understood to this day, which also affects the uncertainty budget of the HLbL contribution. In order to improve the situation, we construct the $a_1$ and $a_2$ as resonances in the $ρπ$ system, which allows us to express the relevant amplitudes in terms of known form factors and properties of the resonances. With this, we aim to obtain a phenomenologically well motivated parameterisation of the transition form factors built from the general principles of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry.

items.title: Are hybrid hydrodynamic models missing soft-pion physics?
items.summary: In this work, we perform a systematic Bayesian analysis of the full parameter space of a state-of-the-art hybrid hydrodynamical model and show that no combination of parameters provides a satisfactory description of the low-$p_T$ region of the pion $(π^{\pm})$ transverse-momentum spectra. This suggests that an additional mechanism enhancing pion production at low $p_T$ may be needed to properly describe the ALICE data. We first reexamine and confirm the existence of an excess of low $p_T$ pions relative to model predictions, showing that no comparable excess is observed in the spectra of kaons $(K^\pm)$, protons $(p)$, or antiprotons $(\bar{p})$. We further demonstrate that this excess persists under a rigorous Bayesian analysis of simulations that include, e.g., a hadronic afterburner, a feature omitted in previous similar studies.
items.author: Osvaldo Ferreira, Thiago S. Domingues, Fernando G. Gardim et al.

items.title: Commercial AlGaAs diodes provide simplified feedback for adaptive femtosecond pulse compression
items.summary: Maintaining high peak power in ultrashort laser pulses is essential for efficient nonlinear interactions, particularly in multiphoton microscopy. Dispersion introduced by optical components broadens these pulses and degrades their peak power, thus motivating adaptive pulse compression guided by pulse-width-dependent feedback. However, the conventional second-harmonic generation feedback requires a nonlinear crystal, spectral filtering, and careful optical alignment. Here, we investigate commercially available AlGaAs laser and light-emitting diodes as alternative two-photon absorption feedback sensors. Their photocurrent exhibits a quadratic dependence on average optical power and inverse dependence on pulse duration, which is consistent with the analytical model predicting maximum response for the shortest, single-peaked pulse.
items.author: Patrycja H. Wysowska, Adrian Chlebowski, Lukasz A. Sterczewski et al.

items.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
items.summary: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories.
items.author: Thomas Nicosanti, Pavel Putrov, Johann Quenta-Raygada

items.title: Light baryon masses from the modified Taylor coupling
items.summary: We present a calculation of the positive-parity baryon octet and decuplet spectra, using a non-perturbative interaction governed by the modified Taylor effective charge and complemented by explicit flavour-dependent contributions. The framework transitions seamlessly from the mesonic domain, where it was first established, to the baryonic sector, requiring no further parameter optimization. By solving the relativistic three-body Faddeev equation, we extract both the ground-state masses and amplitudes for the corresponding baryonic configurations. The resulting spectrum reproduces experimental data within a few percent. Additionally, we derive the evolution of the nucleon and $Δ$ masses as functions of the pion mass, contrast our findings directly against lattice-QCD benchmarks, and evaluate the propagation of the lattice uncertainties into the computed hadronic observables.
items.author: A. S. Miramontes, J. Papavassiliou, H. Sanchis-Alepuz

items.title: Destabilization of Abelian-Higgs vortices at large Chern-Simons coupling
items.summary: We study the effect of the Chern--Simons (CS) coupling on the radial spectral stability of axially symmetric vortices in the $(2+1)$-dimensional Abelian--Higgs model. From the linear stability approach, we obtain the dispersion relations of gauge field perturbations, which signal the existence of a critical CS coupling $k_{\rm c}$ that depends on Maxwell's coupling constant. For $k k_{\rm c}$ real eigenvalues appear, corresponding to exponentially growing radial modes. Direct time-evolution simulations are consistent with the spectral analysis, which shows instability for $k>k_{\rm c}$. Below the threshold, the perturbed vortex relaxes toward its stationary profile, whereas above the threshold, growing fluctuations deform the core and propagate outward.

items.title: Children with Developmental Language Disorder Exhibit Impaired Low-Frequency Speech Tracking
items.summary: Researchers investigated whether automatic cortical tracking mechanisms are altered in children with developmental language disorder by recording magnetoencephalography while participants listened to a story. The study found that children with developmental language disorder exhibited significantly reduced speech-brain coherence in the 0.9 to 2.5 Hertz range, which is associated with prosodic information, particularly within the left supramarginal gyrus and bilateral auditory cortex. Reductions were also noted in the 2.5 to 5 Hertz range linked to syllabic-rate modulations. Furthermore, stronger low-frequency speech-brain coherence correlated with better language performance, indicating that these cortical tracking differences are behaviourally meaningful and relevant to language outcomes in developmental language disorder.
items.author: Mahmoud Keshavarzi, Georgia Feltham, Susan Richards et al.
items.original_title: Children with developmental language disorder show selective impairments in low-frequency neural tracking of speech
items.original_summary: by Mahmoud Keshavarzi, Georgia Feltham, Susan Richards, Lyla Parvez, Usha Goswami Neural tracking of slow temporal modulations in speech supports extraction of the prosodic and syllabic structure thought to be critical for language acquisition by Temporal Sampling (TS) theory, yet whether these automatic cortical tracking mechanisms are altered in children with developmental language disorder (DLD) remains unclear. We recorded MEG while children with and without DLD listened to a story, and quantified source-level lagged speech-brain coherence and frequency-specific cortical functional connectivity across bilateral cortical regions. As expected a priori by TS theory, children with DLD showed significantly reduced coherence in the 0.9–2.5 Hz range associated with prosodic information in the story, spanning bilateral auditory and speech-related cortex.

items.title: Stoichiometric Objectives Influence Microbial Catabolism
items.summary: Microbial catabolism serves two primary functions: synthesizing charged energy carriers and producing carbon precursors. Understanding the relationship between these energetic and biosynthetic parameters remains a core challenge in microbiology. Researchers introduced an unbiased method to quantify stoichiometric relationships within genome-scale metabolic models across various heterotrophic species and growth conditions. The findings reveal that heterotrophic catabolism diversity stems from the entanglement of energy carrier charging and precursor synthesis. Acetyl-CoA emerged as the sole universal precursor across species, while ATP requirements for biomass varied widely. Maximal energetic efficiency is achieved by maximizing charged energy carrier yields during precursor synthesis while minimizing the demand for those carriers during macromolecule conversion.
items.author: Maaike Remeijer, Frank J. Bruggeman
items.original_title: Entangled stoichiometric objectives shape microbial catabolism
items.original_summary: by Maaike Remeijer, Frank J. Bruggeman The understanding of fundamental relationships between energetic and biosynthetic parameters of catabolism and anabolism is a central challenge in microbiology. The large diversity of microbial metabolisms can be compared on the basis of our current definitions of catabolism and anabolism. Catabolism has two functions: synthesising charged energy carriers and carbon precursors. Energy carriers, however, are also involved in precursor synthesis, complicating the analysis. We introduce an unbiased method to quantify stoichiometric relationships between catabolism and anabolism in genome-scale metabolic models. We compare catabolic strategies across diverse (heterotrophic) microbial species and growth conditions, focusing on states of maximal biomass yield per unit of energy source.

items.title: HandShake Predicts Protein Binding Sites Using Sequence Data Only
items.summary: Researchers have developed HandShake, a sequence-only predictor designed to identify partner-specific protein-protein binding sites and pairwise contact matrices. The tool integrates the ProstT5 protein language model with Low-Rank Adaptation, cross-chain attention, and a contact supervision head. Tested across various sequence identity thresholds, the authors found that sequence redundancy significantly inflates performance metrics like AUROC and MCC, highlighting a major methodological confound in computational biology. Even at a strict 30% redundancy threshold, HandShake outperformed previous sequence-only methods and matched the performance of techniques that rely on explicit three-dimensional structural information at test time.
items.author: Nurit Haspel
items.original_title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention
items.original_summary: by Nurit Haspel Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language model pre-trained on structural data, with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), a cross-chain attention mechanism and a contact supervision head. Our method can detect both binding interfaces and pairwise contact matrices.

items.title: Genomic Analysis Reveals Extreme Diversity and Conserved Structure in Beetle Evolution
items.summary: A comprehensive study analyzing 190 chromosome-level genome assemblies across 39 beetle families has shed light on chromosomal evolution within the most species-rich animal order. The findings indicate that while beetle genomes vary greatly in size, chromosome count, and transposable element composition, ancestral linkage groups known as Stevens elements remain remarkably conserved across many lineages for over 200 million years. In contrast, groups like leaf beetles have undergone frequent chromosomal fusions and fissions. Additionally, the analysis identified neo-sex chromosomes in roughly 19.5% of the studied species, revealing a much higher frequency than previously estimated and establishing beetles as an ideal model for exploring chromosomal stability and rearrangement.
items.author: Dwayne G. Tally, Charlie Pittman, Ryan R. Bracewell
items.original_title: Species-rich and genomically diverse: Comparative genomics reveals how fusions, fissions, and sex chromosomes have shaped beetle evolution
items.original_summary: by Dwayne G. Tally, Charlie Pittman, Ryan R. Bracewell Chromosome evolution in animals reflects a balance between long-term conservation of ancestral linkage groups and lineage-specific chromosomal rearrangements that reshape genome structure. Beetles (Coleoptera), the most species-rich animal order, exhibit extensive diversity in karyotype, yet the extent to which their chromosomes retain deep ancestral structure remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 190 chromosome-level genome assemblies spanning 39 families and 16 superfamilies to characterize genome diversity, evaluate the conservation of ancestral linkage groups (Stevens elements), identify neo-sex chromosomes, and explore the role of repetitive elements in driving karyotypic change. Our results reveal that beetle genomes are highly diverse, varying substantially in genome size, chromosome number, GC content, and transposable element (TE) composition.

items.title: Antimicrobial Peptide Mutations Impact Sleep and Memory Differently in Drosophila
items.summary: Molecules involved in host defense can act independently as sleep regulators. Researchers examined mutants of various antimicrobial peptides in Drosophila to understand their roles in sleep and behavioral plasticity. AMP mutants generally slept less, exhibited longer sleep latency, and had lowered arousal thresholds. Notably, double mutants for the anti-fungal peptides Metchnikowin and Drosomycin showed the most severe sleep reductions and exaggerated sleep rebounds, yet retained normal learning, memory, and reduced synapse abundance. In contrast, other AMP mutants suffered concurrent memory impairments that could be reversed by enhancing sleep pharmacologically or behaviorally. These findings demonstrate that different antimicrobial peptides uniquely influence sleep modulation and its downstream cognitive outcomes.
items.author: Rahul Kumar, Gokul Madhav, Priyanka Balasubramanian et al.
items.original_title: Mutations in antimicrobial peptides differently affect sleep and plasticity
items.original_summary: by Rahul Kumar, Gokul Madhav, Priyanka Balasubramanian, Ayur Tadimalla, Rhea Lakhiani, Mugdha Joshi, Vibhu Jaggi, Anushna Pal, Imroze Khan, Krishna Melnattur Molecules implicated in host defense can, independent of their roles as immune mediators, regulate sleep. In mammals, cytokines such as Tumor Necrosis Factor α (TNF α) and Interleukin1β (IL1β) promote sleep. In Drosophila , infection stimulates the systemic release of a battery of antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). These fly immune effectors have been understudied as sleep modulators. We obtained mutants in different AMPs and characterized their functions in sleep and plasticity. AMP mutants slept less with a longer sleep latency, and lowered arousal thresholds.

items.title: Small RNA Arp Regulates DNA Uptake and Motility in Acinetobacter baumannii
items.summary: Acinetobacter baumannii is an opportunistic pathogen capable of natural transformation driven by type IV pili, which facilitate horizontal gene transfer and antimicrobial resistance. While transcriptional control of these pili is studied, post-transcriptional mechanisms remained unexplored. Researchers identified a small RNA named Arp that acts as a post-transcriptional repressor of type IV pili functions. Through structural probing and reporter assays, the team demonstrated that Arp binds to the 5 prime end of the pilA mRNA, blocking the Shine-Dalgarno sequence and inhibiting translation. Deleting arp increased DNA uptake and twitching motility, whereas overexpressing Arp depleted pilA mRNA and severely impaired these phenotypes. This discovery highlights a regulatory layer that could potentially be targeted to impede antibiotic resistance spreading.
items.author: Fergal J. Hamrock, Thomas Guest, Mikaela N. Daum et al.
items.original_title: DNA uptake and twitching motility are controlled by small RNA Arp through repression of pilin translation in Acinetobacter baumannii

Westermann, Carsten Kröger Acinetobacter baumannii is a major opportunistic pathogen capable of natural transformation. This process is driven by type IV pili (T4P) facilitating horizontal gene transfer and accelerating the spread of antimicrobial resistance. While the transcriptional regulation of T4P is increasingly understood, post-transcriptional mechanisms controlling pilus assembly remain unexplored. Here, we identify and mechanistically characterise a small RNA, Arp ( Acinetobacter repressor of pilin), as a post-transcriptional repressor of T4P-mediated functions in A.

items.title: Parasite-Derived MicroRNA Suppresses Liver Fibrosis by Targeting Host Pathways
items.summary: Clonorchis sinensis is a food-borne parasite that promotes liver fibrosis in hosts by activating hepatic stellate cells. Researchers investigated the role of extracellular vesicles derived from the parasite and discovered that a specific microRNA, Csi-miR-71a, is significantly enriched in both these vesicles and infected host cells. Using cellular assays and a carbon tetrachloride-induced mouse model, the team demonstrated that overexpressing Csi-miR-71a suppresses fibrotic markers and alleviates liver damage. Bioinformatic and luciferase assays confirmed that Csi-miR-71a directly targets the Scube3 gene, which subsequently inhibits the TGF-beta/Smad and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways. These findings uncover a novel molecular mechanism of parasite-host communication that regulates host fibrosis responses.
items.author: Meiru Hou, Wei Wei, Ruifeng Mao et al.
items.original_title: Csi-miR-71a delivered by Clonorchis sinensis extracellular vesicles suppresses liver fibrosis by targeting Scube3 to inhibit the TGF-β/Smad and PI3K/AKT signaling pathways

Recent studies have revealed that miRNAs carried by C. sinensis -derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) have important roles in host–parasite interactions. However, their specific functions and underlying regulatory mechanisms in liver fibrosis remain largely unclear. In this study, EVs were isolated from C. sinensis excretory-secretory products and characterized by electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking, and western blotting.

items.title: Macrophage Differentiation Affects Chikungunya Virus Susceptibility and Antiviral Responses
items.summary: Researchers investigated how cytokine-driven macrophage differentiation influences human susceptibility to the Chikungunya virus. Using donor-matched primary macrophage cultures, the study found that GM-CSF-differentiated macrophages are highly permissive to Chikungunya and Mayaro virus infections, supporting strong viral replication. In contrast, M-CSF-differentiated macrophages resist viral replication and lack detectable viral protein expression. Despite these differing replication outcomes, infected cells from both differentiation states exhibited a pro-inflammatory, M1-skewed profile. Furthermore, M-CSF-differentiated macrophages produced higher levels of antiviral factors such as IFNα and IP10/CXCL10, indicating a protective antiviral state. Additional experiments using double-stranded RNA analogs suggested that dsRNA sensing is more significant than ssRNA sensing in driving these cellular antiviral responses. These insights demonstrate that macrophage differentiation significantly dictates susceptibility and immune defense during Chikungunya infections.

Noval, Ana Fernandez-Sesma Chikungunya virus is an arthritogenic alphavirus causing debilitating joint pain in infected individuals. Furthermore, M-CSF-differentiated macrophages produced higher levels of antiviral factors such as IFNα and IP10/CXCL10, indicating a protective antiviral state. Additional experiments using double-stranded RNA analogs suggested that dsRNA sensing is more significant than ssRNA sensing in driving these cellular antiviral responses. These insights demonstrate that macrophage differentiation significantly dictates susceptibility and immune defense during Chikungunya infections.

items.title: Andes Virus Outbreak on Cruise Ship Highlights Public Health Gaps
items.summary: In May 2026, a cluster of laboratory-confirmed Andes virus (ANDV) infections occurred among passengers aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, originating in Argentina and traveling through the South Atlantic. The outbreak involved individuals from 23 countries, resulting in at least 13 cases and three deaths. This event marks the first multi-continental range for an ANDV outbreak and reinforces evidence supporting human-to-human transmission. Currently, no approved treatments or vaccines exist for the virus, highlighting the urgent need for therapeutic and prophylactic development. Researchers emphasize that the outbreak reveals both strengths and weaknesses in global public health infrastructure, underscoring the necessity for expanded genomic surveillance, standardized diagnostic protocols, and accelerated clinical translation of antiviral candidates to enhance future pandemic preparedness.

items.title: Host Protein CTCF Enhances AAV Vector Gene Expression via Chromatin Remodeling
items.summary: Adeno-Associated Viruses (AAVs) are widely utilized to deliver therapeutic transgenes through recombinant AAV vectors. However, limitations in understanding viral gene expression have restricted their efficiency. Researchers investigated regulatory elements outside the inverted terminal repeats of wild-type AAVs to improve vector performance. Using in silico analysis, biochemical pulldowns, and high-throughput sequencing, the study identified that the host architectural protein CCCTC-binding Factor associates with the wild-type AAV type 2 genome. Specifically, a CTCF binding element located upstream of the P5 promoter regulates viral gene expression and shapes the local chromatin landscape. By re-engineering recombinant AAV vectors to include this binding element, scientists observed up to a four-fold increase in transduction efficiency and reporter gene expression across various cell types, driven by increased production of nascent RNA transcripts.

items.original_summary: by Clairine I.S. Larsen, Rhiannon R. Abrahams, Rea Guertler, Elliott M. Wilion, Eda Erata, Zachary H. Sykes, Lorelei I. Stoica, Gopishankar Thirumoorthy, Divya Sinha, Richa Rai, Joydeb Majumder, Elizabeth K. Hofer, Eleanor Hart, Eishika Dissanayake, James E. Gern, David M. Gamm, William L. Murphy, Matthew S. Fuller, Kinjal Majumder Adeno-Associated Viruses (AAVs) are powerful platforms for delivering therapeutic transgenes via recombinant AAV (rAAV) vectors. However, a limited understanding of the regulation of AAV gene expression has narrowed the ability to efficiently express therapeutic transgenes from rAAV vectors. Since rAAVs retain only the wtAAV inverted terminal repeats (ITR), we hypothesized that regulatory elements outside the ITR that govern wild-type AAV (wtAAV) gene expression can be used to modify rAAV genomes to enhance vector performance.

items.title: Maternal Mortality Trends in Taiyuan, China Reveal Persistent Urban-Rural Disparities
items.summary: A population-based observational study examined maternal mortality trends and causes in Taiyuan, China, using surveillance data from 2016 through 2024. Analyzing municipal records encompassing 424,392 live births and 33 maternal deaths, researchers calculated an overall maternal mortality ratio of 7.76 per 100,000 live births. While urban areas experienced significant declines in mortality ratios, rural regions did not show the same statistical improvement, pointing to sustained urban-rural disparities. Indirect obstetric causes emerged as the predominant factor among maternal deaths, signaling a shift in the overall spectrum of fatal complications. The findings indicate that while sustained investments have successfully maintained a low overall ratio, targeted strategies focusing on rural health services and equitable life-course care are required to prevent further maternal deaths.
items.author: Fang Wang, Hailan Yang
items.original_title: Trends and causes of maternal mortality in Taiyuan, China, 2016–2024: A population-based observational study
items.original_summary: by Fang Wang, Hailan Yang Background Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016–2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR. Methods We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports . MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests were used for between-group comparisons.

items.title: Sustainable Biopolymer Treatment Enhances Loess Shear Stiffness
items.summary: Geotechnical stability is often threatened by the susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration. Researchers investigated the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainable biopolymer, using resonant column tests. The study analyzed the evolution of maximum shear modulus and reference shear strain under varying confining pressures, water contents, and TFP dosages. Results indicated that TFP treatment significantly bolsters small-strain shear stiffness. Scanning electron microscope observations revealed film-like and filament-like features around soil particles, pointing to microstructural changes. These findings demonstrate the potential of TFP as a bio-based method to improve loess shear stiffness, particularly in high-water-content conditions.
items.author: Shengting Shi, Haokun Tong, Jingxuan Zhou et al.
items.original_title: Water-induced degradation and small-strain dynamic characteristics of tremella fuciformis polysaccharide treated loess
items.original_summary: by Shengting Shi, Haokun Tong, Jingxuan Zhou, Zhanpeng Ji, Xinlei Zhang The susceptibility of loess to water-induced deterioration poses a major threat to geotechnical stability. This study investigates the small-strain dynamic behavior of loess treated with tremella fuciformis polysaccharide (TFP), a sustainable biopolymer, using resonant column tests. The evolution of the maximum shear modulus ( G max ) and reference shear strain ( γ r ) was systematically analyzed under varying applied confining pressures, water contents, and TFP dosages. Results show that for untreated loess, G max follows a power-law growth with confining pressure and linear attenuation with water content.

items.title: Real-Time PCR Assay Improves Rabies Detection in Non-Brain Samples
items.summary: Rabies remains a significant public health issue in endemic areas, where disease control relies on post-mortem confirmation in animal reservoirs. Traditional methods like the direct fluorescent antibody test depend on fresh brain tissue and are vulnerable to specimen degradation, limiting their use in decentralized systems. A recent study evaluated a locally optimized real-time reverse transcription-quantitative PCR assay targeting the nucleoprotein gene in non-brain animal tissues. The assay demonstrated high analytical sensitivity and strong concordance with results from post-mortem brain samples of dogs. Consistent performance in alternative tissues, such as the nasal planum and follicle-sinus complex, supports the use of safer and more accessible specimens for routine animal rabies surveillance.

Although the direct fluorescent antibody test (dFAT) remains the reference standard, its dependence on fresh brain tissue and susceptibility to specimen degradation limits its operational use in decentralized surveillance systems. The present findings demonstrate that the locally optimized RT-qPCR assay targeting the nucleoprotein gene in non-brain tissues exhibits high analytical sensitivity and strong concordance with dFAT results obtained from post-mortem brain specimens of dogs.

items.title: Study Links Higher Physical Activity to Lower Risk of Self-Reported Emphysema
items.summary: Emphysema represents a major public health concern, prompting researchers to investigate the relationship between physical activity intensity and respiratory health. A cross-sectional study utilized data collected from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey between 2007 and 2016. Using multivariable logistic regression models, researchers examined the association between different levels of physical activity and self-reported physician-diagnosed emphysema among older adults, while adjusting for various demographic, lifestyle, and comorbidity factors. The results revealed that higher physical activity levels, specifically 3000 MET-minutes per week or more, correlated with lower odds of self-reported emphysema. A clear dose-response relationship emerged as increasing activity levels matched progressively lower odds of the condition. However, because the study is cross-sectional, causal relationships cannot be established, and prospective studies are required to confirm the findings.

items.original_title: Association between physical activity intensity and self-reported emphysema: A cross-sectional study using NHANES
items.original_summary: by Qiao Wei, Haiyan Song, Li Jiang, Xiuqin Li, Jihua Zhu Background Emphysema is a significant public health issue. Physical activity (PA) has been suggested to be associated with respiratory health; however, the relationship between PA intensity and emphysema remains insufficiently characterized. Methods This cross-sectional study utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2007 to 2016. Emphysema was defined based on self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association between different levels of PA and the odds of self-reported emphysema among older adults, adjusting for demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, and comorbidities.

items.title: Contrast-Only CT Angiography Safely Reduces Radiation in Aortic Pathology Imaging
items.summary: Acute aortic pathologies are traditionally evaluated using multiphase computed tomography angiography protocols that include an unenhanced phase, which contributes to higher patient radiation exposure. A retrospective study examined whether omitting the unenhanced phase is feasible for detecting and characterizing acute aortic conditions while reducing radiation doses. Researchers evaluated 160 patients who underwent multiphase imaging, comparing a contrast-only protocol against a conventional multiphase protocol across predefined aortic segments. The contrast-only approach demonstrated non-inferior diagnostic performance in detecting major aortic pathologies, including aneurysms, dissections, intramural hematomas, and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers. Furthermore, the protocol achieved a radiation dose reduction of approximately 32%. These findings indicate that omitting the unenhanced phase is clinically feasible and reduces cumulative radiation exposure, particularly for serial surveillance imaging.
items.author: Soo Buem Cho, Jieun Byun
items.original_title: Feasibility of omitting the unenhanced phase in CT angiography for acute aortic pathologies
items.original_summary: by Soo Buem Cho, Jieun Byun Objectives To evaluate the feasibility of a contrast-only computed tomography angiography (CTA) protocol versus a conventional multiphase protocol for detecting and characterizing acute aortic pathologies, and reducing radiation dose. Materials & methods This retrospective study included 160 patients who underwent multiphase CTA for evaluating acute aortic syndrome. Two readers independently evaluated 640 predefined aortic segments for the presence of aneurysms, dissections, intramural hematomas (IMH), and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcers (PAU). Non-inferiority was assessed using generalized estimating equations with a prespecified 5% margin. Inter-protocol and inter-reader agreements were calculated using Cohen’s kappa. Radiation dose also was compared.

items.title: Mobile Radiation Shielding System Cuts Scatter Dose in Orthopedic Wards
items.summary: Portable radiography performed in crowded orthopedic wards exposes healthcare workers and nearby patients to scatter radiation. To address this, researchers designed and evaluated a foldable mobile radiation shielding system consisting of two three-panel units with lead sheets, deployed along the lateral sides of a patient's bed. Scatter dose rates were measured across common orthopedic X-ray projections at multiple distances and angular positions using a survey meter and a portable X-ray unit. The two-unit configuration achieved a median scatter dose reduction of 94.1 percent. Reductions remained substantial across various distances and tube voltages, though effectiveness varied by angular position due to open axial ends. The mobile shield effectively lowers estimated annual occupational doses below standard safety limits and received favorable feedback from medical personnel.
items.author: Jongwat Cheewakul, Natee Ina, Suphalak Khamruang Marshall et al.
items.original_title: Mobile radiation shielding device for scatter dose reduction during portable radiography in an orthopedic ward
items.original_summary: by Jongwat Cheewakul, Natee Ina, Suphalak Khamruang Marshall, Sitthichok Chaichulee Portable radiography in orthopedic wards exposes healthcare professionals and adjacent patients to scatter radiation in open, shared clinical environments. In crowded wards, maintaining an optimal distance or clearing the area during exposure is often impractical. This study designed, constructed, and evaluated a foldable mobile radiation shielding system comprising two three-panel units, each with a chromed steel frame (210 × 180 cm) with 0.6-mm nominal lead sheets covered by a vinyl outer layer (66 × 100 cm) per panel, mounted on wheeled castors for bedside deployment. The two units were deployed together, one along each lateral side of the bed.

items.title: Study Examines Qat Chewing Habits and Temporomandibular Disorder Treatments in Yemen
items.summary: A prospective cohort study evaluated the short-term response to conservative management of temporomandibular disorders among habitual qat chewers and non-chewers in conflict-affected Yemen. Conducted at Sana’a University and Al-Kuwait Teaching Hospital between October 2018 and October 2020, the study tracked 148 consecutive patients diagnosed with temporomandibular disorders, including 54 habitual chewers. All participants received standard care involving reassurance, education, self-care advice, and clinical interventions like NSAIDs, diazepam, amitriptyline, or stabilization splints. At the three-month follow-up, improvement was reported in 87.0% of chewers and 93.6% of non-chewers. While conservative management generally benefited most patients, the study's design and limited sample size mean the findings regarding chewers are primarily hypothesis-generating.

items.original_title: Habitual qat chewing and short-term response to conservative management of temporomandibular disorders: A prospective cohort study in conflict-affected Yemen
items.original_summary: by Raji Mansoor Hajeb, Yousif Osman Yousif, Nader Ahmed Al-Aizari, Essam Ahmed Al-Moraissi Qat (Catha edulis), chewed daily by a substantial proportion of Yemeni adults, contains cathinone, an amphetamine-like alkaloid that augments masticatory muscle activity. Observational evidence links the habit to temporomandibular disorders (TMD), yet none has examined how chewers respond once treated. A prospective cohort of 148 consecutive patients diagnosed by Research Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders Axis I examination was followed at Sana’a University and Al-Kuwait Teaching Hospital between October 2018 and October 2020. Fifty-four (36.5%) were habitual qat chewers, defined as three or more sessions weekly. All received reassurance, education and self-care advice, to which the clinician added an NSAID, diazepam, amitriptyline or a stabilization splint as routine care.

items.title: PLOS One Retracts Digital Economy and Green Finance Study Due to Process Manipulation Concerns
items.summary: PLOS One Editors have retracted a 2023 research article investigating the coupling coordination development between the digital economy and green finance across Chinese provinces. The retraction follows concerns regarding potential manipulation of the publication process, which cast doubt on the validity and provenance of the results. Additional issues identified include extensive text similarity and potential paraphrasing involving another study by different authors, as well as multiple retracted references linked to the paper. While some authors disagreed with the retraction, others could not be reached or did not respond.

items.title: PLOS One Issues Expression of Concern Over Decision-Making Study
items.summary: The editors of PLOS One have issued an Expression of Concern regarding a published research article on multiple attribute group decision-making. The action was taken following the discovery of cumulative issues related to the study's references and methodology. Specifically, several articles cited within the paper's bibliography were subsequently retracted after the initial publication. Additionally, independent concerns regarding the reported methodology have been raised publicly on the platform PubPeer across a large number of the study's cited references. Due to these combined factors, readers are strongly advised to interpret the findings and conclusions of the affected study with caution until further investigations or resolutions are provided by the journal or authors.

items.title: Camera-Trap Study Evaluates Small Carnivore Occupancy and Activity in Nepal
items.summary: Researchers conducted camera-trap surveys between January and February 2023 to evaluate the occupancy and temporal activity overlap of five small carnivore species in the Bagmati-Ratu Complex of Nepal's Madhesh Province. Using Markov Chain Monte Carlo simulations, the team analyzed how anthropogenic and environmental variables affect community-level occupancy. The results showed that the jungle cat had the highest detection probability, while the leopard cat had the lowest. Common palm civets showed the highest occupancy, whereas large Indian civets had the lowest. Most small carnivores demonstrated strong nocturnal activity patterns to avoid humans and reduce daytime activity, with the exception of the jungle cat, which displayed some diurnal behavior. These baseline findings help document human-wildlife coexistence and support future conservation planning.

items.title: Study Finds Limited Evidence Linking Training Load to Lower-Limb Pain in Female Footballers
items.summary: Researchers conducted a secondary longitudinal analysis of the SoccerMon dataset, evaluating 50 players from two Norwegian elite women's football teams to see if training load and wellness changes precede lower-limb pain. Initial retrospective standardization suggested an interaction between acute load and soreness, but this attenuated when using only prior available observations. Consequently, the data do not provide stable evidence that short-term load deviations predict next-day pain. Investigators advise treating daily load and wellness metrics as contextual information rather than strict risk thresholds.
