items.original_title: Within-player load-wellness monitoring and lower-limb pain in elite female football: A reproducible secondary analysis of the SoccerMon dataset
items.original_summary: by Yushuo Liu, Haitao Li Routine athlete-monitoring data can test whether within-player changes in training load and wellness precede health problems, but sparse outcomes and incomplete reporting complicate inference. We conducted a reproducible secondary longitudinal analysis of the public SoccerMon dataset, comprising 50 players from two Norwegian elite women’s football teams monitored in 2020–2021. The outcome was onset on day t (the index player-day) of a self-reported lower-limb pain/injury episode after a 7-day episode washout. The primary risk set contained 42 onset-days from 15 players; the complete-case soreness interaction analysis contained 28 onset-days from nine event players. Under retrospective full-period within-player standardization, the focal acute-load x soreness interaction was estimated below 1.0 by Firth logistic regression (odds ratio [OR] 0.63, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.45–0.97), but uncertainty remained substantial.

items.title: Long Sleep Duration Linked to Increased Mortality Risk in Heart Disease Patients
items.summary: A cohort study tracking US adults with heart disease found that sleeping nine hours or more is associated with higher risks of all-cause, heart-related, and non-heart-related mortality compared to sleeping seven to eight hours. Analyzing data from the National Health Interview Survey linked to the National Death Index, researchers observed the lowest predicted mortality risk at six to seven hours of sleep. The findings suggest sleep duration can serve as a simple marker for residual risk in cardiac patients.

We examined associations between sleep duration and mortality among US adults with heart disease. Methods We analyzed data from 3,287 adults with heart disease participating in the 2004 National Health Interview Survey linked to the National Death Index through December 31, 2019. Sleep duration was categorized as ≤6 hours, 7–8 hours, and ≥9 hours.

items.title: Guava-Derived Compounds Show Promising Anticancer Activity in Laboratory Study
items.summary: Researchers isolated two clerodane-type diterpenes, borapetoside F and borapetoside B, from the medicinal plant Psidium guajava to evaluate their anticancer properties. Using both laboratory assays and animal models, the team assessed cytotoxicity against Ehrlich Ascites Carcinoma cells. Results demonstrated that both compounds significantly inhibited cancer cell proliferation and induced apoptosis. Microscopic examination and DNA fragmentation analyses confirmed cell death characteristics, while gene expression tests showed the upregulation of pro-apoptotic markers like p53 and Bax alongside the downregulation of anti-apoptotic genes such as Bcl-2. Molecular docking further validated these findings by showing favorable interactions with apoptosis-related proteins, highlighting the compounds' potential for future drug development.

items.title: Study Evaluates Feasibility of Computerized Adaptive Tests in Physical Therapy
items.summary: A mixed-methods study investigated the feasibility of using Dutch-Flemish PROMIS Computerized Adaptive Tests within primary care physical therapy for patients with musculoskeletal disorders. Integrated into electronic health record systems across 14 practices, the tools were assessed via therapist surveys and semi-structured interviews with both clinicians and patients. Most participants found the adaptive tests easy to use, efficient, and useful for focusing clinical discussions on symptoms and daily functioning. Reported barriers included difficulties with online portals, simultaneous use of older measurement instruments, and challenges with score interpretation. Researchers concluded that the tests are practical and clinically relevant, though future implementation should focus on phasing out legacy instruments and improving score training.

items.title: Study Links Generative AI Competence in Accounting to Ethical Awareness and Career Readiness
items.summary: This study examines Generative AI-enabled accounting information systems competence among accounting and auditing students in Vietnam. Using survey data from 471 university students, the researchers analyzed relationships involving perceived usefulness, digital learning self-efficacy, AI ethics awareness, and career readiness. The baseline structural equation model revealed significant positive associations, with perceived usefulness emerging as a strong antecedent and competence showing a strong link to ethical awareness. Although endogeneity adjustments rendered certain paths non-significant, the findings underscore the importance of discipline-specific AI competence and its connection to ethical understanding and career preparation in accounting education.

The model is anchored in Socio-Technical Systems Theory (STS) and Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), with technology readiness, TAM, self-efficacy, and facilitating-condition logic used as construct-level underpinning mechanisms. Survey data from 471 students at five Vietnamese universities were analyzed using PLS-SEM, complemented by a common latent factor diagnostic and Gaussian copula endogeneity assessment.

items.title: Decade-Long Study Reveals Decline in Diabetic Ketoacidosis Admissions at Norwegian Hospital
items.summary: A retrospective study conducted at a Norwegian university hospital examined diabetic ketoacidosis admissions among adults with type 1 diabetes between August 2012 and August 2032. Reviewing electronic medical records for 178 participants across 306 admissions, researchers discovered that admission frequency decreased by an estimated 6.9% annually. Despite growth in the hospital's catchment area population, this substantial decline suggests overall improvements in diabetes care. However, researchers noted that repeated admissions remained common and were closely tied to psychosocial vulnerability. While in-hospital mortality was low, five-year mortality remained notable, indicating a need for targeted follow-up care following a diabetic ketoacidosis episode.

Results A total of 178 participants with 306 admissions were included. Median [IQR] age at admission was 34 years [22–51]. Median HbA1c was 88 mmol/mol [72–105]. Diabetic ketoacidosis admission frequency decreased by an estimated 6.9% annually (RR 0.931; 95% CI 0.896–0.968; p Conclusions Diabetic ketoacidosis admissions declined substantially over the 10-year study period despite growth in the hospital catchment area population, suggesting that diabetes care has improved.

items.title: Comparing Surgical Techniques for Soft Palate Reduction in Bulldogs with BOAS
items.summary: A prospective clinical study compared the effectiveness of staphylectomy and folded-flap palatoplasty in reducing soft palate length, thickness, and volume in French and English bulldogs diagnosed with brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome. Sixteen dogs underwent either staphylectomy or folded-flap palatoplasty, with computed tomography performed pre-operatively and four weeks post-operatively. Both surgical procedures successfully reduced soft palate length and volume. However, folded-flap palatoplasty additionally resulted in significant soft palate thinning, whereas staphylectomy did not. Consequently, researchers suggest that folded-flap palatoplasty may serve as the preferred treatment for dogs experiencing concurrent soft palate thickening and elongation.

items.title: Investigating Immunogenicity and Shielding of the Foldon Trimerization Domain in Vaccines
items.summary: Protein subunit and mRNA vaccines that fuse viral antigens to the bacteriophage T4 fibritin Foldon trimerization domain are increasingly tested and utilized in humans, but they can trigger off-target antibody responses. Researchers demonstrated that subunit vaccine antigens containing Foldon successfully elicit antibodies against the domain itself. To mitigate this immune response, scientists engineered influenza antigens with N-glycosylation motif mutations at three distinct sites within Foldon to serve as a shield. Although mass spectrometry confirmed partial modification occupancy and some mutant antigens showed reduced antibody binding in vitro, mice immunized with these mutants did not experience a significant reduction in anti-Foldon antibody production. Ultimately, while N-glycosylation offers partial shielding, it does not substantially lower immunogenicity in a naïve setting, indicating that Foldon's immune impact must be carefully considered in clinical vaccine trials.

items.original_title: Immunogenicity of the Foldon trimerization domain and efforts to shield it
items.original_summary: by John V. Dzimianski, Spencer R. Pierce, Sara M. O’Rourke, Ian Kunkel, Kevin Delgado-Cunningham, Aaron D. Gingerich, Jarrod J. Mousa, Ted M. Ross, Rebecca M. DuBois Protein subunit and mRNA vaccines encoding viral glycoprotein antigens fused to the bacteriophage T4 fibritintrimerization domain are increasingly being tested in human clinical trials. AREXVY and ABRYSVO ® , subunit vaccines composed of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F glycoprotein(s) fused to Foldon, are now FDA-approved and regularly administered. However, administration of vaccine antigens containing the Foldon domain has the potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. Here, we demonstrate that protein subunit vaccine antigens RSV F Foldon and influenza hemagglutinin (HA) Foldon elicit antibodies against the Foldon domain.

items.title: Co-Developing an Implementation Model for Physical Activity in Special Educational Needs Schools
items.summary: Integrating a whole school approach to physical activity within special educational needs school settings faces distinct real-world barriers. To address this, researchers used a collaborative co-development approach involving teachers, leadership, parents, education authorities, and community sports professionals across a UK region. Through workshops guided by behavioural and implementation science, participants identified 31 implementation determinants, consisting of 18 facilitators, 12 barriers, and one mixed factor. These insights informed eight implementation strategies, alongside various outcomes and causal mechanisms, which were mapped onto a comprehensive implementation research logic model. This model ultimately supports a guidance document designed to help schools effectively promote physical activity for students with special educational needs.

This study aimed to embed implementation and behavioural science principles to co-develop an implementation research logic model (IRLM) to guide implementation of a WSA to physical activity in SEN settings.

items.title: Evaluating Online Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy for Multiple Sclerosis Patients with Depression
items.summary: Depression is common among individuals with multiple sclerosis, yet the effectiveness and optimal implementation of online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for this group remain understudied. This protocol outlines a type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation study utilizing an embedded mixed methods experimental design. The quantitative component involves a randomized controlled trial of at least 152 participants with multiple sclerosis and mild-to-moderate depression, who will complete an eight-week online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy course. Depression scores will be tracked from baseline through a three-month follow-up. Concurrently, qualitative data will be gathered via semi-structured interviews with participants, health care providers, instructors, and decision-makers. The RE-AIM PRISM tool will evaluate implementation success, providing valuable evidence on intervention feasibility and effectiveness.

items.title: Compact Single-Layer MIMO Antenna Designed for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Communications
items.summary: Researchers have developed a single-layer circularly polarized multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna tailored for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems. The antenna features 16 truncated-corner patches organized in a 4x4 array and is capacitively driven by a probe-fed rectangular patch, maintaining a low profile of about 0.02 wavelengths at its lowest operating frequency. Testing revealed an effective operating bandwidth between 5.16 and 5.68 GHz, isolation levels exceeding 19 dB, and a peak gain of 9.4 dBi. The structure also displays favorable diversity performance metrics, including envelope correlation coefficient, channel capacity loss, and mean effective gain, indicating strong potential for aerial communication networks.

The antenna comprises 16 truncated-corner patches arranged in a 4×4 configuration and capacitively excited by a probe-fed rectangular patch, enabling a low-profile single-layer structure. The final two-port MIMO antenna has a low profile of approximately 0.02λ at the lowest operating frequency. The measured results demonstrate an effective operating bandwidth of 5.16–5.68 GHz, corresponding to 9.6%, with isolation better than 19 dB and a peak gain of 9.4 dBi. In addition, the antenna exhibits good diversity performance in terms of envelope correlation coefficient (ECC), channel capacity loss (CCL), and mean effective gain (MEG).

items.title: Scoping Review Maps Clinical Use of Reticulocyte Hemoglobin Indices in Perinatal Care
items.summary: Detecting iron deficiency early in pregnancy and the postpartum period remains difficult with standard markers, leading researchers to explore reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalents and content. A scoping review following established guidelines mapped clinical and research applications of these indices across studies published between 1990 and 2026. Out of numerous records, 35 studies met the inclusion criteria, showing that reticulocyte hemoglobin indices generally offer good diagnostic accuracy for iron deficiency and correlate well with iron-related biomarkers. However, significant variations in study design, cut-off values, and limited longitudinal data present obstacles to widespread clinical adoption. While promising for tracking responses to iron therapy, further standardized research is needed before routine implementation.
items.author: Miki Ohtsuki, Takuma Ohsuga, Kohei Ida et al.
items.original_title: Clinical applications of reticulocyte hemoglobin indices, including reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent (Ret-He) and reticulocyte hemoglobin content (CHr), among pregnant and postpartum women: A scoping review and evidence map
items.original_summary: by Miki Ohtsuki, Takuma Ohsuga, Kohei Ida, Kaori Tsuyuki, Miho Egawa, Mayumi Toyama, Yoshimitsu Takahashi, Takeo Nakayama, Masaki Mandai Early detection of iron deficiency during pregnancy and the postpartum period, a common condition associated with adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, remains challenging with conventional iron markers. Reticulocyte hemoglobin indices, including reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalent and reticulocyte hemoglobin content, may enable earlier detection of iron-restricted erythropoiesis. We conducted a scoping review to map the clinical and research applications of these indices in pregnant and postpartum women. Following Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance, we searched PubMed, CENTRAL, Web of Science, and Ichushi Web for studies published from January 1, 1990, to May 31, 2025, and performed an updated search on April 21, 2026, for newly added or indexed records.
items.ai_title: Scoping Review Maps Clinical Use of Reticulocyte Hemoglobin Indices in Perinatal Care
items.ai_summary: Detecting iron deficiency early in pregnancy and the postpartum period remains difficult with standard markers, leading researchers to explore reticulocyte hemoglobin equivalents and content. A scoping review following established guidelines mapped clinical and research applications of these indices across studies published between 1990 and 2026. Out of numerous records, 35 studies met the inclusion criteria, showing that reticulocyte hemoglobin indices generally offer good diagnostic accuracy for iron deficiency and correlate well with iron-related biomarkers. However, significant variations in study design, cut-off values, and limited longitudinal data present obstacles to widespread clinical adoption. While promising for tracking responses to iron therapy, further standardized research is needed before routine implementation.

Screen and select eligible studies involving pregnant or postpartum women.
Extract data on diagnostic accuracy, iron-related biomarkers, and therapy responses.
Construct an evidence map to visualize research distribution and identify existing gaps.

items.title: FOXA1 Expression Identified as an Independent Indicator of Poor Progression-Free Survival in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
items.summary: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is known as the most aggressive and poorest-prognosis breast cancer subtype. While FOXA1 acts as a crucial pioneer factor in luminal breast cancer, its precise role in TNBC has remained unclear. A retrospective cohort study investigated 283 women with TNBC to assess FOXA1 expression and its connection to clinical survival outcomes. Using chi-square tests, t-tests, multivariate logistic and Cox regression models, and Kaplan-Meier curves, researchers discovered that FOXA1 positivity strongly correlates with grade II tumors and lower Ki-67 levels. Furthermore, multivariate and treatment-adjusted models demonstrated that FOXA1 expression serves as an independent predictor of poorer progression-free survival, irrespective of the systemic chemotherapy received.
items.author: Angela V. Fonseca-Benitez, David Diaz-Baez, Giulia Capella et al.
items.original_title: FOXA1 expression and survival outcomes in triple-negative breast cancer: A retrospective cohort study
items.original_summary: by Angela V. Fonseca-Benitez, David Diaz-Baez, Giulia Capella, Milena Rondón-Lagos, Isabella Castellano, Nelson Rangel Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains the most aggressive breast cancer subtype, with the poorest prognosis among all forms of breast cancer. FOXA1 is a well-known pioneer factor in luminal breast cancer, however, despite its vital role in this tumor subtype, detailed information about FOXA1 expression and function in TNBC is notably lacking. This gap highlights the importance of exploring whether FOXA1 plays different roles across breast cancer subtypes. Accordingly, the present study aimed to assess the independent prognostic value of FOXA1 expression in a well-characterized cohort of 283 women with TNBC, evaluating its association with progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and distant metastasis, and to determine whether this association is independent of the systemic treatment received.

items.title: New Probabilistic Ranking Strategy Improves Efficiency in Spatio-Temporal Logistics Optimization
items.summary: Spatio-temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems typically involve multiple objectives and varying evaluation times. Traditional multi-objective optimization algorithms often perform high-fidelity evaluations on all objectives for promising solutions, which can lead to computational inefficiency. To resolve this issue, researchers introduced a Surrogate-assisted Evolutionary Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer with Probabilistic Ranking Strategy (SAE-MOGWO-PRS). This new method intelligently selects which population individuals and objective functions undergo high-fidelity testing. Comparative testing against four state-of-the-art surrogate-assisted algorithms across four test problems demonstrated superior performance, confirming the enhanced convergence and diversity generated by the probabilistic ranking strategy.
items.author: Yitong Liu, Tianyu Li, Hong Zhang
items.original_title: SAE-MOGWO-PRS: A probability ranking strategy-based grey wolf optimizer for spatio-temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization
items.original_summary: by Yitong Liu, Tianyu Li, Hong Zhang The spatio-Temporal adaptive collaborative logistics network optimization problems investigated in this paper involve multiple objectives. Most evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithms, however, do not account for the heterogeneity in evaluation times. Instead, they perform high-fidelity evaluations on all objectives for promising population positions identified by their associated surrogate-assisted optimization algorithms in the solution space. While this approach provides complete and error-free solution evaluations, it does not yield the most computationally efficient procedure. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Surrogate-assisted Evolutionary Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer with Probabilistic Ranking Strategy (SAE-MOGWO-PRS). This algorithm is designed to determine which individuals and objective functions within the population should undergo high-fidelity evaluation, thereby enhancing their ability to generate non-dominated solutions with improved convergence and diversity in the Multi-objective Grey Wolf Optimizer.

items.title: Study Examines Plant Life-Form Patterns Across Elevation and Aridity Gradients in Xinjiang Deserts
items.summary: Mountain temperate deserts in northern Xinjiang are influenced jointly by elevational constraints and an east-west aridity gradient driven by westerly circulation. To clarify how these factors affect community structure, researchers surveyed 527 plots across five desert sub-regions during the growing seasons. The study analyzed four structural attributes across shrubs, semi-shrubs, perennial herbs, and annual herbs. Results revealed that community attributes largely followed a unimodal trend along elevations, peaking between 700 and 1100 meters, while overall performance declined from humid western regions toward hyper-arid eastern areas. Different plant life-forms also showed unique adaptive strategies, with shrubs and semi-shrubs maintaining stability under harsh conditions, perennial herbs favoring mid-elevation mesic zones, and annual herbs responding strongly to water variation.
items.author: Cheng Fei, Yi Qiang Dong, Shazhou An
items.original_title: Spatial patterns of plant life-forms along elevation and aridity gradients in temperate deserts of northern Xinjiang, China
items.original_summary: by Cheng Fei, Yi Qiang Dong, Shazhou An Located in the arid hinterland of Central Asia, the mountain temperate deserts in Xinjiang are jointly shaped by elevational geographic constraints and the east-west-oriented drought stress gradient. Nevertheless, the joint coupling relationships between these two gradient factors and community-level vegetation structural attributes across woody and herbaceous plant functional groups remain unclarified quantitatively at present.

items.title: Study Examines Relationships Among Algebraic Classes
items.summary: A new study explores the mathematical relationships connecting the BCI-algebraic class, the GB-algebraic class, and the class of algebras of type (2,0). The findings show that both the BCH-algebraic and GB-algebraic classes are distinct classes that contain the BCI-algebraic class. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that proper BCH-algebras and proper GB-algebras exist, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for each. It also determines that all (2,0)-type algebras form a proper class, with the GB-algebraic class functioning as a proper subclass.
items.author: Miao Liu, Nueraminaimu Maihemuti, Jiayin Peng et al.
items.original_title: GB-algebraic class
items.original_summary: by Miao Liu, Nueraminaimu Maihemuti, Jiayin Peng, Jiangang Tang The purpose of this article is to study the relationships among the BCI-algebraic class, the GB-algebraic class, and the class of algebras of type (2,0). The results indicate that: (1) The BCH-algebraic class and the GB-algebraic class are two distinct algebraic classes, both of which contain the BCI-algebraic class. (2) There exist a proper BCH-algebra and a proper GB-algebra, and necessary and sufficient conditions are provided for BCH-algebras and GB-algebras to be proper BCH-algebras and proper GB-algebras, respectively. (3) All (2,0)-type algebras form a proper class, and the GB-algebraic class is a proper subclass of the class of algebras of type (2,0).

items.title: Machine Learning Identifies Predictors of Severe Asthma Treatment Response
items.summary: Researchers utilized machine learning techniques to identify real-world predictors of patient response to mepolizumab in severe asthma cases. By analyzing thirty features from the REALITI-A dataset across linear regression, random forest, and XGBoost models, the team evaluated exacerbation changes and freedom from exacerbations over one to two years. The analysis revealed that factors such as pre-exposure exacerbation rates, body mass index, baseline activity impairment, questionnaire scores, and geographic residency significantly predict patient response. These insights can help guide clinical decisions and improve therapeutic outcomes for severe asthma sufferers.
items.author: Koyo Usuba, Lingjiao Zhang, Xinyang Liu et al.
items.original_title: Machine learning approaches for the identification of real-world predictors of mepolizumab response
items.original_summary: by Koyo Usuba, Lingjiao Zhang, Xinyang Liu, Tim Tian Yu Han, Natalie Nightingale, Ali Tehrani, Peter Howarth, Rafael Alfonso-Cristancho Background Mepolizumab improves control and reduces clinically significant exacerbations in severe asthma patients. Further research is needed to understand factors influencing patient response. Objective Identify predictors of response to mepolizumab using machine learning techniques. Methods Thirty clinically relevant features from the REALITI-A dataset were analyzed. Response to mepolizumab was defined as change in clinically significant exacerbations at Year 1 post-exposure, being free from clinically significant exacerbations at Year 1, and being free from clinically significant exacerbations at both Year 1 and Year 2 post-exposure for primary, secondary, and exploratory analyses, respectively.

items.title: Fundamental and multihumped multimode solitons in fibers : new families of solitons and their properties
items.summary: We describe multimode solitons made of purely spatial modes using the mathematical formalism developed for the elliptical polarization soliton, and we extend this formalism to solitons made of more than two modes. The main difference with the polarization mode case is the asymmetry in the nonlinear coefficients. Strictly speaking, these objects are solitary waves, whose modal temporal profiles remain invariant owing to the incoherent nonlinear interaction between modes. The approach consists of finding the trajectories of a unit-mass ball in an analogous potential, which correspond to stationary solutions of our set of nonlinear coupled equations. Our analysis reveals a rich variety of multimode solitons with more complex temporal profiles, so-called multihumped multimode solitons.

items.title: Linear-optical generation of approximate higher-component cat states
items.summary: We propose a method for generating higher-component cat states by interfering two $N$-component cat states on a half beam splitter and measuring one output with a photon-number-resolving detector. The Fock components of the conditional output are restricted to a single residue class modulo $2N$. For $N=3$, an ideal six-component cat state can be generated exactly, while for arbitrary $N$, the conditional output approaches an ideal $2N$-component cat state for sufficiently large input amplitudes.

items.title: Optical Representation Neural Networks Enabled by Weakly Supervised Learning
items.summary: Diffractive optical neural networks (ONNs) show remarkable promise in high-speed and energy-efficient optical computing. However, most existing ONNs are optimized to reproduce predefined output intensity distributions, with the desired optical responses explicitly specified before training. Here, we introduce optical representation neural networks (ORNNs) enabled by coarse-grained weak supervision. Using handwritten Devanagari, Arabic, and English characters as three semantic groups, a modified contrastive objective encourages samples from the same script to cluster into similar optical representations. Remarkably, ORNNs improve the classification accuracy by approximately 9% over conventional supervised ONNs, while requiring only around 18% of the training steps to reach a stable test accuracy of 84.5%.
items.author: Bochang Wu, Cheng-Feng Pan, Xuhao Luo et al.

items.title: Symmerty-Engineered Moire Metasurface for Multibeam Control
items.summary: Moiré metasurfaces offer a versatile platform for wavefront engineering through the relative rotation of periodic structures. Despite extensive demonstrations of continuous beam steering, the physical mechanisms governing beam multiplicity remain poorly understood, hindering the systematic design of multibeam radiation states. Here, we establish a predictive framework for engineering beam multiplicity in reflective moiré metasurfaces based on the dominant Fourier coefficients of their constituent patterns. We reveal that the rotational symmetry of these Fourier components in reciprocal space fully determines the symmetry of the resulting moiré unit cell and, consequently, its radiation characteristics. By further incorporating their phase information, both beam multiplicity and steering trajectories can be accurately predicted.
items.author: Yu Chen, Lan Ke, Shaojie Ma et al.

items.title: Exploring NGC 206 Within the Andromeda Galaxy
items.summary: NASA's Astronomy Picture of the Day features NGC 206, a massive stellar association located inside the spiral Andromeda galaxy, situated roughly 2.5 million light-years away. Spanning approximately 4,000 light-years, NGC 206 is characterized by bright, young blue stars that are less than 10 million years old. The region resides within the dusty spiral arms alongside pinkish star-forming areas. This immense stellar grouping is significantly larger than typical open clusters found within the Milky Way disk, matching the scale of giant star-forming nebulae like NGC 604 in the M33 galaxy and the Tarantula Nebula.

items.title: Global Satellite Data Reveals Surprising Recovery of Mangrove Forests
items.summary: After decades of widespread loss, global mangrove forests have experienced an unexpected rebound. Researchers analyzing Landsat satellite imagery from 1984 to 2023 discovered that while nearly 3,000 square kilometers of mangroves were lost between 1984 and 2010, the trend reversed around 2010. Since then, the world has seen an increase of nearly 2,000 square kilometers of mangroves, alongside denser canopies indicating healthier ecosystems. About two-thirds of this expansion stems from natural colonization, while the remaining third is attributed to restoration and regrowth. Regions like Southeast Asia, South America, and Australia led the comeback, driven by stronger legal protections, post-tsunami awareness, sediment deposition, and abandoned agricultural fields being reclaimed by nature. However, experts warn that localized losses continue due to tropical cyclones and human activity, meaning ongoing conservation remains critical.

items.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
items.summary: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction.

items.title: An Inverse-Designed Multilayer Selective Emitter for High-Efficiency Thermophotovoltaics
items.summary: High thermophotovoltaic (TPV) conversion efficiencies have typically relied on photovoltaic cells that reflect sub-bandgap radiation back toward the emitter. Here, we numerically investigate an alternative approach in which spectral selectivity is engineered primarily on the emitter side. We optimize an emitter consisting of 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si coating on tungsten, for coupling to a GaSb cell with an antireflection coating and an Au mirror. A detailed-balance framework incorporates polarization- and angle-resolved emissivity, multiple reflections, and Auger nonradiative recombination. At an emitter temperature of 1500 K, the optimized structure suppresses 97.1% of the incident-blackbody-equivalent sub-bandgap power at the source; a further 1.9% is returned to the emitter by the cell, leaving 1.0% absorbed parasitically in the cell.

items.title: A Unified Device-Level Physical Framework for DRAM Read Disturbance
items.summary: Read disturbance in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) depends on both local device interactions and the electrical conditions imposed by shared array circuitry. Here, we combine DIMM-level characterization results, device measurements, and TCAD simulations to interpret RowHammer, RowPress, and ColumnDisturb within a unified device-level physical framework. We relate charge evolution at the floating storage node to three key mechanisms: trap-assisted electron migration (EM), capacitive coupling (CC), and sense-amplifier-mediated disturb (SAMD). EM is local and trap-sensitive, while CC weakens with wordline separation. SAMD extends disturbance through shared column circuitry by modifying unselected-cell leakage under rail-level bitline biases, a contribution supported by the approximately ninefold higher OFF-state leakage measured relative to retention-like conditions for a high-voltage storage state.

items.title: Distinct Connectivity and Cortical Modulation by Basal Forebrain Subnuclei
items.summary: The basal forebrain regulates multiple behavioral functions via brain-wide projections, though the anatomical reasons for this functional diversity remain poorly understood. Researchers compared two mouse basal forebrain subnuclei, the horizontal diagonal band and the substantial innominata, using tracing methods. The findings indicate that these subnuclei target largely segregated forebrain regions while receiving inputs from partially overlapping subsets of areas. Many individual neurons project to only one subnucleus, pointing to independent recruitment. Combining optogenetics and widefield calcium imaging, the study showed that stimulating prefrontal cortical projections to either subnucleus drives distinct patterns of large-scale cortical activity through a cholinergic mechanism.

items.original_title: Distinct input-output relationships between basal forebrain subnuclei underlie heterogeneous cholinergic modulation of the mouse cortex
items.original_summary: The basal forebrain (BF) supports many behavioral functions via its brain-wide projections, which can be recruited independently and task specifically. However, the anatomical underpinnings for this functional heterogeneity are poorly understood. Here, we compared two mouse BF subnuclei, the horizontal diagonal band (HDB) and the substantial innominata (SI), in terms of their anatomical connectivity and functional recruitment. Using anterograde and retrograde tracing, we show that they target largely segregated forebrain regions, but their input comes from a partially overlapping subset of regions. However, many neurons within each region project to just one of the subnuclei, suggesting they can be recruited independently.

items.title: Neural Circuit Mechanisms for Visual Predator Recognition in Flies
items.summary: Animals survive by visually recognizing objects and responding appropriately through multi-stage processing that transforms visual scenes into object identities and motor actions. In Drosophila, researchers identified a specific neural circuit responsible for recognizing a natural predator, the parasitoid wasp, and triggering defensive behaviors. Flies exhibit defensive actions structured by the wasp's location in their field of view, driven by visual detection of the wasp's elongated antennae. Specific lobula columnar visual projection neurons respond to the wasp's features and relay signals to LC9, which builds a composite representation of the predator. Spatial filtering then maps the location of the wasp onto a descending premotor pathway to coordinate defense.
items.author: Denagamage, S., Foltz, M., Dalstein, V. M. et al.
items.original_title: Visual object recognition in the fly: the internal representation of a predator drives defensive behaviour
items.original_summary: Animals recognize visual objects and respond to them appropriately to survive. This process is thought to unfold in stages: the visual scene is first deconstructed into constituent features, which are then reconstructed into representations of object identity and relayed to motor circuits. Here we define a neural circuit in Drosophila that underlies the visual recognition of a natural predator, the parasitoid wasp, and orchestrates defence. We found that flies exhibit a repertoire of directed defensive actions structured by the wasp's position within the fly's field of view. Expression of these behaviours is driven by visual detection of a conspicuous morphological cue -- the wasp's elongated antennae.

items.title: Anticancer Drug Clofarabine Inhibits Enteric Bacterial Pathogenesis
items.summary: Infections caused by enteropathogenic and enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli lead to severe global diarrhoeal disease and feature attaching and effacing lesions where bacteria generate actin pedestals. To discover new anti-virulence treatments, researchers screened compounds and identified the anticancer nucleotide analogue clofarabine as a potent inhibitor of bacterial growth and pedestal formation. Unlike its role in oncology, clofarabine targets bacterial ATP-dependent processes, impeding gene transcription, protein synthesis, and Type III Secretion System function. However, the bacteria can counteract this by cleaving clofarabine to resume growth. Additionally, clofarabine suppresses protein translation in human monocytes, revealing shared vulnerabilities to purine antimetabolites in both hosts and pathogens.
items.author: Deans, N. D., Naylor, K. L., Srour, S. et al.
items.original_title: Clofarabine enforces dual host-pathogen translational arrest and disarms enteric bacterial virulence
items.original_summary: Enteropathogenic and enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EPEC/EHEC) cause severe global diarrhoeal disease, exacerbated by rising antimicrobial resistance. Pathogenesis relies on attaching and effacing lesions, where bacteria generate actin pedestals to adhere, replicate, and destroy intestinal microvilli. To identify novel anti-virulence candidates targeting this process, we conducted a high-throughput phenotypic screen quantifying pedestal formation via high-content fluorescence microscopy. We identified the anticancer nucleotide analogue clofarabine as a potent inhibitor of EPEC growth and pathogenesis. Distinct from its oncology mechanism - inducing DNA chain termination and apoptosis - clofarabine competes with bacterial ATP-dependent processes to impede gene transcription, protein synthesis, and Type III Secretion System (T3SS) function.

items.title: Deep Learning Approach Enhances Prediction of Short Linear Motifs
items.summary: Short linear motifs are small interaction modules situated within intrinsically disordered protein regions that govern critical biological processes. Traditional identification methods often suffer from high rates of false positives because of limited motif definitions. To overcome this, researchers developed SLiMMine, a deep learning-based tool utilizing protein embeddings trained on refined annotations of known motif classes. SLiMMine improves functional motif identification, eliminates approximately 80% of false positives from standard pattern matching, and uncovers novel motifs based solely on sequence features. Furthermore, narrowing interactor-domain definitions helps link predicted motifs more precisely to known protein interactions.
items.author: Pancsa, R., Ficho, E., Kalman, Z. E. et al.
items.original_title: Reliable prediction of short linear motifs in the human proteome
items.original_summary: Short linear motifs (SLiMs) are small interaction modules within intrinsically disordered regions of proteins that interact with specific domains, and thereby regulate diverse biological processes. The limited information in SLiM definitions leads to frequent false positive hits in computational and experimental SLiM identification methods. Here, we refined the annotations of known motif classes to create a high-quality training dataset, and developed SLiMMine, a deep learning-based method to identify SLiMs in the human proteome. Relying on protein embeddings, SLiMMine outperforms similar approaches in identifying functional SLiMs, while eliminating ~80% of the pattern matching-based hits as false-positives. Furthermore, it can uncover novel SLiMs that do not fit known motif classes purely based on sequence features.

items.title: Bacterial Co-culture Enables Efficient Paracetamol and Toxic Metabolite Removal
items.summary: Pharmaceutical biodegradation often leaves behind toxic metabolites that threaten aquatic environments. To tackle this, researchers studied a two-species microbial co-culture combining the paracetamol-degrading bacterium Delftia P1 with Microbacterium lacus, which contains a homolog of the sadB monooxygenase gene capable of transforming the dead-end metabolite 4-aminophenol. The relative cell density between the two strains heavily influenced removal efficiency. The optimal ratio achieved complete removal of both paracetamol and 4-aminophenol in wastewater and laboratory settings without accumulating harmful byproducts, highlighting the value of complementary metabolic capabilities in co-cultures.
items.author: Demaria, F., Schaffter, M., Zimmardi, C. et al.
items.original_title: Coupling Complementary Pathways in a Bacterial Co-culture Enables 4-Aminophenol Removal during Paracetamol Degradation
items.original_summary: Pharmaceutical biodegradation can generate potentially toxic metabolites that persist after the parent compound has been removed, posing additional risks to aquatic environments. Microbial co-cultures offer a promising strategy to address this challenge by combining complementary metabolic capabilities to remove both pharmaceuticals and their harmful transformation products by coupling complementary degradation pathways. Here, we investigated a two-species co-culture combining the paracetamol-degrading bacterium Delftia P1 with Microbacterium lacus to enable subsequent 4-AP removal. While Delftia P1 efficiently degraded paracetamol, it accumulated 4-AP as a dead-end metabolite. M. lacus was selected to complement this metabolic limitation because its genome contains a homolog of sadB, a monooxygenase gene involved in 4-AP transformation.

items.title: Chronic Airway Adaptation Alters Pseudomonas aeruginosa Antibiotic Responses
items.summary: Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections often persist despite intensive antibiotic therapy guided by standard susceptibility testing. Researchers investigated how longitudinal clinical isolates from cystic fibrosis patients respond to antibiotics under standard laboratory conditions compared to an airway epithelial infection model that mimics the natural infection environment. While standard tests mostly reproduced major resistance phenotypes, discordance emerged among isolates recovered after prolonged airway persistence. Several isolates classified as susceptible in standard tests showed substantial survival in the airway model, driven by mutations tied to classical resistance and chronic adaptation. These findings demonstrate that conventional laboratory assays do not fully capture bacterial responses shaped by long-term infection environments.
items.author: Laborda, P., Cebrian-Sastre, E., La Rosa, R. et al.
items.original_title: Infection-dependent antibiotic response phenotypes emerge during chronic airway adaptation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
items.original_summary: Objectives Chronic Pseudomonas aeruginosa airway infections can persist for years despite intensive antibiotic therapy guided by standard antimicrobial susceptibility testing. While this technique captures the emergence of resistance, it does not reproduce many features of the infection environment, where adaptation acquired during chronic infection may alter bacterial responses to antibiotics in ways that are not fully reflected by conventional susceptibility testing. Here we investigated antibiotic responses of longitudinal clinical isolates under standard laboratory conditions and in an airway epithelial infection model. Methods Six longitudinal pairs of P. aeruginosa isolates from people with cystic fibrosis were analysed. Changes in bacterial growth following exposure to tobramycin, ceftazidime and ciprofloxacin were quantified under standard laboratory conditions and compared with changes in bacterial burden after treatment measured in differentiated airway epithelial cultures maintained under air-liquid interface (ALI) conditions that reproduce key features of the airway infection environment.

items.title: Diatoms Use Phosphoproteome Remodeling to Adapt to Fluctuating Phosphorus
items.summary: Diatoms play a major role in marine phosphorus cycling and rapidly adapt to fluctuating nutrient supplies by storing excess phosphorus as polyphosphate. To understand how these organisms regulate such adaptations, researchers examined system-wide changes in the Phaeodactylum tricornutum phosphoproteome during phosphorus deficiency and resupply. The study revealed widespread dephosphorylation across 44 percent of phosphosites, highlighting a novel phosphorus-sparing strategy. Following nutrient resupply, the cells quickly reprogrammed their phosphoproteome within minutes. This rapid response involves intracellular phosphorus trafficking and calcium-dependent protein kinase signaling. Overall, the findings show that the phosphoproteome acts as a flexible intracellular reservoir, allowing diatoms to successfully manage changing environmental phosphorus levels.
items.author: Meeda, Y., Touhami, Y., Wharam, S. et al.
items.original_title: Flexible phosphorus allocation to the phosphoproteome underpins diatom regulatory adaptations to fluctuating phosphate supply
items.original_summary: Diatoms are major drivers of marine phosphorus (P) cycling and are highly adapted to cope with variable P supply. P-starved diatoms can sense increases in P availability within seconds, accumulating this limiting resource through luxury polyphosphate (polyP) storage. Yet, how diatoms coordinate such responses is unknown. Protein phosphorylation is a core mechanism for environmental signal transduction in eukaryotes, but how cells balance investment in protein phosphorylation against competing physiological demands during P limitation is poorly understood. Here, we characterise system-wide remodelling of the Phaeodactylum tricornutum phosphoproteome in response to P deficiency and subsequent resupply. We identify widespread proteome dephosphorylation across 44% of phosphosites, revealing a previously unrecognised P-sparing strategy in marine phytoplankton.

items.title: Engineered eTasR Platform Improves PAMless Genome Editing
items.summary: Researchers have developed a highly active genome editing variant called eTasR by using structure-guided rational design on the compact TIGR-Tas system and fusing it with the TREX2 exonuclease. The new tool significantly increases mammalian editing efficiency and enables effective in vivo delivery.
items.author: Zhang, X., Zhu, Q., Zhang, Z. et al.
items.original_title: Engineered Miniature ParTasR Enables Efficient PAMless Genome Editing
items.original_summary: TIGR-Tas system holds great promise for genome-engineering applications owing to its compact size and PAMless targeting capability. However, its low editing efficiency in mammalian cells severely limits its broader utility. Here, we engineered a highly active variant of ParTasR, termed eTasR, through structure-guided rational design of ParTasR combined with co-expression of the 3'[->]5' exonuclease TREX2. eTasR increased editing efficiency in mammalian cells from the original average 4.29% to 48.94% with an average 26.52-fold improvement, substantially outperforming the popular PAM-free version of nuclease-SpRY. Moreover, a single AAV delivery of eTasR in vivo effectively alleviates the disease phenotype of hereditary tyrosinemia type I (HT1) mouse model through targeted Hpd editing.

items.title: Positive Selection Targets Exposed Regions on Human Proteins
items.summary: Positive selection drives the evolution of protein function by favoring amino acid substitutions that enhance fitness, yet the precise structural locations of these changes have remained debated. To clarify these patterns, researchers analyzed curated collections of positively selected genes and residues. The results show that positively selected residues in human proteins are significantly enriched in secreted and cell membrane proteins, preferentially locating on solvent-exposed surfaces, coil structures, and interaction interfaces rather than within internal domains or disordered regions. Furthermore, these residues frequently cluster near host-pathogen interaction interfaces, pointing to pathogen neutralization as a primary driver of human protein adaptation. These residues also show connections to human variation data and clinical drug targets, providing new insights into the structural basis of adaptive evolution.
items.author: Dobson, L., Schad, E., Ficho, E. et al.
items.original_title: Positive selection tends to act on exposed extracellular regions and delineate interaction modules targeted by pathogens
items.original_summary: Background: Positive selection shapes protein function by favoring amino acid substitutions that increase fitness. Although numerous studies have identified positively selected genes (PSGs), the structural principles underlying residue-level positive selection remain incompletely understood and previous studies have produced conflicting conclusions, particularly regarding the preferential location of positively selected residues (PSRs) within intrinsically disordered regions. In order to resolve these issues and to better understand the driving forces underlying positive selection in human proteins, we performed a comprehensive analysis on a manually curated, high quality collection of PSGs and PSRs as well as on a large-scale PSR dataset restricted to proteins with experimental structures.

items.title: Hypoxia and Reoxygenation Drive Intestinal Repair in Drosophila
items.summary: Fluctuating oxygen levels challenge intestinal tissues, but the mechanisms driving damage and repair remain poorly understood. Using the adult Drosophila intestine, researchers demonstrated that hypoxia and reoxygenation trigger distinct phases of epithelial repair. During hypoxia, separate enterocyte populations activate an AMPK-p53-dependent pathway that primes cells for apoptosis and an independent cytokine response that stimulates stem cell signaling. However, neither cell death nor stem cell proliferation occurs until oxygen returns. Upon reoxygenation, enterocyte loss and stem cell division happen simultaneously to restore intestinal length. The findings reveal how the intestinal epithelium coordinates space and time during oxygen fluctuations.
items.author: Bodkhe, P., Ding, K., Grewal, S. S.
items.original_title: Parallel enterocyte caspase and cytokine responses couple hypoxia to reoxygenation-dependent intestinal regeneration in Drosophila
items.original_summary: Intestinal oxygen availability fluctuates during both normal physiology and disease, yet how the intestinal epithelium adapts to these changing environments remains poorly understood. Using the adult Drosophila intestine, we show that hypoxia and reoxygenation drive distinct phases of an epithelial damage and repair response. Hypoxia induces two parallel responses in largely separate enterocyte populations: an AMPK-p53-dependent response that primes enterocytes for apoptosis, and an independent Upd cytokine response that activates JAK-STAT signaling in intestinal stem cells (ISCs). Despite activation of both pathways during hypoxia, neither apoptosis nor ISC proliferation occurs until oxygen is restored. Upon reoxygenation, enterocyte loss and ISC proliferation proceed together and both are required for recovery of intestinal length.

items.title: Mechanical Stress Influences Inner-Ear Hair Cell Regeneration
items.summary: The regeneration capacity of inner-ear sensory hair cells (HCs) drops sharply during early postnatal development in mice, limiting recovery from hearing and balance disorders. Traditionally, HC regeneration is viewed through a classical lateral inhibition model involving neighboring supporting cells. Researchers combined live imaging with single-HC ablation in mouse vestibular explants to explore this decline. They discovered that age-dependent shifts in mechanical stress alter standard differentiation patterns. A mathematical model incorporating local mechanical regulation alongside Notch signaling successfully replicates these observations across different ages. These findings point to mechanical stress as a critical regulator of HC development and regeneration, offering a potential new target for therapeutic strategies.
items.author: Inbar Kasirer, S., Shraga, M., Dullweber, T. et al.
items.original_title: Age-dependent mechanical stress underlies unexpected vestibular differentiation and regeneration patterns
items.original_summary: Loss of inner-ear sensory hair cells (HCs) is a major cause of hearing and balance disorders. Promoting HC regeneration offers a potential therapeutic strategy, but regenerative capacity is limited in adult mammals and declines rapidly during early postnatal development in mice. HCs can regenerate through trans-differentiation of neighboring supporting cells in a process controlled by Notch mediated lateral inhibition. However, the factors underlying the decrease in regeneration capacity are poorly understood. Here, we combine live imaging with single-HC ablation in mouse vestibular explants to track the dynamics of HC development and regeneration. We reveal unexpected age-dependent deviations from the classical lateral inhibition model, in which new HCs differentiate adjacent to existing HCs.

items.title: New Tool Uses Remote Sensing to Assess Ecosystem Impacts of Beaver Dams
items.summary: Beavers strongly influence riparian ecosystems by altering water levels and vegetation, yet ecologists often lack accessible tools to analyze remote sensing data for these changes. To bridge this gap, researchers developed a Google Earth Engine-backed Streamlit application. This graphical user interface allows users to upload locations of active dams or installed beaver dam analogs. The app automatically generates comparable dam-absent reference locations and outputs numerical data and plots. These visuals display temporal shifts in water, vegetation, temperature, and evapotranspiration metrics. Supported by open datasets from 2017 onward, the tool is available via a static cloud URL or locally through GitHub, enabling broader conservation use without requiring specialized software expertise.
items.author: Tyree, Q., Etheredge, J., Kong, Z. et al.
items.original_title: Beaver Impacts Tool: A Graphical User Interface for Analyzing Ecosystem Impacts of Beaver Dams Using Remote Sensing Data
items.original_summary: Beavers are being increasingly recognized as driving factors in diverse and resilient riparian ecosystems. Many of their impacts, including changes to water levels and vegetation, can be studied through remote sensing. However, ecologists and conservationists may lack the tools to easily analyze remote sensing data for these purposes. We offer here a Google Earth Engine-backed Streamlit app that allows users to easily upload locations of observed dams or installed beaver dam analogs for analysis. Via a graphical user interface, users then generate a set of dam-absent locations for comparison and receive plots and numerical data indicating how indices associated with vegetation, water, temperature, and evapotranspiration change over time for dam-present and dam-absent locations.

items.title: Using eDNA Time Series to Map Prey Landscapes for Endangered Beluga Whales
items.summary: Tracking foraging habits and prey dynamics is essential for protecting endangered species like the Cook Inlet beluga whale. Researchers utilized quantitative environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding alongside visual observations to study seasonally changing prey fields across two estuarine systems. By combining coho quantitative PCR assays with MiFish 12S metabarcoding, the team estimated fish abundances and tracked predator-prey co-occurrence. Weekly time series data successfully captured shifts in predator presence and prey availability, revealing beluga whales co-occurring with spikes in coho DNA near the Twentymile River. Conversely, monthly sampling on the Kenai River showed a mismatch with spring eulachon runs. The findings highlight the effectiveness of pairing shore-based eDNA sampling with visual surveys to monitor dynamic habitats.
items.author: Gold, Z., Shelton, A., Tobin, D. D. B. et al.
items.original_title: Characterizing the Prey Landscape of Endangered Cook Inlet Beluga Whales Using an eDNA Time Series
items.original_summary: Our ability to understand habitat utilization in the context of foraging, prey dynamics, and anthropogenic disturbance is critical for the effective management of protected species globally. Here we examine the occurrence of the endangered Cook Inlet beluga whale (Delphinapterus leucas) in the context of seasonally changing prey fields by leveraging quantitative eDNA metabarcoding approaches. Specifically, eDNA approaches were used to generate estimates of fish abundances using a joint modeling framework that derives total DNA concentration from a coho (Oncorhynchus kisutch) qPCR assay and bias-corrected proportional abundance of multiple salmonid species using MiFish 12S metabarcoding of environmental and mock community samples.
items.ai_title: Using eDNA Time Series to Map Prey Landscapes for Endangered Beluga Whales
items.ai_summary: Tracking foraging habits and prey dynamics is essential for protecting endangered species like the Cook Inlet beluga whale. Researchers utilized quantitative environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding alongside visual observations to study seasonally changing prey fields across two estuarine systems. By combining coho quantitative PCR assays with MiFish 12S metabarcoding, the team estimated fish abundances and tracked predator-prey co-occurrence. Weekly time series data successfully captured shifts in predator presence and prey availability, revealing beluga whales co-occurring with spikes in coho DNA near the Twentymile River. Conversely, monthly sampling on the Kenai River showed a mismatch with spring eulachon runs. The findings highlight the effectiveness of pairing shore-based eDNA sampling with visual surveys to monitor dynamic habitats.
flow: Collect environmental DNA and visual observation data using weekly or monthly time series sampling.
Generate total DNA concentration estimates using a coho qPCR assay.
Determine bias-corrected proportional abundance of multiple salmonid species using MiFish 12S metabarcoding.
Analyze the temporal overlap between predator occurrence and specific prey DNA concentrations.

items.title: Drought-Resilient Trees Provide Critical Refuge for Desert Parasitoid Wasps
items.summary: Increasing aridity driven by climate change threatens dryland parasitoid wasps by limiting environmental resources. Native, drought-tolerant plants like Ziziphus spina-christi could help sustain these beneficial insect populations by offering floral resources and habitats. Over a two-year study across four sites spanning a rainfall gradient, researchers compared parasitoid communities on Z. spina-christi trees versus surrounding vegetation. Parasitoid abundance was consistently higher on the trees, particularly during harsh summer conditions, while diversity varied by site and season. Additionally, sugar-feeding frequency increased when flowers were more abundant. These insights indicate that Z. spina-christi acts as a vital nutritional resource and ecological refuge, supporting conservation efforts in arid ecosystems.
items.author: Saabna, N., Keasar, T.
items.original_title: Manuscript, raw data, and R code: Ziziphus spina-christi as a Refuge and Resource for Parasitoids in Arid Ecosystems
items.original_summary: 1. Climate change is increasing aridity in dryland ecosystems, potentially threatening parasitoid wasps through reduced resource availability and environmental stress. Native drought-adapted plants may help sustain parasitoid communities by providing floral resources and refuge habitats. The tree Ziziphus spina-christi (L.) tolerates drought and heat stress, making it a promising candidate species for desert afforestation and dryland restoration. Its abundant flowering attracts a wide range of insects, supports honey production, and provides valuable forage resources for pollinators. 2. In this two-year study, we investigated the role of Ziziphus spina-christi in supporting parasitoid wasps across four sites that span a 200-600 mm annual rainfall gradient.

items.title: AI-Powered Image Analysis Streamlines Insect Biodiversity Monitoring
items.summary: Monitoring insect biodiversity is vital for ecological assessments and sustainable landscape management, but traditional methods are hindered by the need for extensive taxonomic expertise. Researchers developed an AI-supported index that estimates flying insect biodiversity using the visual features of insect bodies. Flying insects were captured using yellow sticky traps across diverse Mediterranean habitats and seasons in Israel. The traps were scanned at high resolution, and a machine learning model automatically detected and delineated the insects to extract visual traits such as body size, color, and shape. Biodiversity was then calculated from distances among feature vectors. The AI-derived index correlated strongly with expert taxonomic identification, showing that morphological image variation serves as an effective biodiversity proxy and offering a rapid, cost-effective monitoring solution.
items.author: Cabra-Leykin, L., Keasar, T., Keasar, C.
items.original_title: Rapid estimation of insect biodiversity using AI assisted image analysis:a cost-effective tool for monitoring and ecological assessmen
items.original_summary: Protection of natural areas and environmentally friendly management of anthropogenic landscapes require reliable tools for monitoring and comparing biodiversity. Bioindicator-based approaches can support large-scale ecological assessment, but insect monitoring remains constrained by the taxonomic expertise required for species identification. Here, we propose an AI-supported index for estimating the biodiversity of flying insects, based on the diversity of visual features of insect bodies. Flying insects were captured using yellow sticky traps across agricultural and natural habitats, seasons, crops, and sites in Israel's Mediterranean region. Traps were scanned at high resolution and uploaded to a dedicated image database. A machine learning model was used to detect and delineate insects, after which engineered visual features representing body size, color, and shape were extracted.
