items.title: Kelp Species Adjust Reproduction Strategy Based on Environmental Cues
items.summary: Many organisms alternate between distinct life stages and can switch between sexual and asexual reproduction, though the mechanisms coordinating these choices remain unclear. Researchers explored the molecular basis of life stage identity and reproductive modes in the kelp Laminaria pallida by combining gene expression analyses, developmental experiments, and population-level approaches. The study shows that asexual reproduction in this kelp is linked to endoreduplication and reduced fitness, and while it is preserved in natural populations, it is rarely expressed. Crucially, the presence of potential mating partners actively reduces asexual development, demonstrating that the kelp adjusts its reproductive mode depending on available opportunities. This conditional strategy allows asexual reproduction to serve as a backup when mates are scarce, while preserving the long-term benefits of sexual reproduction when partners are accessible.
items.author: Daniel Liesner, Rémy Luthringer, Lineekela Kandjengo et al.
items.original_title: Life-cycle plasticity enables conditional asexual reproduction in a kelp
items.original_summary: by Daniel Liesner, Rémy Luthringer, Lineekela Kandjengo, John J. Bolton, Mark D. Rothman, Myriam Valero, Fabian B. Haas, Susana M. Coelho Many organisms alternate between distinct life stages and can reproduce either sexually or asexually, yet the mechanisms coordinating these developmental and reproductive transitions remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the molecular basis of life stage identity and reproductive mode in the kelp Laminaria pallida , a multicellular organism with a complex life cycle. By combining gene expression analyses with developmental experiments and natural population-level approaches, we characterize the transcriptional signatures associated with developmental state transitions in both sexual and asexual contexts.

items.ai_summary: Many organisms alternate between distinct life stages and can switch between sexual and asexual reproduction, though the mechanisms coordinating these choices remain unclear. Researchers explored the molecular basis of life stage identity and reproductive modes in the kelp Laminaria pallida by combining gene expression analyses, developmental experiments, and population-level approaches. The study shows that asexual reproduction in this kelp is linked to endoreduplication and reduced fitness, and while it is preserved in natural populations, it is rarely expressed. Crucially, the presence of potential mating partners actively reduces asexual development, demonstrating that the kelp adjusts its reproductive mode depending on available opportunities. This conditional strategy allows asexual reproduction to serve as a backup when mates are scarce, while preserving the long-term benefits of sexual reproduction when partners are accessible.

items.title: Decomposing Bacterial Pangenomes into Additive Gene Modules
items.summary: Bacterial pangenomes combine vertically inherited chromosomes with horizontally acquired mobile elements, creating complex architectures that traditional phylogenetic methods struggle to resolve. To address this, researchers utilized non-negative matrix factorization to decompose the accessory pangenome of 1,398 Staphylococcus aureus genomes into 24 additive gene modules called phylons. This framework cleanly separates lineage-defining components from mobile genetic elements with high accuracy and precision. The additive representation successfully recovered known biological structures and uncovered new insights, such as horizontal transfer events linking pandemic lineages. The approach also accurately discriminated host origins and antibiotic resistance profiles without retraining, while external validations on independent assemblies demonstrated robust performance. This organism-agnostic framework offers a scalable way to dissect the modular architecture of bacterial pangenomes.
items.author: Siddharth M. Chauhan, Bernhard O. Palsson, Jonathan M. Monk
items.original_title: Decomposition of the S. aureus pangenome reveals evolving genetic repertoire associated with adaptation and virulence
items.original_summary: by Siddharth M. Chauhan, Bernhard O. Palsson, Jonathan M. Monk Bacterial pangenomes are mosaics of vertically inherited chromosomal backgrounds and horizontally acquired mobile elements, yet existing analysis methods either assign each genome to a single phylogenetic group or treat genes independently, failing to resolve this composite architecture. Here, we show that non-negative matrix factorization decomposes the accessory pangenome of 1,398 curated Staphylococcus aureus genomes into 24 additive gene modules (“phylons”) that cleanly separate lineage-defining components from mobile genetic element repertoires, achieving 90% reconstruction accuracy with 96% precision. The additive representation, where each genome equals a primary lineage phylon plus one or more mobilome phylons, recovers known biology (clonal complex structure, immune evasion cluster types) and reveals previously uncharacterized structure, including multiple horizontal transfer events linking the CC30 and hybrid ST239 pandemic lineages.

items.title: Updated GapMind Tool Enhances Prokaryotic Amino Acid Pathway Analysis
items.summary: Researchers have updated the automated web-based tool GapMind to better annotate amino acid biosynthesis pathways in archaeal and bacterial genomes. By combining comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics, the team identified candidate genes to fill previously unknown metabolic gaps and verified the activity of ten new enzymes using cross-species complementation assays. Notable additions include a new route to glycine via glyoxylate, alternative enzymes for phosphoserine phosphatase, N-succinyl-L,L-diaminopimelate desuccinylase, N-acetylornithine deacetylase, and a putative bifunctional MetB/MetC. Following these updates, the average number of unexplained missing steps in amino acid biosynthesis across 208 high-quality prokaryotic genomes dropped significantly from 1.4 to 0.7 per genome. The remaining gaps are predominantly tied to the gain or loss of phosphate groups.

items.original_title: Novel enzymes for amino acid biosynthesis in diverse bacteria and archaea: GapMind 2026

We used GapMind to identify gaps in biosynthetic pathways and systematically used comparative genomics and high-throughput genetics to identify candidate genes to fill these gaps. items.title: Fish Virus Protein Exploits FTR86 to Inhibit Innate Immunity
items.summary: Researchers explored the role of the fish-specific TRIM subfamily protein EcFTR86 during Singapore grouper iridovirus infection. They found that EcFTR86 localizes to lysosomes and is heavily upregulated in grouper spleen cells during viral infection. Overexpressing EcFTR86 promoted viral replication, while knocking it down reduced infection, confirming its role as a pro-viral factor. Mechanistically, EcFTR86 negatively regulated type I interferon signaling by triggering the autophagic degradation of the STING-TBK1 axis, a process mediated by the cargo receptor Tollip. Furthermore, the viral protein VP018 interacted with EcFTR86 to accelerate this targeted degradation and suppress the host interferon response.
items.author: Linyong Zhi, Mengdi Yuan, Guimei Zhang et al.
items.original_title: Singapore grouper iridovirus VP018 exploits FTR86 to promote viral replication through Tollip-mediated degradation of the STING-TBK1 axis
items.original_summary: by Linyong Zhi, Mengdi Yuan, Guimei Zhang, Dongmiao Xiao, Xinyi Ren, Qiwei Qin, Xiaohong Huang, Youhua Huang Members of the tripartite motif (TRIM) family have been demonstrated to exert crucial roles in immune defense against pathogens. However, functions of the fish-specific TRIM subfamily (FTR), which lacks mammalian orthologues, remains poorly understood. In the current study, we investigated the potential roles of grouper FTR86 (EcFTR86) on innate immune response and its actions during fish virus infection. EcFTR86 was found to localize to lysosomes, and its transcription was significantly up-regulated in grouper spleen cells upon Singapore grouper iridovirus (SGIV) infection. Notably, the exogenous expression of EcFTR86 markedly enhanced SGIV replication, whereas knockdown of endogenous EcFTR86 significantly attenuated viral infection, demonstrating that EcFTR86 functions as a pro-viral factor against virus infection.

items.title: Study Links Social Media Integration to PTSD Symptoms Among South African Students
items.summary: A cross-sectional study of 491 South African university students investigated how social media integration relates to PTSD-consistent symptomatology, with a focus on problem-solving appraisals and perceived social support. The findings indicate that higher social media integration correlates positively with increased PTSD symptom severity across multiple clusters. Conversely, effective problem-solving appraisals and perceived social support appear to act as protective factors. Problem-solving partially mediated the link between social media use and symptom severity, while social support moderated several specific symptom dimensions. Researchers suggest that interventions bolstering coping strategies and social networks could help mitigate trauma-related distress among frequent social media users.
items.author: Tyrone B. Pretorius, Anita Padmanabhanunni
items.original_title: Problem-solving and social support appraisals in the cross-sectional association between social media integration and PCL-5 symptom severity
items.original_summary: by Tyrone B. Pretorius, Anita Padmanabhanunni The present study investigated the relationship between social media integration and PTSD-consistent symptomatology among South African university students, with a specific focus on the roles of problem-solving appraisal and perceived social support. Participants were 491 students who completed the Social Media Use Integration Scale, the Problem-Solving Inventory-20, the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support, and the Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, correlations, and mediation and moderation analyses with PROCESS. Social media integration was positively associated with overall PTSD-consistent symptomatology and all symptom clusters measured by the PCL-5.

items.title: Study Examines Myeloid Transcriptional Programs and Ex Vivo Sensitivity in ARDS
items.summary: Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is biologically diverse, prompting researchers to investigate how myeloid transcriptional programs relate across blood and lung compartments. The study evaluated whether a pre-specified neutrophil degranulation program and a perturbation-response module provide convergent evidence across public cohorts. Utilizing patient samples, purified neutrophil comparisons, and ex vivo treatments, researchers assessed gene coexpression networks and cellular responses. Results showed that the neutrophil degranulation program increased consistently in ARDS patients, rose after granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor exposure, and decreased following broad PI3K inhibition. However, the findings support an ARDS-associated myeloid effector program rather than establishing a prognostic signature, a causal outcome mechanism, or targeted therapeutic efficacy.
items.author: Wei Wei, Jing Liu, Ying Zhou et al.
items.original_title: Paired neutrophil association and ex vivo perturbation sensitivity define a bounded myeloid activation model in ARDS
items.original_summary: by Wei Wei, Jing Liu, Ying Zhou, Rui Zhao, LinGang Zhang Background Acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) is biologically heterogeneous, but how myeloid transcriptional programmes relate across blood and lung compartments remains uncertain. We examined whether a pre-specified neutrophil effector/degranulation programme and a separately derived perturbation-response module provide convergent, boundary-aware evidence across public cohorts. Methods Patient-level analyses descriptively localized programmes in a seven-patient peripheral blood mononuclear cell cohort and assessed paired bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and longitudinal alveolar-macrophage profiles. PBMC disease groups were severely confounded with expression-inferred sex. In purified neutrophils, paired ARDS–healthy-volunteer comparisons and healthy-donor granulocyte–macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF)/broad phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K) perturbations were analysed separately.

items.title: Study Links Social Media Dietary Habits and Behavioral Constructs in University Students
items.summary: University students frequently encounter nutrition information, peer norms, and food marketing on digital platforms, yet research connecting these exposures to Integrated Behavioral Model constructs remains limited. A cross-sectional study of 385 undergraduates at King Khalid University investigated these dynamics using an Arabic questionnaire on social media and dietary habits. The findings revealed that all model constructs were positively correlated with dietary habits. Multiple linear regression indicated that positive attitudes, regular physical activity, and moderate daily social media use of up to four hours were associated with higher dietary habit scores. These results highlight that behavioral beliefs and lifestyle contexts can inform digital nutrition programs aimed at young adults.
items.author: Amani Alhazmi, Maha Ali, Manal Mohammed Hawash et al.
items.original_title: Social media–related dietary behaviors and integrated behavioral model constructs among university students: A cross-sectional study
items.original_summary: by Amani Alhazmi, Maha Ali, Manal Mohammed Hawash, Bali Sharma, Ali Mohieldin, Mahmoud Abdelwahab Khedr Background Social media exposes young adults to nutrition information, food marketing, peer norms, and health-related content. However, evidence on social media–related dietary behaviors and their links to Integrated Behavioral Model (IBM) constructs among Saudi university students is limited. This study examined these behaviors, IBM constructs, and factors associated with the Dietary Habits score among King Khalid University (KKU) students. Methods A cross-sectional study included 385 KKU undergraduates, recruited through convenience sampling between February and April 2026. Participants completed the Arabic IBM-based Social Media and Dietary Habits Questionnaire.

items.title: Researchers Find Evidence of Cretaceous Strandline Deposit in Wyoming's Lance Formation
items.summary: Excavations at the Hanson Ranch within the Maastrichtian Lance Formation of Wyoming have historically uncovered tens of thousands of disarticulated vertebrate fossils across various bonebeds. Recently, however, seven newly discovered quarries yielded associated remains of multiple dinosaur taxa, including Triceratops, Edmontosaurus, Thescelosaurus, and Anzu, in a configuration previously unseen at the site. These quarries align along a southeasterly direction, matching the orientation of long axes in many elongate bones found within the deposits. The preservation of associated skeletal elements indicates that soft-tissue connections or integumentary containment remained intact during transport and burial. Scientists conclude that these encapsulated, floating carcasses were stranded along a shoreline of the Western Interior Seaway.
items.author: Keith Snyder, Nelson Llempen, Caleb Darling et al.
items.original_title: Evidence for an upper cretaceous strandline deposit in the Lance Formation, Wyoming, USA
items.original_summary: by Keith Snyder, Nelson Llempen, Caleb Darling, Alessandro Franchini, Matthew McLain, Arthur Chadwick A series of apparently related quarries in the Maastrichtian (uppermost Cretaceous) Lance Formation of Wyoming provided the opportunity to evaluate the taphonomic mode for a suite of vertebrate fossils. Extensive work on the Hanson Ranch over the past three decades has exposed tens of thousands of fossils from dinosaur-bearing bonebeds. All of these bonebeds consist of disarticulated and disassociated remains. However, seven recently discovered quarries have yielded the remains of one or more dinosaur taxa (e.g., Triceratops, Edmontosaurus, Thescelosaurus, Anzu) in a state of association that was hitherto unknown on the ranch.

items.title: New Multiplex Real-Time PCR Assay Detects Parasites Directly in Canid Feces
items.summary: Echinococcus multilocularis and Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato cause alveolar and cystic echinococcosis, posing significant public health concerns. Traditional diagnostic methods like copromicroscopy are labor-intensive and require specialized personnel, while certain molecular assays lack adequate sensitivity or specificity. To address these limitations, researchers developed a real-time PCR assay utilizing species-specific probes to detect both parasites directly from domestic and wild canid fecal samples. The protocol demonstrated high analytical performance, achieving a limit of detection of a single egg per reaction and 100% specificity for both species. By extracting DNA directly from feces and eliminating sequencing requirements through specific probes, the method significantly reduces laboratory processing time and expenses during wildlife surveillance.
items.author: Graziana Da Rold, Filippo Marzoli, Federica Obber et al.
items.original_title: Analytical performances and field assessment of a multiplex Real-Time PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of Echinococcus multilocularis and Echinococcus granulosus sensu stricto in wild canids fecal samples
items.original_summary: by Graziana Da Rold, Filippo Marzoli, Federica Obber, Roberto Celva, Alessia Franzoso, Giacomo De Conti, Elisa Dalla Libera, Patrizia Danesi, Sofia Sgubin, Rudi Cassini, Erica Marchiori, Dominik Trenkwalder, Piero Bonelli, Giovanna Masala, Chiara Rossi, Heidi Christine Hauffe, Carlo Vittorio Citterio Echinococcus multilocularis and Echinococcus granulosus sensu lato are the causative agents of alveolar and cystic echinococcosis, two important zoonoses with significant public health implications. Several diagnostic approaches are currently available for the detection of these parasites in definitive hosts, including classical parasitological methods and molecular techniques. However, conventional techniques such as intestinal scraping or copromicroscopy are often labor-intensive, time-consuming, and require skilled personnel, while some molecular assays may show limited sensitivity or specificity.

items.title: Study Explores Physiological and Cognitive Responses to Watching Long Videos
items.summary: As online learning and conferences expand, understanding how prolonged video viewing impacts psychological states and physiological regulation becomes increasingly important. Researchers evaluated autonomic nervous system and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis activities while twenty-six university students watched 90-minute high-interest comedy videos and low-interest lecture videos. Participants provided subjective ratings and submitted saliva samples for stress markers, while heart rate and heart rate variability were monitored. Subjective concentration, comprehension, and interest scores were significantly higher during the high-interest video, whereas fatigue was lower. Physiological metrics showed distinct temporal variations in heart rate and heart rate variability across time, and salivary cortisol decreased throughout viewing, though stress indicators like amylase showed no significant changes.
items.author: Hiroki Matsui, Rina Tanabe, Rikako Mogi et al.
items.original_title: Cognitive and physiological responses to prolonged video viewing: Activities of the autonomic nervous system and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal axis in relation to video interest
items.original_summary: by Hiroki Matsui, Rina Tanabe, Rikako Mogi, Yuka Sugiura, Hana Yokomachi, Tomoyuki Yokoyama In recent years, online lectures and conferences have become widespread, but prolonged video viewing has been suggested to affect psychological state and physiological regulation. However, few studies have objectively examined how such viewing influences autonomic and endocrine activity. This study aimed to evaluate changes in autonomic nervous system (ANS) activity and hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activity during the viewing of high- and low-interest videos. Twenty-six university students (10 males, 16 females; aged 21–24 years) watched high-interest (comedy) and low-interest (lecture) videos (90 minutes each). After viewing each video, they recorded subjective ratings of concentration, comprehension, interest, and fatigue.

items.title: A Poisson-multinomial model for quantifying gene therapy vector integrity using quadplex digital PCR
items.summary: by Lauren Tereshko, Matthew Ryals, Cullen Mason, Romi Admanit, Jake Gagnon Quantitative characterization of gene therapy vectors is critical for confirming product safety and efficacy. While digital PCR (dPCR) strategies are widely used to estimate sequence integrity, accurate statistical interpretation of multiplexed assays remains a persistent challenge due to limitations of existing analytical models. Here, we describe a quadplex droplet dPCR approach for quantitative characterization of vector integrity across four targets within a single reaction. We adapt a Poisson-multinomial model to enable quantitation of sequence integrity and genetic linkage across all combinations of the four targeted regions. We evaluate both the capabilities and limitations of this approach and provide practical guidance for multiplexed assay design and data interpretation.

items.title: Network analysis of physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress among Chinese university students
items.summary: by Jingbo Wang, Yuanyuan Ma, Tong Han, Juan Wang Objective Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress may be interconnected among university students, but their dimension-specific associations remain unclear. This study examined their network structure and compared male and female networks. Methods A convenience sample of 1,600 university students from two higher-education institutions in central China was surveyed from 16 March to 29 May 2026. Physical exercise, sleep quality, and psychological distress were assessed using the Physical Activity Rating Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and 21-item Depression Anxiety Stress Scales. A 12-node regularized partial correlation network was estimated. Expected influence, bridge expected influence, bootstrap procedures, and network comparison tests were used.

items.title: The true cost of dialysis modalities: A detailed analysis from a UK renal centre
items.summary: by Nitin V. Kolhe, Andrew Muggleton, Lisa Page, Richard J. Fluck, Maarten W. Taal Purpose Dialysis accounts for more than £1 billion of annual NHS expenditure, yet contemporary modality-specific costing studies using real-world operational data remain limited. Accurate cost estimates are essential for service planning, reimbursement, and workforce allocation. We hypothesised that home-based dialysis modalities, particularly home haemodialysis (HHD) and continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD), would be less costly and associated with a more favourable cost–benchmark margin than in-centre haemodialysis (ICHD) when workforce, consumables, infrastructure, and overheads were fully allocated. Materials and methods A comprehensive micro-costing analysis was undertaken at University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust during 2023–24.

items.title: An invariant-guided model for automated detection of anomalous execution regimes from production telemetry
items.summary: by Viacheslav Kovtun, Frederic Huralnyk, Artem Huralnyk, Marta Yankiv, Jamil Abedalrahim Jamil Alsayaydeh Modern cloud-based distributed software systems increasingly exhibit persistent changes in execution behaviour that cannot be adequately characterised by isolated events or threshold violations alone. Although contemporary production environments already provide mature observability infrastructures for collecting logs, metrics, and traces, the formal representation of execution regimes derived from such telemetry remains insufficiently developed. This paper proposes an invariant-guided geometric framework for modelling execution regimes and detecting anomalous regime transitions under weak supervision. The framework applies common principles of invariant-based feature mapping, weighted pseudometrics, and geometric regularisation to log-derived and KPI-derived regime representations.
items.author: Viacheslav Kovtun, Frederic Huralnyk, Artem Huralnyk et al.

items.title: Dose-dependent hepatorenal toxicity of polystyrene microplastics in BALB/c mice
items.summary: by Samia Iftikhar, Hassien M. Alnashiri, Mehnaz Akhtar, Zuniar Ahsan, Muhammad Latif, A. El-Shabasy, Mohamed Mostafa Soliman Microplastics have emerged as pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing concern regarding their potential adverse effects on mammalian health. However, comprehensive evaluations of the dose-related hepatorenal toxicity of polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs) remain limited. This study investigated the effects of oral exposure to PS-MPs on hepatic and renal function in BALB/c mice. Animals were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 10/group) and orally administered 0 (control), 10, 20, or 30 mg PS-MPs/kg body weight/day for 28 consecutive days. Hepatorenal toxicity was evaluated using serum biochemical biomarkers, histopathological examination, semi-quantitative lesion scoring, and Pearson’s correlation analysis.
items.author: Samia Iftikhar, Hassien M. Alnashiri, Mehnaz Akhtar et al.

items.title: Seasonal dynamics of leaf macro- and micronutrients in three commercial avocado varieties at Mojo and Melkassa, Ethiopia
items.summary: by Zeyede Aregahegn, Edossa Etissa, Israel Bekele, Dejene Abera Seasonal leaf nutrient data needed to guide fertilization are scarce for Ethiopian avocado orchards. We measured total nitrogen (TN), Ca, Cu, Fe, Mn and Zn in leaves of tagged Hass, Fuerte and Ettinger trees at the Melkassa Agricultural Research Center (February–July) and of Hass trees on three farms at Mojo (February–June), and described the soils of both sites. Data were analysed with linear mixed models, Tukey’s test and repeated-measures correlation. Mean leaf TN (1.13–1.41%) was below the sufficiency range in all varieties and did not differ significantly between months, varieties or sites, and leaf Zn was below 20 mg/kg in most samples.
items.author: Zeyede Aregahegn, Edossa Etissa, Israel Bekele et al.

items.title: Patient complaints in dentistry: A qualitative meta-synthesis
items.summary: by Lorraine Snyman, Thomas Corne Postma, Werdie Van Staden Introduction Patient complaints in dentistry concern their dissatisfaction, safety concerns, quality of care, and challenges within the patient-practitioner relationship. Whilst existing research of these complaints has largely focused on quantitative analysis of regulatory complaints and malpractice, these studies capture little of the meaning that patients express in their complaints. This study synthesized a qualitative understanding of patient complaints across various dentistry settings. Method This qualitative meta-synthesis followed the six-step approach of Sandelowski and Barroso, drawing on previously published qualitative findings from various studies that constituted a higher-order case as suggested by Hoon’s design framework.

items.title: The effect of self-determination interventions on reading outcomes for middle and high school students with learning disabilities: A systematic review
items.summary: by Mohammed A. Aljufayr, Abdulrahman S. Alsultan, Abdulaziz M. Alasmari Background Students with learning disabilities (LD) often struggle with reading skills, increasing the need for interventions that enhance their reading outcomes. Self-determination (SD) interventions can develop reading skills for students in all grade levels, but previous reviews of SD intervention studies have focused on elementary school students. This systematic review investigated the effects of SD interventions on reading outcomes for middle and high school students with LD. Methods Seventeenth studies published between 1982 and 2025 in scholarly journals were reviewed, examining participant demographics, settings, designs, intervention procedures, dependent variables, interobserver agreement, procedural fidelity, social validity, maintenance, generalization, intervention effects, and quality.

items.title: RPDL-YOLO: An efficient YOLOv8 framework for small bird detection in airport airside environments
items.summary: by Xinling Wen, Liming Liu, Yu Chen, Zhaoyu Liu, Zhengxiang Ma, Yapeng Wu, Kun Liang, Teng Jiang, Heng Yang Bird intrusions into airport security zones pose significant threats to aviation safety. However, the small size, rapid movement, and irregular flight patterns of birds often result in missed detections and false alarms in vision-based surveillance systems, especially in complex open-sky environments with low contrast and significant background interference. Although YOLOv8s achieves strong real-time performance, it remains limited in fine-grained feature representation and small-object detection capability. To address these challenges, we propose an improved detection model termed RPDL-YOLO (Refined Perception with Dual-branch Detection and Localization YOLO).
items.author: Xinling Wen, Liming Liu, Yu Chen et al.

items.title: The effectiveness of compression garments on RRI prevention in half- and full-marathon runners: Emulation of a RCT using data from an observational study
items.summary: by T. P. C. Franke, N. P. A. Zuithoff, F. J. G. Backx, B. M. A. Huisstede Background Runners use compression garments (CGs) to reduce the risk of lower extremity running-related injuries (RRIs). However, studies investigating if using CGs alters the risk of RRIs in runners are scarce. Purpose To study the effect of CGs on the occurrence of lower extremity RRIs in half and full marathon runners. Study design Observational cohort study Method We emulated a hypothetical target trial, an imaginary RCT, using data from the observational SUMMUM-2017 study. Runners who participated in one of the four cohorts of this study during their preparation for the half or full Utrecht Marathon were followed for 16 weeks.

items.title: Prevalence and factors associated with irregular red blood cell antibodies among blood donors in Eastern Tanzania
items.summary: by Mariam Charles Monah, Vulstan James Shedura, Peter Richard Torokaa, Loveness Urio, Seif Abdul, Rosemary Bulemo, Mariam R. Mbwana, Sephord S. Ntibabara, Oscar Mwashiuya, Beatrice Tingo, Macdonald Mahiti, Upendo Kibwana, Salim Masoud, Joel Manyahi, Mtebe Majigo, Agricola Joachim, Doreen Kamori Background Irregular red blood cell (RBC) antibodies are antibodies other than naturally occurring anti-A and anti-B. Although the global prevalence of these antibodies is relatively low, ranging from 0.2% to 2%, donors who have irregular RBC antibodies can present immunological risk for patients due to hemolytic transfusion reactions. Hence, it is imperative to determine the prevalence of these antibodies in resource-limited settings where laboratory infrastructure for screening is limited.

items.title: The effects of dual task training to improve self-efficacy, functional performance, and quality of life in individuals with Parkinson’s disease: A study protocol
items.summary: by Alvaro Reyes-Ponce, Travis Cruickshank, Andrea Mira, Nuria Pérez-Romero, Josefa Domingos Introduction Dual tasking is impaired in Parkinson’s disease (PD) and adversely impacts activities of daily living and quality of life. The benefits of different dual-task training modalities and the prioritization strategy (directing attention to both tasks versus shifting between them) in individuals with or without cognitive impairment are unclear. It is also unknown whether motor-cognitive benefits from dual-task training are associated with reduced attentional demand. In addition, lower perceived ability to succeed at a specific task (self-efficacy) is associated with worse motor and non-motor symptoms and quality of life.

items.title: Public evaluation of food safety: Changes and influencing factors from the perspective of social governance — Evidence from CSS data (2006–2023)
items.summary: by Han Lin This study used descriptive analysis and multinomial logistic regression on seven‑wave Chinese Social Survey (CSS) data spanning 2006‑2023 to systematically examine long‑term trends and determinants of public food‑safety evaluation. Public food‑safety evaluation exhibited a phased “rise‑fall‑rise” mean score pattern across the study period. Level of social security showed a consistent significant positive correlation with food‑safety evaluation in all seven survey years ( p < 0.001) with fluctuating‑yet‑growing effect sizes; for the “very safe vs. very unsafe” contrast, the odds ratio fell from 2.056 (2006) then rebounded to 2.201 (2023). In year‑stratified models, educational attainment had a stable negative association with food‑safety evaluation, whereas control‑variable effects including gender and age varied across survey waves.

items.title: The relationship between ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and reactive postural control mechanisms in response to anterior perturbations
items.summary: by Mosa Pashaei, Hadi Ramezanloo, Mohamadreza Hatefi Adequate ankle dorsiflexion range of motion (DF-ROM) is essential for generating sufficient corrective torque during an ankle strategy; however, limitations in dorsiflexion may mechanically constrain this response, potentially leading to earlier reliance on hip or stepping strategies. Although indirect evidence links dorsiflexion capacity to dynamic balance performance, it remains unclear whether restricted dorsiflexion influences the selection of reactive postural control strategies in healthy young adults. Twenty active male participants were recruited for this study. Ankle DF-ROM was measured via the weight-bearing lunge test and categorized as either normal (≥20°) or restricted ( χ 2 (2) = 0.826, p = 0.662).

items.title: SeqBattNet: A discrete-state physics-informed neural network with aging adaptation for battery modeling
items.summary: by Khoa Tran, Hung-Cuong Trinh, Vy-Rin Nguyen, T. Nguyen-Thoi, Vin Nguyen-Thai, Hung Pham, Ho-Si-Hung Nguyen Accurate battery modeling is essential for reliable state estimation in modern applications, such as predicting the remaining discharge time and remaining discharge energy in battery management systems. Existing approaches face several limitations: model-based methods require a large number of physical parameters; data-driven methods rely heavily on labeled datasets; and current physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often lack aging adaptation, still depend on many physical parameters, or require continuous state regeneration. In this work, we propose SeqBattNet, a discrete-state PINN with built-in aging adaptation for battery modeling to predict terminal voltage during the discharge process.
items.author: Khoa Tran, Hung-Cuong Trinh, Vy-Rin Nguyen et al.

items.title: Mobility-state- and handover-direction-aware analytical and machine learning-based HCP optimization in 5G heterogeneous networks
items.summary: by Fozia Panhwer, Muhammad Mujtaba Shaikh, Beenish Ansari, Iqra Ameer, Mohamed A. Elmagzoub, Asadullah Shaikh The use of ultra-dense small cells in 5G heterogeneous networks increases capacity, coverage and spectral efficiency, but it also complicates mobility management. In dense macro-small-cell networks, user devices often cross cells with varying coverage, transmit power, and propagation conditions, which can lead to high risks of radio-link failure, handover failure, ping-pong handover and unnecessary handover. These problems are exacerbated by using fixed handover-control settings, in which a single-value handover margin and time-to-trigger cannot provide a good trade-off across UE velocities and handover directions. In this paper, we propose a mobility-state- and handover-direction-aware HCP optimization for 5G HetNets while retaining the Event A3 handover scheme, state-based handover flow and radio-link-monitoring framework.

items.title: Generation and in vitro functional characterization of anti-CD22 chimeric antigen receptor T cells derived from newly generated monoclonal antibody clones
items.summary: by Wipawadee Ruengdej, Vichaya Chuthaphakdikun, Sirirut Jewmoung, Nithidol Sakunrangsit, Chatikorn Boonkrai, Trairak Pisitkun, Supannikar Tawinwung, Koramit Suppipat Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of B-cell malignancies, but relapse after CD19-directed therapy remains a major challenge, often because of loss or downregulation of CD19 expression. CD22 is an attractive alternative target because it is expressed on malignant B cells, including in many cases of CD19-negative disease. In this study, we generated and characterized novel anti-CD22 monoclonal antibody–derived CAR constructs for in vitro evaluation. Four anti-CD22 monoclonal antibody clones were initially screened, and two clones, 24A7G6 and 29H9C8, were selected for CAR development based on their favorable binding and CAR surface expression profiles.

items.title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
items.summary: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties.

items.title: Hubble Gravitational Lenses Prepare Ground for Roman Space Telescope
items.summary: A new gallery of gravitational lenses captured by the Hubble Space Telescope highlights diverse cosmic formations that will serve as targets for the upcoming Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Gravitational lensing happens when a massive foreground object bends and magnifies the light of a distant background object. Researchers use these distorted light patterns to study mass distribution and dark matter. While Hubble excels at high-resolution images of individual lenses, Roman will capture broader cosmic panoramas. Combining data from both observatories allows scientists to build precise lens models, detect small dark matter clumps, and improve understanding of galaxy evolution.

items.title: Large Pockels Effect in Multiaxial Ferroelectrics Induced by Polarization Reorientation
items.summary: Materials with large linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect have significant potential for fabricating energy-efficient photonic devices. Previous strategies have mostly relied on structural softness---associated with phase boundary, domain wall, or strain induced phase transition---to create large Pockels effect in ferroelectrics. In this Letter, we show that polarization reorientation in multiaxial ferroelectrics may create structural softness and thus induce large Pockels effect. By developing a phenomenological theory, we find that multiaxial ferroelectrics exhibit a hysteretic relationship between the azimuth angles of the polarization and the electric field, and a possible divergence of the linear electro-optic coefficient may occur at an appropriate polarization azimuth angle.

items.title: Discrete anomaly inflow from SymTFT of $U(1)$ global symmetry: the modified Villain resolution
items.summary: We construct a lattice SymTFT for a $U(1)$ global symmetry with anomaly coefficient $k$ using the modified Villain formulation, in which the spin structure required for odd $k$ is realised explicitly by lattice Majorana fermions. We demonstrate that the same Majorana fermions sit at the junctions of the symmetry lines, exactly where the fusion of two $U(1)$ elements wraps around the circle. From the lattice algebra of lines and junctions we derive the $R$- and $F$-symbols in the bulk and on the gapped boundary, and show that for odd $k$ the boundary $F$-symbol obeys the Gu-Wen relation for the $U(1)$ symmetry defect, without passing through a bosonic shadow.

items.title: Is Spin Slow in Hot QCD?
items.summary: Promoting spin to a hydrodynamic variable requires slow relaxation, as mass-suppressed helicity flips in hot QCD suggest. Using the full leading-order collision operator, we show instead that light-quark spin damps at the transport rate $g^4T\ln(1/g)$, nearly as fast as vector currents. Since spatial spin locks to momentum, helicity-conserving soft, small-angle scatterings readily rotate it. Damping involves multiple kinetic modes beyond a single relaxation time, global rotation adds only reversible precession, and stronger coupling further disfavors a slow spin mode in quark-gluon plasma.

items.title: Accelerating solitons in Rindler space
items.summary: Relativistic nonlinear field theories that are integrable in two-dimensional Minkowski spacetime remain integrable in Rindler space. We investigate the properties of classical sine-Gordon (SG) solitons in Rindler space. Accelerating observers in each of the two Rindler wedges can see only a portion of the full soliton in Minkowski spacetime; this portion itself forms a soliton carrying a partial topological charge. The soliton solution admits the following interpretation: a soliton incoming from the horizon decelerates to stop at some point, then falls back and accelerates to the speed of light toward the horizon. Energy can flow into and out of the Rindler horizon.

items.title: Matching lattice and continuum chiral determinants at finite volume
items.summary: Recent formulations of lattice chiral gauge theories define a complex fermion weight either through Craig's gauge-invariant overlap measure or, following Hsu and Witten, through a continuum Weyl determinant on a reconstructed gauge connection, with its phase fixed by the five-dimensional $η$-invariant. For one $SU(5)$ generation on a flat four-torus, we prove that their relative weights agree in the continuum limit along smooth gapped paths, after fixing a normalization and subtracting a local Yang-Mills counterterm, whose coefficient we determine. On bounded smooth families a uniform Dirac gap suffices: the vacuum expansion need not converge. We obtain explicit uniform convergence rates for the logarithmic variations and, for Craig's interpolation, prove the reconstruction bounds that the matching requires, extending Hsu's small-field comparison to finite amplitude.

items.title: Affine Vertex Operator Algebras and Correlation Functions on Elliptic Curves
items.summary: Let $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra attached to a finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra at arbitrary level, and let $M=\bigoplus_{N=0}^{\infty}M_N$ be a $V^{\Bbbk}(\mathfrak{g})$ -module. We give an explicit formula for every genus-one trace of affine currents as a finite sum over cycle partitions. We then show the convergence of all fixed zero-mode trace series, hence absolute locally uniform convergence of the current traces and their meromorphic continuation on the elliptic configuration space. The same conclusion is obtained for arbitrary affine-state insertions. Finally, we compute the cases of at most four currents and the nodal limit $q\to 0$, in which the type-1 and type-2 elliptic cycle coefficients degenerate to rational genus-zero cycle coefficients and the module trace reduces to the ground-state space.

items.title: Poles Are Not Enough: Zeros of Dyson-Schwinger Gluon Propagators in Yang-Mills Thermodynamics
items.summary: A normalized two-point function with several poles does not, on its own, fix the source-free thermal partition function. For the Gaussian measure of the original gluon field, a positive-residue rational propagator contributes determinants from its poles and from zeros interlaced between them. The zero factors distinguish this completion from a gas of independent pole fields and restore two ultraviolet polarizations per adjoint eigenvalue at every finite truncation. We apply the construction to a background-covariant completion of the elliptic Dyson-Schwinger gluon kernel. The first-order SU(3) transition is already present with a single pole, and the saturated six-pole result shifts $T_c/M_g$ by only $1.48\%$, where $T_c$ is the coexistence temperature and $M_g$ is the lowest pole mass.

items.title: Thermodynamics within and across AdS Gauss--Bonnet holographic CFTs
items.summary: We study thermal competition within individual holographic conformal field theories (CFTs) and across theories with different anomaly coefficients in five-dimensional AdS Gauss--Bonnet gravity. We derive the work term conjugate to the dimensionless coupling from the boundary first law and use a common boundary clock to compare charged spherical saddles at fixed external source. Varying this source drives a first-order switch between the CFTs at the endpoints of the chosen coupling interval. In the unit-lapse cylinder clock with the zero-type-D vacuum energy, strict concavity at fixed radius reduces the global comparison to these two endpoints. The preferred coupling jumps across the coexistence line, whose slope is related to the entropy difference by a generalized Clapeyron relation.
items.author: Limin Zeng

items.title: Generalized Kosmann derivative and symmetry operators on Dirac structures
items.summary: We develop a spinorial symmetry framework for metric Dirac structures in $H$-twisted exact Courant algebroids. A generalized metric equips a Dirac structure with an intrinsic Riemannian Lie-algebroid geometry and identifies it isometrically with the positive subbundle of the generalized tangent bundle. For sections preserving the generalized metric, we prove an exact intertwining between the positive-spinor Kosmann--Dorfman action and the intrinsic Kosmann derivative. The comparison is independent of the auxiliary compatible generalized connection. Within the intrinsic geometry we derive Killing--Yano (KY) and conformal Killing--Yano (CKY) integrability identities, construct Killing-spinor-preserving operators from odd special KY and even special closed CKY forms, and obtain these forms from Hermitian bilinears of Killing spinors with imaginary Killing number.

items.title: Scotland's Flow Country Peat Bogs Store Vast Amounts of Carbon
items.summary: The Flow Country in northern Scotland features extensive blanket bogs that store massive amounts of carbon. Because these soggy, waterlogged soils prevent microbes from fully breaking down dead plant material, partially decayed matter accumulates into thick layers of peat. These unique ecosystems require abundant rainfall, poor drainage, and low evapotranspiration. Covering about 1,900 square kilometers of the Scottish Highlands, the area represents Europe's largest blanket bog ecosystem and the first of its kind to earn UNESCO World Heritage status. While forests typically store carbon in living trees that can release it when damaged, peat bogs can preserve carbon for thousands of years. Globally, peatlands cover a tiny fraction of Earth's land surface yet store more than twice as much carbon as all the world's forests combined.

items.title: Bright and Uniform Silicon Carbide Nanophotonic Arrays for Scalable Nanoscale Quantum Sensing
items.summary: Silicon carbide (SiC) spin defects are emerging as powerful platforms for nanoscale quantum sensing due to their near-surface stability, near-infrared emission, and CMOS compatibility. However, poor photon collection efficiency and the reliance on randomly distributed defects hinder the realization of practical, large-scale devices. Here, we demonstrate scalable, ultra-bright, and highly uniform SiC quantum nanophotonic arrays. By combining a self-aligned fabrication process with localized oxygen ion implantation, we deterministically position PL5 and PL6 centers at the exact center of 4H-SiC nanopillars. This architecture yields record-high photon count rates of $\sim$1 Mcps (PL5) and $\sim$2 Mcps (PL6), establishing a new benchmark for SiC color centers while maintaining near-identical brightness across the array.

items.title: Curiosity Completes Drilling at Nazca Site to Investigate Crystal Forms
items.summary: The Curiosity rover finished its drilling operations at the "Nazca" bedrock location, which features unique disk-shaped and potato chip-shaped crystal forms. Throughout the week, the rover delivered drill samples to the SAM instrument, conducted ChemCam LIBS measurements on various crystal targets like "Ahi Veremos," "Colca," and "Bermejo," and captured extensive Mastcam and RMI image mosaics. Environmental monitoring included dust devil surveys and horizon movies. Friday's plans prioritized imaging a solar eclipse by the Martian moon Phobos, executing nighttime MAHLI LED imaging of the crystals, and driving the rover away from the drill site to resume its southerly exploration route.
