In this prospective cohort of 400 active LN patients followed for 12 months, the primary outcome was 12-month CRR. Candidate predictors were assessed at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Four ML models (Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, Elastic Net, and eXtreme Gradient Boosting) were developed and validated on a test set.
items.author: Song S, Fan Y, Zhang X, Cheng J, Gao D, Zhang J, Ding T, Ji L, Zhang Z.

items.title: "It pushes me, but it also drains me": A qualitative study of perfectionism and well-being among doctoral students in India.
items.summary: Purpose Although perfectionism has been linked to academic achievement and psychological functioning, less is known about how doctoral students experience, interpret, and negotiate perfectionism in their academic lives, particularly within Indian higher education. This qualitative exploratory study examined how doctoral students in India experience perfectionism. Method The study was conducted between October 2024 and March 2026 following institutional ethics approval (Ref: IEC2: 177/2025). Thirteen doctoral students were recruited purposively after screening for sociodemographic variation and scores on the Frost Multidimensional Perfectionism Scale. Data were collected through in-depth semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. Results Five themes were identified: Making sense of perfectionism, Expressions of perfectionistic tendencies, Influences on perfectionism, The double-edged experience, and Managing perfectionism.
items.author: Sugumar P, Vaidyanathan S.

items.title: Effects of COVID-19 vaccination type and vaccination-infection interval on viral clearance dynamics in Omicron BA.5 patients at Guangzhou Fangcang shelter hospitals: A propensity score matched multicenter retrospective cohort study.
items.summary: The Omicron BA.5 subvariant exhibited pronounced immune evasion and was associated with widespread breakthrough infections. Unlike settings where mRNA vaccines predominated, China mainly used inactivated vaccines, with the adenovirus type 5-vectored vaccine Ad5-nCoV also administered at scale. Real-world evidence on post-infection viral clearance associated with these platforms remains limited. This multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolled 16,533 mild or asymptomatic Omicron BA.5 cases from two Fangcang shelter hospitals in Guangzhou, China, from Novernber 5 to December 8, 2022. The primary objective was to compare viral-clearance time between unvaccinated and vaccinated participants. The secondary objective was to compare inactivated-vaccine recipients, or and Ad5-nCoV recipients, containing regimens in a propensity score-matched cohort; the last-dose-to-infection interval analysis was exploratory.
items.author: Jiang Z, Wang Q, Kong X, Lin X, Ma D, Chen F, Cai Q, Sun Q, Deng Z, Zeng H, Xu Y.

items.title: The p16 isoform of CDKN2A inhibits ferroptosis to promote the progression of papillary thyroid carcinoma by influencing the p53/SLC7A11/GPX4 pathway.
items.summary: Background Although papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) has a relatively good prognosis, it is also prone to recurrence and metastasis. Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 2 A (CDKN2A) can affect tumor progression by regulating ferroptosis, but its role in PTC remains unclear. Materials and methods The expression of CDKN2A, p14, p16, GPX4, and TFRC in PTC was assessed by qPCR, western blotting, and immunohistochemistry, and their clinical correlations were analyzed. In TPC-1 and BCPAP cells, CDKN2A/p14/p16 expression was modulated, followed by evaluation of ferroptosis-related changes using GPX4, TFRC, Fe 2 ⁺, ROS, GSH, C11-BODIPY lipid peroxidation, and transmission electron microscopy. Cell proliferation and migration were assessed by CCK-8, colony formation, wound-healing, and Transwell assays.
items.author: Wang Y, Mou YK, Yang T, Wang HR, Song XY, Liu WC, Shen H, Ren C, Song XC.

items.title: Delays in screening, diagnosis and monitoring are associated with worse clinical and economic outcomes for patients with chronic kidney disease: a narrative review.
items.summary: Background Chronic kidney disease (CKD) has substantial associated morbidity, mortality and healthcare costs that increase as CKD progresses. Despite newer, more effective treatments, the global burden of CKD continues to increase. Objective To understand patterns of screening, diagnosis, monitoring and treatment in CKD and how earlier treatment initiation could help mitigate CKD burden. Methods Targeted searches of bibliographic databases and grey literature sources identified studies published 2015-2025. Eligible evidence comprised observational studies on CKD screening and diagnosis rates, factors associated with delayed treatment initiation, clinical and economic burden of delayed diagnosis/treatment, and economic evaluations of population-based CKD screening. Thirty-five studies were synthesized narratively according to the CKD care pathway; no meta-analysis or formal quality assessment was conducted.
items.author: Fusco N, Weatherall J, Hurrell J.

items.title: Sensory responsiveness as a moderator of the association between cumulative trauma exposure and dissociation: a cross-sectional study.
items.summary: Background: Exposure to traumatic events is a well-established risk factor for dissociative symptoms; however, factors associated with individual variability in dissociation remain insufficiently understood. Objective: This study examined the relationships among sensory modulation difficulties, that is, atypical sensory responsiveness to everyday input, dissociation, and trauma exposure. Two forms of sensory responsiveness were examined: high sensory responsiveness, which denotes exaggerated and prolonged reactions to ordinary, non-painful sensory experiences (e.g. being bothered by sounds or textures), and low sensory responsiveness, which denotes reduced sensitivity to sensory input (e.g. enjoying loud noises or strong smells). The study also tested whether sensory modulation moderates the relationship between the number of traumatic events and dissociation beyond the effects of age, gender, and emotion regulation difficulties.
items.author: Lahav Y, Lifshitz M, Bar-Shalita T.

items.title: Substrate-specific mitochondrial bioenergetics and metabolic flexibility in visceral adipose tissue across obesity-related glycemic states.
items.summary: Obesity is characterized by the expansion of metabolically dysfunctional visceral adipose tissue (VAT) and chronic low-grade inflammation, which contribute to the development of insulin resistance. However, to what extent VAT bioenergetics and substrate preferences differ across distinct obesity-related glycaemic status profiles remains poorly understood. The present study aimed to assess substrate utilization and metabolic flexibility of VAT from individuals with obesity across different glycaemic statuses, namely euglycemia, prediabetes, and type 2 diabetes (T2D). VAT from individuals with obesity with euglycemia ( n = 11), prediabetes ( n = 12) and T2D ( n = 6) was harvested during bariatric surgery.
items.author: Mendonça DA, Bernardino RL, Topete M, Andrade S, Guimarães M, Pereira AM, Oliveira SB, Costa MM, Nora M, Monteiro MP, Pereira SS.

items.title: ID-SCAN: a functional MRI protocol for neurophenomenological phenotyping of dissociative identity disorder without trauma provocation.
items.summary: Background: Dissociative identity disorder (DID) is a trauma-related dissociative disorder in which two or more identity-agents recur within one person, each experiencing and evaluating itself and its surroundings. Most existing neuroimaging paradigms rely on symptom provocation using trauma-related autobiographical material. Identity-agent effects that are independent of symptom provocation need to be disentangled from emotional responses to trauma-related material and from the co-consciousness of other identity-agents. Objective: To introduce ID-SCAN (Identity-agent State Characterisation and Analysis), a functional MRI protocol without trauma provocation for within-person neurophenomenological characterisation of identity-agent expression and switching, and to test its feasibility in a co-conscious case. Method: A woman with DID living with persistent co-consciousness between two identity-agents (Adu and Ado) completed two fMRI tasks: identity-cued evaluation of identical insect photographs the agents made sense of in opposite ways, and trait judgments about self, the other agent and a shared intimate other.
items.author: Kajimura S, Okano K, Ueno S, Yamada J, Fukui H, Hirai A, Ito A, Abe N, Nakai R, Noma S, Murai T.

items.title: Potentially modifiable mediators of the association between child abuse and dementia.
items.summary: Background: Literature investigating mediation of the association between child abuse and dementia has largely considered composite adverse childhood experience scores rather than individual adverse experiences, despite evidence that different experiences have different impacts on dementia risk. Additionally, prior studies consider mediators in isolation, despite known associations between mediators which may impact indirect pathways from child abuse to dementia. Objectives: To investigate whether potentially modifiable health and lifestyle factors mediate the association between child abuse and dementia. Methods: We used data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing to investigate associations between child abuse and dementia ( N = 5,448). Indirect pathways through four mediator categories (education, health behaviours, mental health and cardiovascular health) were examined.
items.author: Taylor K, Howe LD, Lacey RE, Anderson E, Mukadam N.

items.title: Measurement invariance of the Clinician Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 between trauma-exposed non-Western refugee patients and Dutch patients seeking treatment for PTSD.
items.summary: Background: The Clinician-Administered PTSD Scale for DSM-5 (CAPS-5) is the gold standard to assess post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Although the CAPS-5 was developed and validated primarily in Western samples, it is often used to assess PTSD in non-Western refugees. Objective: This study investigated whether PTSD as assessed with the CAPS-5 has the same factor structure, item-factor relationships and symptom severity scores across trauma-exposed, treatment-seeking individuals with either a Dutch (i.e. Western) background or a non-Western refugee background . Methods: We evaluated four DSM-5 PTSD models and tested different levels of measurement invariance in non-Western refugee (nWr) patients ( N = 710) and Dutch patients ( N = 1162) using confirmatory factor analyses (CFA).
items.author: van der Velden L, van der Aa N, Boeschoten MA, de la Rie SM.

items.title: Resilience and vulnerability factors for post-traumatic symptoms among Israeli adults: the aftermath of 7 October events.
items.summary: Background: Understanding the factors that contribute to resilience and vulnerability following extreme trauma is critical for improving psychological outcomes in affected populations. While previous studies have addressed this question, they often focused on a single phase of trauma or were confounded by socioeconomic and displacement factors, leaving gaps in understanding how pre-, peri-, and post-traumatic variables jointly shape psychological outcomes. Objective: The present study investigated predictors of post-traumatic stress symptoms in the aftermath of the 7 October 2023 attacks in Israel, aiming to provide an integrated model of symptom development. Method: A total of 377 Israeli adults completed online self-report measures assessing pre-, peri-, and post-traumatic experiences, including the PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5).
items.author: Berebbi S, David M, Kalanthroff E.

items.title: Distinguishing programmatic change from data artifacts in hospital certification records: a change‑point and leakage-audit approach in Thailand.
items.summary: Background Routine Health Information Systems (RHIS) produce administrative data where apparent shifts may reflect recording practices rather than genuine program changes. Methods appearing to support such shifts can share hidden information with them, a reproducibility concern in machine‑learning research. Objective This study aims to illustrate a leakage pattern that can produce misleading corroboration in change‑point and clustering analyses of routine health data and to propose a protocol to reduce such circularity. This is a preliminary, proof-of-concept validation, not a full operating-characteristic evaluation. Methods Certification records from 86 hospitals in a regional environmental‑certification program in Thailand were analysed. Change‑point detection on a recorded outcome field was assessed against three checks: an alternative construct, an alternative definition, and clustering restricted to timing-unrelated features.
items.author: Sinchai S, Sinchai A.

items.title: The institutional afterlife of a pandemic: Zimbabwe's One Health strategy and the limits of crisis-driven governance.
items.summary: Governance structures built during a crisis often outlive the emergency that produced them. Zimbabwe's National One Health Strategic Plan 2026-2030 (the Plan) is a direct institutional legacy of the COVID-19 pandemic. Its coordination structure sits in the Office of the President and Cabinet rather than a line ministry, deliberately echoing the Whole-of-Government arrangement credited with the country's pandemic response. This debate piece asks whether governance built in a crisis survives once the crisis is over. It draws on the Plan itself, a 2024 baseline assessment of One Health in Zimbabwe, the self-assessment phase of the country's 2025 Joint External Evaluation of health security capacities, and published case studies from Kenya and Rwanda.
items.author: Zinyemba C.

items.title: Clinical significance of the systemic immune-inflammation index as a minimally invasive biomarker reflecting histological activity in IgA nephropathy.
items.summary: Background The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a prognostic biomarker in IgA nephropathy (IgAN), but its relationship with acute versus chronic histological lesions remains unclear. Methods This retrospective study included 71 adults with biopsy-proven primary IgAN. To distinguish systemic inflammation drivers, histopathological severity was evaluated using continuous variables: the proportions of glomeruli with acute (cellular/fibrocellular crescents, necrosis) and chronic (global/segmental sclerosis, fibrous crescents) lesions. Associations between SII and these lesions were assessed using multiple linear regression. An additional sensitivity analysis adjusting for age and eGFR was performed. Results Median SII was 508.87. In the linear regression model adjusted for age, sex, estimated glomerular filtration rate, and proteinuria, acute lesions showed a positive but statistically nonsignificant association with SII (β = 10.615, 95% CI -0.629-21.860, p = 0.064), whereas chronic lesions also showed no statistically significant association ( p = 0.871).
items.author: Miyazaki T, Matsumoto K, Kawanishi M, Anzai K, Kajio Y, Mimura Y, Fujita T, Takeshima A.

items.title: Nutritional risk, inflammation, and hospitalization after hemodialysis initiation.
items.summary: Evidence linking nutritional and inflammatory markers at hemodialysis initiation to subsequent hospital stay remains limited. We examined whether the Geriatric Nutritional Risk Index (GNRI) and C-reactive protein (CRP) at hemodialysis initiation were associated with prolonged post-initiation hospital stay. This single-center retrospective study included patients who initiated hemodialysis during hospitalization and transitioned to maintenance hemodialysis between 2004 and 2024. The primary outcome was hospitalization for 30 days or longer after hemodialysis initiation. Multivariable logistic regression was used with adjustment for age, sex, cardiovascular disease, diabetes mellitus, initiation modality, calendar period, and pre-hemodialysis vascular access status. Among 517 patients, 501 were included in multivariable analysis, and 166 patients (32.1%) experienced prolonged post-initiation stay.
items.author: Uematsu H, Toida T, Tanaka Y, Joki N.

items.title: Cilengitide limits syndromic and sporadic thoracic aortic aneurysm by targeting specific αV integrin.
items.summary: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, still lacking an etiologic therapy. Aberrant activation of TGF-β and dysregulation of mechanotransduction signalling in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) play a key role in the pathology. However, a precise picture of molecular mechanisms in the disease is still unclear. Integrins containing the αV subunit are central in pro-fibrotic pathways mediated by TGF-β and mechanotransduction signalling pathways, but their role as a potential therapeutic target in syndromic and sporadic TAAs still needs investigation. We showed higher expression levels of αV integrin in both types of human TAAs and that the αV integrin inhibitor Cilengitide limits pro-fibrotic events in patient-derived VSMCs.
items.author: Rega S, Bouhuis S, Brusati M, Maverna T, Fanotti N, Casaburo M, Vodret S, Riccitelli F, Celotto F, Lambroia L, Climent M, Elia L, Vescio M, Pattini L, Santoro R, Myasoedova V, Poggio P, Bonalumi G, Udugampolage NS, Taurino J, Pini A, Zacchigna S, Pompilio G, Perrucci GL.

items.title: Comparative Diagnostic Accuracy of the American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS) and the European Thyroid Imaging and Reporting Data System (EU-TIRADS) for Thyroid Nodule Malignancy: A Systematic Review.
items.summary: Background The American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS) and European Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (EU-TIRADS) estimate thyroid nodule malignancy risk but use different category definitions and fine-needle aspiration thresholds. This diagnostic test accuracy (DTA) systematic review compared their performance, focusing on ACR TR5 and EU-TIRADS 5. Methods PubMed, Europe PMC, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Google Scholar, and Crossref were searched through October 12, 2026. Adult studies reporting diagnostic findings for either system were assessed. All three authors participated in selection and extraction; disagreements were resolved by discussion. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool and certainty with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach for DTA studies (GRADE-DTA).
items.author: Buckley S, Karoratna AM, Cushing B.

items.title: Group Selection has the Potential to Increase Yield and Resource Use Efficiency in Cereal Crops.
items.summary: The initial stages of crop breeding rely on selecting the best performing individuals, despite these often possessing competitive traits that hinder collective yield. Group selection, where the best-performing groups, rather than individuals, form subsequent generations, is one proposed solution but lacks empirical support. Here we present the results of a group selection experiment targeting protein yield in oat and barley. After eight generations, group-selected oat and barley plants produced higher protein and grain yield than the first generation of plants in the target environment at the beginning of the experiment. Although yield showed an overall positive linear trend across generations, the negative quadratic component indicated a deceleration of this increase, suggesting that further gains may not continue at the same rate.
items.author: Vain S, Semchenko M, Tamm Ü, Tamm I, Davison JA, Zobel K.

items.title: Quality Preservation and Storage Stability of Mozzarella Cheese Using Active PLA/Tragacanth Gum Films Incorporated With Zataria multiflora Essential Oil.
items.summary: This study evaluated the potential of active polylactic acid (PLA)/tragacanth gum films incorporating Zataria multiflora essential oil (ZEO) as a natural packaging approach to improve the quality and shelf life of mozzarella cheese during refrigerated storage. Mozzarella cheese samples were coated with PLA/tragacanth gum films containing different concentrations of ZEO (0.3%-0.9%), while untreated samples served as the control. The effects of these treatments on microbial quality, chemical stability, and sensory properties were evaluated during 9 days of refrigerated storage. In addition, an experimental challenge test was performed to assess the effect of the films on aflatoxin production by Aspergillus parasiticus at 25°C.
items.author: Bargh AH, Noori N, Basti AA, Khanjari A, Gandomi H, Khorrami R, Azizian A, Ghadami F.

items.title: Trajectory as the Diagnostic Signal: Persistent Multifactorial Anemia Leading to a Diagnosis of Coeliac Disease.
items.summary: A man in his late 50s with no documented prior medical history and no laboratory contact for several years presented with inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. Initial bloodwork showed hemoglobin of 170-182 g/L with normal red cell indices, possibly reflecting haemoconcentration during acute illness. Hemoglobin then declined to 126-130 g/L and remained persistently low. The decline was accompanied by transient macrocytosis, vitamin B12 deficiency, severe folate deficiency, and progressive iron-store depletion, with ferritin falling from 186 to 55 μg/L alongside falling serum iron and transferrin saturation, although these values stayed within reference ranges. Repletion of B12 and folate normalized the mean corpuscular volume but produced negligible hemoglobin recovery, and a reticulocyte production index of approximately 0.65 confirmed a hypoproliferative marrow response.
items.author: Manafa CC, Okafor-Udah CO, Okoli N, Adilih S.

items.title: A Case of Multiple Omphalomesenteric Duct Anomalies in a 15-Year-Old Female.
items.summary: Adolescents with symptomatic abnormalities of the omphalomesenteric duct are quite uncommon. We describe a 15-year-old who has an umbilical polyp, cyst, sinus, Meckel's diverticulum, and a fibrous band linking them. This case emphasizes the importance of comprehensive surgical investigation and total excision in atypical umbilical complaints, especially beyond infancy.
items.author: Riaz T, Hameed MA, Singh R.

items.title: Strain-Dependent Fermentation of Banana Pulp by Lactic Acid Bacteria Modulates Bioactive Metabolites and Supports Plant-Based Ingredient Development.
items.summary: Lactic fermentation of fruit matrices can yield functional ingredients; yet the potential of banana pulp as a substrate remains poorly explored. This study characterized the fermentation of banana pulp purée by three lactic acid bacteria (LAB) species, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (P), Levilactobacillus brevis (B), and Weissella cibaria (W), applied as single and mixed starter cultures. At strain level, the three species were assessed for exopolysaccharide (EPS) production, antifungal activity, carbohydrate utilization and cell growth in the plant matrix. All the strains reached from 8 to 9 log 10 CFU/mL within 24 h. W. cibaria was the only EPS producer but acidified slowly and remained closest to the control, whereas L.
items.author: Morandi S, Rocchetti G, Cortimiglia C, Bassi D.

items.title: Hidradenocarcinoma: A Rare Eccrine Tumor Mimicking an Epidermoid Cyst of the Scalp-Case Report and Literature Review.
items.summary: Hidradenocarcinoma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of suspicious or recurrent scalp lesions resembling benign epidermoid cysts. Histopathological examination is essential for diagnosis, whereas complete surgical excision with clear margins and long-term surveillance remain key components of management.
items.author: Eryürük S, Balagué N, Guiotto M.

items.title: Case Image: Syringocystadenoma Papilliferum in a Blaschkoid Distribution.
items.summary: Syringocystadenoma papilliferum is a rare benign adnexal tumor, usually congenital, located in the head and neck region. We report a 52-year-old woman with grouped papules and nodules in a Blaschkoid distribution over the left T4-T5 region, recently enlarging and bleeding. Biopsy confirmed the diagnosis. Surgical excision was advised.
items.author: Adhikari P, Sainthwar SS, Kunwar B, Gupta N.

items.title: Krackow Stitch Augmentation for Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair: Surgical Technique.
items.summary: Despite the advances in arthroscopic rotator cuff repair, postoperative structural failure remains a persistent problem. Retear patterns are commonly classified as type 1 failure, which is associated with the poor quality of the torn tendon edge, and type 2 failure, which occurs at the medial suture site owing to stress concentration within the repaired tendon. Consequently, we propose an arthroscopic medial augmentation technique using a suture tape-based Krackow construct placed medial to the footprint as an adjunct to conventional rotator cuff repair. By obtaining additional fixation in more medial tendon tissue, this technique may reduce dependence on a compromised tendon stump and may also help distribute the load away from the medial suture site.
items.author: Nakamura H, Mitsui Y, Abe R, Sakai S, Higuchi K, Yoshida T, Gotoh M.

items.title: Ultrasound-Assisted Endoscopic Lesser Trochanter Resection for Ischiofemoral Impingement.
items.summary: Ischiofemoral impingement is a rare cause of buttock pain resulting from narrowing of the space between the ischial tuberosity and the femoral lesser trochanter. Although most cases improve with conservative treatment, refractory cases may require surgical treatment. One such treatment option includes endoscopic resection of the lesser trochanter, which is an uncommon, extra-articular, endoscopic surgery that carries several complication risks, such as injury of important neurovascular structures. By marking the sciatic nerve preoperatively and making a portal under ultrasound guidance, this surgery can be performed safely and easily.
items.author: Mitsuya Y, Miyatake K, Kusaba Y, Arakawa H, Tsujiku S, Inaba Y.

items.title: Arthroscopic Flipped Coracoid Transfer (Laterjet Procedure) With Endobutton Fixation for Anterior Shoulder Instability.
items.summary: Glenoid bone loss is one of the most important risk factors for recurrent anterior shoulder instability. Transfer of the coracoid process is a well-established procedure for this. In the classic Latarjet procedure, the subscapularis tendon is split and the graft is fixed with screws. The subscapularis split may weaken the tendon, and screws may contact the humeral head after partial graft osteolysis, leading to cartilage damage. To avoid splitting the subscapularis, the "flipped" coracoid transfer technique has been described, in which the coracoid process is passed above the subscapularis and the superior instead of the inferior surface of the graft is fixed to the anterior glenoid.
items.author: Patzer T, Zolle M, Hofmaier A.

items.title: Satellite Tracking and Citizen Science Provide Complementary Insights Into Spatial and Temporal Migration Patterns of Eastern Buzzards.
items.summary: Individual bird tracking can resolve continuous migration processes but is limited by small sample sizes, whereas citizen-science records provide broad spatial and multi-year coverage but are affected by observation effort and spatial accessibility. However, few studies have evaluated how citizen-science records and individual tracking correspond across both spatial and temporal components of the same migratory system, including migration routes, stopover sites, migration timing, and broad-scale spatial coverage. We integrated 105,630 valid satellite locations from 22 rescued and released Eastern Buzzards ( Buteo japonicus ), of which 10 completed 27 full migrations, with 25,651 records of this species from eBird and GBIF.
items.author: Dong K, Zhao X, Yang Q, Lu C.

items.title: A Multi-Stage Framework for Diagnosing Structural Redundancy Between Selected Functional Diversity Metrics: Empirical Applications Under an A Priori Expectation of Overlap.
items.summary: Functional diversity (FD) is widely used to study ecosystem processes, leading to the continuous development of FD metrics. However, the proliferation of these descriptors raises concerns regarding structural redundancy, particularly in ecological modelling, where the simultaneous use of highly concordant FD metrics may compromise model parsimony.We propose a multi-stage approach to diagnose structural redundancy among selected FD metrics when theoretical, mathematical, or empirical considerations suggest overlap, using complementary analyses across continuous and categorised representations. We illustrate the approach through two pairwise comparisons: the community-based weighted functional dendrogram index (wFDc), which incorporates the species community pool, versus richness-quadratic entropy (RQ) and Rao's quadratic entropy (Q) versus functional dispersion (FDis).
items.author: Sotomayor G, Forio MAE, van der Heyden C, Lozano Rodríguez PX, Goethals PLM.

items.title: Time From Medication Order to Administration of Cabazitaxel vs Lutetium-177-PSMA-617 in Patients With Metastatic Castrate-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
items.summary: Introduction Cabazitaxel and lutetium-177-prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-617 are approved for patients with metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) pretreated with docetaxel and an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor. Administering lutetium-177-PSMA-617 requires extensive resources and coordination across specialties, potentially delaying its administration. In this study, we sought to compare the time from medication order to administration of cabazitaxel vs lutetium-177-PSMA-617. Materials and methods This study used patient-level data from the U.S.-based Flatiron Health electronic health record-derived deidentified database. Inclusion criteria were availability of the date of the first order of single-agent cabazitaxel or lutetium-177-PSMA-617 and the date of their first administration in patients with mCRPC.
items.author: Hage Chehade C, Jo Y, Ozay ZI, Gebrael G, Sayegh N, Hardy T, Ostrowski M, Murdock EG, Ji R, Thomas VM, Li H, Roy S, Maughan BL, Riaz IB, Agarwal N, Swami U.

items.title: Erratum: Editorial Comment: Advancing Patient-Centered Decision Making in Localized Prostate Cancer: Erratum.
items.summary: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1097/JU9.0000000000000497.].
items.author: Schmidt B, Randell ZSW.

items.title: Valorization of Casimiroa edulis seed biowaste into magnetic biochar for efficient removal of ciprofloxacin and norfloxacin from wastewater.
items.summary: The discharge of pharmaceutical wastewater containing antibiotic residues poses a significant environmental concern. In this study, a magnetic biochar composite derived from Casimiroa edulis seed biowaste (Fe 3 O 4 -CSBC) was synthesized by in situ co-precipitation for the adsorptive removal of ciprofloxacin (CIP) and norfloxacin (NOR) from wastewater. The composite was characterized by FTIR, BET, XRD, TGA, SEM-EDS, and XPS to investigate its surface functional groups, textural properties, crystalline structure, thermal stability, morphology, elemental composition, and surface chemical states. Under optimized conditions, removal efficiencies of 95% for CIP and 93% for NOR were achieved at a contact time of 40 min, an adsorbent dosage of 0.3 g L -1 , and pH values of 6.5 and 7.0 for CIP and NOR, respectively.
items.author: Tegie TT, Derbe T, Workie YA, Tessema DA.

items.title: Siamese banana peel-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles and their broad-spectrum antibacterial activity.
items.summary: Plant-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) using agricultural by-products is not only a strategy to develop sustainable nanoparticle synthesis methods but also helps address environmental pollution caused by agricultural waste. In this study, Siamese banana peel (SBP) extract was used as a natural reducing and stabilizing agent for the synthesis of AgNPs. The effects of reaction time, AgNO 3 solution concentration, and the volume ratio between the AgNO 3 solution and banana peel extract on the formation of AgNPs were evaluated using UV-Vis spectroscopy via surface plasmon resonance (SPR). The physicochemical characteristics of AgNPs under optimal conditions were assessed via UV-Vis, FTIR, XRD, and HR-TEM analyses.
items.author: Van Nguyen TT, Nguyen PA, Vu TT, Gia-Thien Ho T, Do BL, Lai CT, Van Nguyen TT, Ta Truong TB, Nguyen-Tran H, Nguyen T.

items.title: Differences in Imaging and Surgical Management of Patellar Instability in Children and Adolescents Between Asia-Pacific and North America: A Systematic Review.
items.summary: Purpose To compare diagnostic imaging practices and surgical interventions for patellofemoral instability in children and adolescents between Asia-Pacific and North America. Methods A systematic review was conducted using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guideline. Inclusion criteria were original surgical studies of patellofemoral instability in children or adolescent patients, with a sample size of more than 5, from either Asia-Pacific or North America. Exclusion criteria included nonoriginal research, cadaveric/biomechanical studies, imaging-only reports, unrelated diagnoses, and adult-only cohorts. Data were synthesized descriptively by region. Results Sixty-eight studies were included, with 15 from Asia-Pacific and 53 from North America.
items.author: Heng WT, Zhang S, Tan SHS, Hui JHP.

items.title: Ultrasound-driven nitrogen oxidation: a sonoelectrochemical pathway to ammonia synthesis boosted by contact-electro-catalysis.
items.summary: Ultrasound activates N 2 , forming reactive NO 2 - and NO 3 - intermediates that are electrochemically reduced to NH 3 . Integrating ultrasound with contact-electro-catalysis significantly enhances N 2 activation and NH 3 yield, offering a simple pathway for sustainable NH 3 synthesis.
items.author: Toghraei A, Guay D.

items.title: Statistically Fragile Evidence Underlies Comparative Trials of Arthroscopic Meniscectomy Versus Nonoperative Management for Degenerative Meniscus Tears.
items.summary: Purpose To assess the statistical robustness of comparative studies and randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing arthroscopic meniscal debridement or meniscectomy with nonoperative or sham interventions. Methods Comparative studies and RCTs of meniscus debridement or meniscectomy versus nonoperative or sham interventions were identified through a comprehensive literature search in June 2025 following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Study characteristics, dichotomous outcomes, and continuous outcomes were extracted. The fragility index and continuous fragility index were calculated as the number of event reversals required to change significance; these metrics were normalized by sample size to calculate the fragility quotient (FQ) and continuous FQ.
items.author: Bosco AP, Rasquinha RD, Voyer E, Rosenberg AE, Quinn M, Marcaccio S.

items.title: Effect of rapid thermal annealing on the optoelectronic figures of merit of a vanadium nitride/porous silicon heterojunction photodetector.
items.summary: Rapid thermal annealing (RTA) is an essential step in the fabrication of photovoltaic devices. It considerably improves crystallinity, dopant activation, electrical conductivity, optical efficiency, and contact formation while minimizing unwanted diffusion. These improvements, in turn, facilitate the fabrication of high-performance devices. In this study, vanadium nitride (VN) thin films and porous silicon (PSi) were prepared using reactive DC sputtering and photoelectrochemical etching (PECE) techniques, respectively. The effects of RTA at 1023 K for 35 s on the structural, morphological, optical, and electrical properties of the VN films and the figures of merit properties of VN/PSi/ n -Si heterojunction photodetectors were systematically studied.
items.author: Kasim ST, Hadi HA, Ismail RA, Hayif ND.

items.title: Competitive ligand exchange of Fe 3+ catecholate complexes with novel biobased chelators: a DFT-metadynamics investigation.
items.summary: The complexation of metal ions by polyphenolic compounds is a ubiquitous phenomenon in both natural and engineered systems, encompassing a vast multidimensional landscape of metal-ligand interactions. An important challenge in a range of applications, including textile care, is the efficient removal of stains formed by polyphenolic compounds coordinated to metal ions at the molecular level. In this study, we investigate the ligand-exchange process between a catecholate ligand coordinated to an Fe 3+ center - a key molecular origin of persistent colored stains - and six candidate chelating ligands using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. The selected ligands were chosen for their potential derivation from bio-based feedstocks, offering promising routes toward sustainable and environmentally benign stain-removal technologies.
items.author: Heshmat M, Kostetskyy P, van Es DS.

items.title: A phosphinic acid bioisostere of hydroxyethylamine as a novel antiplasmodial scaffold: design, synthesis, and in vitro and in silico evaluation.
items.summary: Malaria remains a major global health concern, and the emergence of drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum strains highlights the need for new antimalarial scaffolds. In this study, a phosphinic acid-based analogue 2 was designed and synthesized through bioisosteric replacement of the hydroxyethylamine motif found in plasmepsin inhibitor scaffolds. The target compound was obtained through a multistep synthetic approach and evaluated for its antiplasmodial activity against the drug-resistant P. falciparum W2 strain. Compound 2 showed moderate whole-cell antiplasmodial activity with an IC 50 value of 3.63 ± 0.11 µM. In silico ADMET analysis indicated favorable absorption-related properties and revealed several parameters requiring further experimental investigation.
items.author: Abdou MM, Khodair AI, Qiu D, El-Saeed RA, Bahtati N, Khan FI, Matziari M.

items.title: Modulation of the RNA-sensing RIG/MAVS pathway bypasses resistance to hypomethylating agents in acute myeloid leukemia.
items.summary: DNA hypomethylating agents (HMAs) such as 5-azacytidine (5-AZA) are a cornerstone in the treatment of acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but development of resistance represents a major clinical challenge. Apart from epigenetic reprogramming of malignant cell clones, therapy with HMA is increasingly recognized to facilitate antineoplastic immunity, yet the relevance of these molecular mechanisms in AML remains poorly defined. Here, we show that AML cell-intrinsic sensing of aberrant RNA via the innate receptor system retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I)/mitochondrial antiviral-signaling protein (MAVS) is essential for the therapeutic activity of HMAs. In human and murine AML cell lines, HMA treatment induced robust RIG-I/MAVS pathway activation and subsequent Type I interferon (IFN-I) release.
items.author: El Khawanky N, Nedelko T, Mandracci G, Barth Y, Jiang Y, Wang K, Rosenbaum M, Weiß C, Geisenberger C, Enßle S, Gómez Martínez AM, Göttert S, Hamed N, Fischer JC, Ruland J, Busch DH, Poeck H, Götze KS, Illert AL, Bassermann F, Heidegger SM.

items.title: Wavelength-controlled photothermal reduction of carbon dioxide to produce fuels over Nb 2 AlC/TiO 2 heterostructures in a continuous-flow reactor.
items.summary: A highly conductive Nb 2 AlC MAX phase was coupled with TiO 2 to construct Nb 2 AlC/TiO 2 heterostructures and evaluated for CO 2 photothermal reduction under solar radiations. Incorporation of 10 wt% Nb 2 AlC into TiO 2 significantly improved the photocatalytic performance with 858.8 and 10.5 µmol g -1 h -1 of CO and H 2 respectively with a water-methanol mixture at 150 °C. Using the water-methanol mixture, the CO production rate is 77.7 and 1.7 fold higher than using water and pristine TiO 2 only. Similarly, the corresponding rates were 3.6 and 1.2 fold higher for H 2 production.
items.author: Sharma A, Tahir M, Kumar N.

items.title: Fabrication of guggulsterone-E-integrated chitosan-zinc nanohybrids: surface chemical insights, biointerface interactions and multi-target antidiabetic mechanisms.
items.summary: The research focuses on evaluating the potential anti-diabetic efficacy of encapsulating guggulsterone-E extract within chitosan-ZnO NPs (Gu@ChZn NPs) through a sustainable production method. UV-vis, FT-IR, FE-SEM, HR-TEM, EDX, XPS, and XRD characterizations were used to identify the physicochemical properties of the Gu@ChZn NPs. The UV-visible absorption peak was noted at 320 nm, and morphological analysis revealed that the particles were mainly spherical with uneven surface characteristics and sizes of 5-45 nm. Based on the biological evaluation, it was found that compared with guggulsterone-E alone, Gu@ChZn NPs had a greater inhibitory effect on selected enzymes such as lipase, α-glucosidase, and α-amylase.
items.author: Boomija RV, Kamaraj C, Karthick Rajan D, Thirunavukkarasu S, Al-Ghanim KA.

items.title: Oil-In-Water or Water-In-Oil Pickering Emulsion: Role of Lignocellulose-Based Nanoparticle Wettability and Geometry.
items.summary: Pickering emulsion behavior is governed by particle wettability, surface chemistry, and geometry, yet stabilization mechanisms for renewable lignocellulosic nanoparticles remain unclear, limiting surfactant‑free design. This study tests hypothesis that tuning the surface energy of lignin nanoparticles shifts emulsion type from oil-in-water to water in oil, while combining spherical and fibrillar particles achieves high emulsification capacity and stability through synergy. Influence of spherical lignin nanoparticles (LNPs) and lignin‑containing cellulose nanofibrils (LCNFs) on emulsion type, droplet size, emulsification capacity, and stability is investigated by optical microscopy, dynamic light scattering, conductivity, and field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM). Unmodified kraft LNPs (K-LNPs; water contact angle in oil θ o/w = 81.6°) form oil-in-water emulsions, whereas lauric-acid-esterified LNPs (LA-LNPs; θ o/w = 106.4°) favor water-in-oil emulsions, confirming wettability-controlled emulsion type.
items.author: Solihat NN, Farooq M, Valle-Delgado JJ, Garcia EM, Meinander K, Österberg M.

items.title: Bisspirooxindole synthesis: a comprehensive review of starting material-based strategies (2006-2026).
items.summary: Bisspirooxindole frameworks constitute an important class of heterocyclic compounds because of their unique three-dimensional architectures, the presence of two spiro carbon centers, and widespread presence in biologically active natural products, pharmaceuticals, and functional materials. Owing to their structural complexity and significant pharmacological potential, the development of efficient and selective synthetic methodologies for the construction of bisspirooxindole scaffolds has attracted continuous attention in modern organic synthesis. Despite the remarkable advances achieved over the past two decades, a comprehensive review that systematically categorizes the synthetic strategies toward bisspirooxindole and highlights recent advances has not yet been presented. This review, provides the first extensive and strategy-oriented overview of synthetic methodologies for the synthesis of bisspirooxindole scaffolds reported between 2006 and 2026.
items.author: Ahmadi F, Abdi Z, Javadi M.

items.title: Tracking Temporal Changes in Metal Pollution in Estuarine Sediments: Population Pressure, Pollution Trends, and Policy Responses in India, China, and the USA.
items.summary: This study introduces the Population Normalized Pollution Load (PNPL) as a complementary approach to the Pollution Load Index (PLI) to evaluate sediment metal contamination in relation to population pressure. A global comparative assessment of sediment metal contamination was conducted across major estuarine systems from India, China, and the United States using published data sets. The PLI ranked the investigated estuaries from least to most polluted as: Galveston Bay < Yellow River Estuary < Hudson Estuary < Hooghly (Ganga) Estuary < Mahanadi Estuary < Yangtze Estuary < Chesapeake Bay < Pearl River Estuary < Cochin Estuary < Ulhas Estuary. Temporal PLI trends revealed contrasting contamination trajectories, which reflected differences in historical pollution intensity, population pressure, and pollution control practices.
items.author: Chatterjee S, Chakraborty P, Das A, Roy G, Mohanta S, Chakraborty S.

items.title: Hydrogen peroxide-responsive fluorescent probes based on aromatic imidazole derivatives: design, optimization and biomedical applications.
items.summary: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a key bioactive molecule involved in various physiological processes, including cellular signal transduction, oxidative stress regulation, and immune metabolism. Disruption of H 2 O 2 homeostasis is closely associated with the initiation and progression of multiple diseases, particularly tumors. In this study, we leveraged the ultrahigh brightness of aromatic imidazole carbaldehyde derivatives to design a series of novel H 2 O 2 -responsive fluorescent probes. By integrating two distinct H 2 O 2 -responsive moieties with these highly luminescent fluorophores, we successfully synthesized the probes designated as BTI, BTB, PTI, and PTB, which could be specifically activated by exogenous or endogenous H 2 O 2 in cancer cells.
items.author: Zhu Y.

items.title: Targetoid Eruption With Oral and Ocular Mucositis in a Young Woman.
items.summary: Young adults presenting with fever, targetoid lesions, and severe mucositis pose a diagnostic challenge because drug-induced severe cutaneous adverse reactions and infection-associated mucocutaneous eruptions may appear clinically similar. Correct identification matters because misattributing the eruption to a drug can result in an unnecessary lifelong drug allergy label, and marked ocular involvement may require prompt ophthalmological care to prevent long-term sequelae.
items.author: Jaruvijitrattana P, Tawanwongsri W, Eden C.

items.title: Micropost-integrated acoustofluidic device for enhanced microparticle trapping and release.
items.summary: Acoustofluidics is a powerful tool in the development of devices to focus, trap, or otherwise manipulate microparticles for many uses in materials processing, biomedical analysis, and sample preparation. Most approaches have used the primary acoustic force for positioning and trapping, but this force is dramatically weaker as particles move into the nanoscale. This has driven interest in trapping of particles to surfaces using the acoustic secondary force, which has enabled creation of both acoustically enhanced filters and acoustic trapping via seed particles, effectively trapping particles at the nanoscale. These approaches remain constrained by fluidic drag and limited residence-time control within acoustic fields.
items.author: Senavirathna D, Trujillo RJ, Sellapperumage AF, Oglesby R, Shreve AP, Campen MJ, Graves SW, Piyasena ME.

items.title: Discovery of novel 1,3,4-thiadiazole derivatives as potential dual EGFR/VEGFR inhibitors with activity against breast, colon, and liver cancer cells: biological evaluation and molecular docking investigation.
items.summary: New derivatives of the 1,3,4-thiadiazole scaffold were synthesized and evaluated for their cytotoxic effects on breast (MCF-7), hepatic (HepG-2), and colorectal (HCT-116) carcinomas. The most active compounds (7, 8, 15, and 16) exhibited substantial, broad-spectrum anticancer efficacy, with IC 50 values ranging from 1.58-4.27 µM relative to doxorubicin. To explore their potential modulatory capacity on receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), compounds 7, 8, 15, and 16 were evaluated for enzymatic efficacy against VEGFR-2, and the most active hits, 7 and 15, were further assessed against EGFR. The findings suggest a possible VEGFR/EGFR-mediated inhibition of cancer cell proliferation, with compounds 7 and 15 showing enzymatic inhibitory activity, displaying IC 50 values of 0.42 and 0.23 µM for EGFR and 0.17 and 0.16 µM for VEGFR-2, respectively.
items.author: Belal A, Abourehab MAS, Alsantali RI, Obaidullah AJ, Erfan R, Elwan Y, Gaber AA, Mehany ABM, Sabour R, Elgammal WE.

items.title: Regenerative Medicine in Chronic Inflammatory Dermatoses: A Scoping Review.
items.summary: Background Chronic inflammatory dermatoses persist despite immunomodulatory and biologic therapy, and none of these treatments directly restores damaged tissue. Regenerative products have been tested in several of them, but the clinical evidence has not been mapped. Objective This study aimed to map the clinical evidence on platelet concentrates, cell-based products, exosomes and secretome, and biomaterial-based strategies in chronic inflammatory dermatoses and to identify gaps. Methods Following Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) guidance and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), we searched PubMed on 10 October 2026 (four modality-specific searches limited to clinical trials, observational studies, meta-analyses, and systematic reviews, English, from 2018) for studies on nine dermatoses, including hidradenitis suppurativa (HS).
items.author: Arora S, Arora G.

items.title: Strain-tuned mechanical, ferromagnetic, thermoelectric and pressure-induced thermodynamic properties of the double perovskite Ba 2 InMoO 6 for energy-harvesting purposes.
items.summary: The biaxial strain in oxide-based double perovskites provides significant insight into their electronic and magnetic properties, showing their potential for spintronic applications. A first-principles study of the mechanical, ferromagnetic, thermoelectric and thermodynamic properties of the double perovskite Ba 2 InMoO 6 has been conducted using the WIEN2K simulation package. The structural properties are illustrated via lattice parameters, ground-state energies and optimized curves. The computed values of the elastic constants ( C 11 , C 12 and C 44 ) verify the crystal rigidity, mechanical stability and elastic behaviour, as well as the bonding nature, of the materials. A Pugh's ratio greater than 1.75, a positive Cauchy pressure, and a Poisson's ratio greater than the critical value of 0.26 confirm the ductility of the studied compound.
items.author: Shah STH, Hussain A, Almutairi BS, Khan MN, Nazir S.

items.title: Association of obstetric factors with maternal morbidity and mortality in patients who gave birth preterm.
items.summary: Background Preterm birth is associated with an increased rate of serious maternal complication compared with those who deliver at term. However, data are limited on risk factors for maternal morbidity and mortality specifically in the setting of preterm birth. Improved understanding of risk factors for morbidity in patients with preterm birth can help optimize interventions to best support patients experiencing preterm birth. Objective To assess associations between obstetric factors and maternal morbidities and mortality among patients who gave birth less than 35 weeks' gestation. Study design This is a secondary analysis of a multicenter registry of gravidas carrying singletons or twins who gave birth at 16 0/7 to 34 6/7 weeks' gestation January through August 2019.
items.author: Des Jardin MK, McGee PL, Sibai BM, Clifton RG, Costantine MM, Varner MW, Longo M, Bell EF, Stoll BJ, Allard D, Salazar A, Thorp JM, Reddy UM, Miller ES, Rouse DJ, Simhan HN, Tita ATN, Bailit JL, Dugoff L, Macones GA, Saade GR, Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development Maternal‐Fetal Medicine Units (MFMU) Network.

items.title: Perinatal outcomes after implementation of a blended virtual and in-person prenatal care model in integrated healthcare systems.
items.summary: Background Traditional US prenatal care typically includes 12-14 standardized in-person visits. COVID-19-related barriers accelerated adoption of blended virtual/in-person prenatal care, but evidence from large, diverse populations is limited. Objective To compare perinatal outcomes after implementation of a blended prenatal care model versus traditional in-person care in a large health maintenance organization. Methods Retrospective cohort study in Kaiser Permanente Northwest and Southern California comparing blended care (cases, July 22, 2022 to December 31, 2024) with traditional in-person care (controls, January 1, 2018 to December 31, 2019). Groups were compared using t -tests/Wilcoxon and chi-square tests; multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).
items.author: Fassett MJ, West EV, Gibson EC, Tim LSC, Avila CC, Shi JM, Chiu VY, Chung JW, Rudolph EE, Khadka N, Jentz CJ, Mosen DM, Nonog JC, Audelo JW, Getahun D.

items.title: Beyond symptom severity: Prognostic information from subjective person-specific problem networks in young people.
items.summary: Background Person-specific network models are increasingly proposed to support personalized assessment and psychotherapy, but it remains unclear whether the information they contain is prospectively informative in young people. We tested whether characteristics derived from a brief perceived causal network (PECAN), particularly its perceived relational structure, provided prognostic information about subsequent psychopathology beyond baseline symptom severity. Methods Participants were 361 children, adolescents, and young adults assessed by self-report or parent-report. At baseline, participants selected personally relevant problems, rated their severity, and indicated how they perceived these problems to be related. Psychopathology was assessed with the pediatric symptom checklist (PSC-D) at baseline and approximately 4, 8, and 12 weeks later.
items.author: Vogel F, Jungmann S.

items.title: Morphological Diversity of Basal Ganglia Enlarged Perivascular Spaces in Cerebral Small Vessel Disease: A Report of Two Cases.
items.summary: In cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD), apathy, gait impairment, and executive dysfunction may coexist as the apathy, gait impairment, and executive dysfunction (AGED) triad, particularly in association with hypertensive arteriopathy. Major magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) markers of CSVD include lacunes, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), cerebral microbleeds (CMBs), and enlarged perivascular spaces (ePVS). The total CSVD score, which integrates these imaging markers, is widely used as a simple measure of the overall imaging burden of CSVD. We compared two older female patients with CSVD who had hypertension as the major vascular risk factor and shared the apolipoprotein E (APOE) ε3/ε3 genotype.
items.author: Hayashi M, Hayashi K, Kobayashi K.

items.title: Operant conditioning in Indian free-ranging dogs: effects of positive and threatening cues on sociability.
items.summary: Sociability towards humans is an adaptive trait in free-ranging dogs (FRDs), enabling them to access resources while navigating the risky anthropogenic habitat. We investigated whether operant conditioning shapes sociability in Indian FRDs and whether learned responses generalize to an unfamiliar individual. We exposed 54 dog groups to either a positive or a threatening cue over five consecutive days, followed by tests on day 6 with an unfamiliar and then the familiar experimenter. Using Bayesian GLMMs, we analysed approach proportion, approach latency and demeanour. The threatening cue reduced approach behaviour, increased approach latency and caused a shift towards neutral responses to the familiar experimenter, with the changes occurring earlier compared with the positive cue.
items.author: Nandi S, Roy D, Adak A, Sarkar R, Bhadra A.

items.title: Discovery of new polyacetylenes from the rhizomes of Adenia cardiophylla through activity-directed phytochemical investigation and evaluation of their anti-inflammatory properties.
items.summary: Adenia cardiophylla (Mast.) Engl. Passifloraceae has long been used in traditional medicine throughout Vietnam and Southeast Asia for the treatment of rheumatism, bone pain, and pneumonia. Based on bioassay-guided isolation, seven previously undescribed compounds, including one cyanogenic glycoside (1), four polyacetylenes (2-4, 6), and two cyclopentene carboxylic acid derivatives (20 and 21), together with sixteen known compounds from the rhizomes of Adenia cardiophylla were isolated. The chemical structures were determined by detailed spectroscopic methods (UV, IR, HRMS, NMR), ECD, and computational NMR calculation methods. Anti-inflammatory activity was evaluated by measuring nitric oxide (NO) production in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophage cells.
items.author: Tran DH, Nguyen QPN, Van Thanh Vo N, Truong DDK, Ly TL, Yoon YC, Hoang AV, Kwon SW, Ma CT.

items.title: Uncovering and understanding "transesterification triggers" in aliphatic polyester synthesis with bis-Zn catalysts.
items.summary: On paper, the generation of block copolymers through sequential copolymerisation of two lactones should be straightforward when using a living polymerisation. In practice, this is often not the case, and random copolymer architectures can occur due to transesterification processes. The ability to predict whether certain lactone monomer combinations will deliver block or random copolymers is currently missing. Through a systematic study of monomer features, this work uncovers the impact of monomer substituents, ester functional group density, Lewis basicity, and chelation potential, to identify the key factors that favour or disfavour transesterification. This work uncovers a general trend where the most Lewis basic monomers promote transesterification.
items.author: Tufano F, Hughes JWJ, Neal TJ, Radetzky K, Lamberti M, Garden JA.

items.title: (OTA) 3 FeMo 6 -DES: a liquid catalyst integrating catalytic and extractive functions for room-temperature oxidative desulfurization.
items.summary: To address the intrinsic limitations of up-to-date oxidative desulfurization, this study adopted a synergistic polyoxometalate (POM) - deep eutectic solvent (DES) catalytic strategy to prepare a liquid catalyst (POM-DES) with dual functions of catalysis and extraction through simple stirring. Experimental results demonstrate that the catalyst-composed of an Anderson-type polyoxometalate (OTA) 3 FeMo 6 and a p -toluene sulfonic acid-based ternary DES-achieves complete removal of DBT under mild conditions (30 °C, O/S = 2.8, DES dosage = 0.5 mL, POM loading = 0.02 g mL -1 ) within 30 minutes. Moreover, the catalyst exhibits excellent recyclability, maintaining high activity over five consecutive cycles without significant deactivation.
items.author: Bai Y, Hua Y, Shen Y, Meng X, Yang Y, Zhang H.

items.title: Composition-property correlations of SiO 2 content in CO 2 -based PPC/ionic-liquid composite zinc electrolytes.
items.summary: The performance of multicomponent polymer electrolytes for Zn batteries is governed collectively by the local ionic environment, bulk ion transport, Zn 2+ -associated steady-state response, and electrode/electrolyte interfaces. Here, laboratory-synthesized CO 2 -based poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC) was used as a film-forming matrix, together with PYR 13 TFSI, Zn(TFSI) 2 , and varying contents of SiO 2 , to construct PPC/PYR 13 TFSI/Zn(TFSI) 2 /SiO 2 solid-state composite polymer electrolytes. Systematic composition-property correlations were established between SiO 2 content and multiscale properties in a fixed PPC/PYR 13 TFSI/Zn(TFSI) 2 ternary matrix. Because PPC incorporates CO 2 as a comonomer-derived carbon source, this material platform provides a CO 2 -valorization-oriented electrolyte design.
items.author: Mu G, An S, Ren G, Wang H, Guo L.

items.title: Chitosan- and alginate-based biopolymeric composites for the adsorption of heavy metal ions from wastewater: modification strategies, composite architectures, adsorption behaviour and regeneration.
items.summary: Chitosan and alginate offer complementary amino, hydroxyl and carboxylate functionality for the removal of dissolved metal contaminants. Their practical performance depends on chemical modification, network stability, solution composition and sorbent architecture. This narrative review examines modification strategies, composite architectures, adsorption behaviour and regeneration, with particular attention to chitosan-alginate hybrids. The review links polymer chemistry and fabrication to reported adsorption performance, distinguishing literature-reported capacities from evidence of mechanism and operational durability. A descriptive compilation identifies study-specific results and gaps in experimental reporting. It is not a normalised benchmark or a systematic meta-analysis. Hybridisation and functionalisation can improve selected properties, but the available cross-study data do not establish universal superiority over single-polymer sorbents or isolate donor chemistry from composition and test conditions.
items.author: Aden M, Elmi A, Idriss S, Idriss AI.

items.title: Chiral amines in the asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral allenes through catalysis and covalent chirality transfer.
items.summary: Axially chiral allenes are useful motifs and intermediates in stereoselective synthesis. Chiral amines provide several routes to these structures, but their operational roles differ. An amine may act as a regenerated organocatalyst, cooperate with a metal catalyst, or serve as a stoichiometric covalent mediator that transfers stereochemical information through a propargylamine. This review compares these roles using amine loading, substrate activation, stereochemical evidence and regeneration as organizing criteria. Noncovalent additions, isomerizations and proton-transfer reactions are considered alongside enamine and dienamine catalysis, stereoselective functionalization of pre-existing allenes, and cooperative palladium-amine and gold-squaramide chemistry. Metal-assisted rearrangements of chiral propargylamines provide complementary access to allenes through covalent chirality transfer.
items.author: Alakonda LM, Nael MA, Elokely KM.

items.title: Current Approaches to the Treatment of Hepatorenal Syndrome.
items.summary: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) is a life-threatening complication of advanced cirrhosis that requires early recognition, treatment of precipitating factors, and coordinated transplant assessment. This narrative review examines pharmacological treatment, fluid management, kidney replacement therapy (KRT), transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS), and liver transplantation in adults, with emphasis on HRS with acute kidney injury (AKI). Contemporary diagnostic criteria recognize that hepatorenal physiology can coexist with tubular injury or chronic kidney disease (CKD) and discourage a routine 48-hour albumin challenge. Clinical assessment should integrate perfusion, oxygenation, and congestion, with ultrasound used as an adjunct when available. Terlipressin with individualized albumin improves renal reversal in suitable patients, but a consistent overall survival benefit has not been established, and respiratory failure remains a major safety concern.
items.author: Rosales CA.

items.title: Coordination-gated oxovanadium electrolyte for scalable high-temperature vanadium flow batteries.
items.summary: Vanadium flow batteries (VFBs) are promising for grid-scale energy storage, but their thermal operating window is limited by VO 2 + instability. Above 45 °C, VO 2 + undergoes oxo-bridged condensation and causes V 2 O 5 precipitation, leading to system failure. Here we report a heterocationic coordination-gating strategy to regulate V(v) condensation. In the designed electrolyte, Ti(iv) exists as TiO 2+ -like oxophilic units that form VO 2 + through persistent V-O-Ti bridges. These bridges occupy reactive oxo sites of V(v) species, gating V-O-V network formation and delaying V 2 O 5 nucleation. Consequently, a 2 M VO 2 + electrolyte containing TiO 2+ remains stable for 40 days at 50 °C ( vs.
items.author: Long H, Zhao Z, Liu T, Xing F, Jiang J, Hua L, Chen S, Xie C, Li X.

items.title: Peer review of the pesticide risk assessment of the active substance fatty acids from hydrolysed vegetable oils.
items.summary: The conclusions of the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) following the peer review of the initial risk assessments carried out by the competent authorities of the rapporteur Member State, Greece, and co-rapporteur Member State, Austria, for the pesticide active substance fatty acids from hydrolysed vegetable oils are reported. The context of the peer review was that required by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 844/2012, as amended by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) No 2018/1659. The conclusions were reached on the basis of the evaluation of the representative uses of the active substance as an acaricide and insecticide on strawberry, tomato, cucumber, pome fruits and stone fruit, fruiting vegetables, pulses, ornamentals (annual and perennial), brassica vegetable, leafy and stem vegetable, root and tuber vegetable, bulb vegetable and berry fruit.
items.author: European Food Safety Authority (EFSA), Álvarez F, Arena M, Auteri D, Leite SB, Binaglia M, Castoldi AF, Capilla TC, Chiusolo A, Colagiorgi A, Colas M, Crivellente F, De Lentdecker C, De Magistris I, Fabrega J, Fait G, Ferilli F, Santonja GG, Gouliarmou V, Ippolito A, Istace F, Kardassi D, Kienzler A, Lanzoni A, Lava R, Leuschner R, Linguadoca A, Romano ML, Louisse J, Lythgo C, Mangas I, Mazzega S, Mioč A, Miron I, Molnar T, Padovani L, Padricello V, Panzarea M, Parra Morte JM, Rizzuto S, Santos M, Serafimova R, Sharp R, Szentes C, Theobald A, Tiramani M, Vianello G, Villamar-Bouza L, Becirovic A, Mavriou G.

items.title: Wildfire Drivers, Impacts, and Predictive Modeling: Opportunities in Sensing and Machine Learning.
items.summary: Wildfire prediction and management remain inherently challenging because fire behavior is governed by complex, nonlinear interactions among the atmosphere, biosphere, geosphere, and human influences. Intensified by climate change and anthropogenic activities, wildfires are becoming more severe in portions of the world, degrading air quality, threatening public health, generating substantial economic losses, and producing secondary hazards such as debris flows and water contamination. This review synthesizes recent advances in multi-sensor remote sensing and machine learning approaches for wildfire management, focusing on three key domains: pre-fire risk monitoring, active-fire detection, and post-fire severity assessment. It highlights how emerging sensing technologies and predictive models integrate diverse environmental variables, remotely sensed spectral indices, and geospatial data sets to improve wildfire forecasting, situational awareness, and decision-making.
items.author: Tung JY, Mishra A, Sadegh M, Sabut A, Aghakouchak A, Abatzoglou J, Devineni N, Sankarasubramanian A.

items.title: Metabolic signature combined with changes in proteome and transcriptome shape respiratory syncytial virus infection and response to vaccination in a bovine model.
items.summary: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major respiratory disease in infants leading to long-term morbidity. Bovine RSV (bRSV) serves as a clinically translatable large animal model to understand host responses in neonates to vaccination and re-infection enabling straightforward and accessible sample collection not often possible in human infants. This study probes clinically relevant bovine biointerfaces by combining Raman spectroscopy-based metabolic profiling with proteomics and gene expression in nasal fluid, serum, and lung tissues collected from 11 vaccinated (V) and 11 non-vaccinated (NV) neonatal calves following bRSV rechallenge. The analyses showed at Day 7 post-challenge, 16 significant Raman metabolite peaks in nasal fluid, 17 peaks in sera, and 17 peaks in lesioned lung tissue differentiated V from NV calves including features associated with glucose, lipids and fatty acids, and phenylalanine among others.
items.author: Kothadiya S, Mathew AP, Schoofs AD, Nandu RK, Niolo-Velesaca CA, McGill J, Bardhan R.

items.title: High-precision authentication of cigarettes using surface-enhanced Raman scattering spectroscopy combined with machine learning.
items.summary: Rapid and reliable authentication of genuine versus counterfeit cigarettes is challenging because products vary across brands and production batches. Here, we develop a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS)-based screening method for cigarette authentication and evaluate it across 17 commercial brands using tobacco water extracts from genuine and confirmed counterfeit products. Method optimization identified citrate-reduced silver nanoparticles (AgC NPs) as the most reproducible SERS substrate, and an extraction temperature of 40 °C provided the best balance of signal stability and class separability. Under these conditions, eight machine-learning classifiers were benchmarked on SERS spectral fingerprints; a quadratic-kernel support vector machine (SVM) achieved the best overall performance, combining high accuracy with strong generalization while limiting overfitting.
items.author: Yang H, Huang Y, Zhou H, Xu Y, Huang N, Su X, Peng J, Kong H, Zhao R, Tang P.

items.title: Preparation, Characterization, and Anti-Fatigue Activity of Clamworm ( Perinereis aibuhitensis ) Hydrolysate and Its Peptide and Polysaccharide Fractions.
items.summary: Fatigue is a prevalent health issue necessitating effective nutritional interventions. Perinereis aibuhitensis (clamworm) is a commercially important marine species traditionally valued for its rich nutritional profile and medicinal properties. This study investigated the preparation, characterization, and anti-fatigue activity of Perinereis aibuhitensis hydrolysate (PAH). Optimized enzymatic hydrolysis yielded PAH rich in small molecular peptides ( p < 0.05). Furthermore, PAH effectively maintained muscle morphology, boosted energy reserves (glycogen and ATP), reduced metabolite accumulation (lactic acid, urea nitrogen, and creatine kinase), and enhanced antioxidant enzyme activities (superoxide dismutase and glutathione peroxidase increased by 42.92%-65.34% and 42.51%-52.49%, respectively). These findings reveal that the potent anti-fatigue efficacy of PAH may be associated with the contributions of both its bioactive constituents of BCAAs, putative glycogen-like polysaccharides, and sulfated polysaccharides.
items.author: Qiu D, Fang S, Cui F, Zhou H, Zhang M, Zhao Z, She W, Obadina AO, Wu H, Wang W.

items.title: Push-pull luminescent imidazole derivatives: ICT enables efficient picric acid sensing.
items.summary: Two push-pull fluorophores (3a-b) based on a tri-substituted imidazole core appended with donor-acceptor groups were successfully synthesized by the catalysis of Amberlite IR 120H + and were fully characterized by NMR and mass spectral analyses. The synthesized compounds exhibit strong luminescent properties due to their donor-acceptor (push-pull) electronic structures and possess pronounced excited-state charge transfer characteristics, as evidenced by steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic experiments. Imidazole incorporated with donor groups in the phenyl rings at the 4- and 5-positions (3b) shows a greater extent of charge transfer and emits yellow color in polar solvents like DMSO and acetonitrile. Both the fluorophores were found to act as sensors of picric acid in the solution phase with a very low detection level (nM) by static quenching of the fluorescence emission mechanism.
items.author: Dey M, Bhattacharyya A, Roy S, Majumdar S.

items.title: Quinazoline derivatives with dual EGFR and VEGFR-2 inhibition: insights from docking, molecular dynamics, and in vivo studies.
items.summary: Tumor growth, angiogenesis, and metastasis are influenced by EGFR and VEGFR-2; therefore, dual targeting of EGFR and VEGFR-2 is an attractive approach for cancer management. Here, novel quinazoline analogues 4-23 were designed and synthesized as dual EGFR and VEGFR-2 TK inhibitors. In vitro enzymatic inhibitory activities against EGFR and VEGFR-2 and cytotoxic activities against lung A549 and breast MCF-7 cancer cell lines were evaluated. Compound 18 had potent cytotoxicity against A549 cells with an IC 50 value of 9.41 µM, compared with 9.43 µM for sorafenib. On the other hand, compound 15 had potent cytotoxicity against MCF-7 cells with an IC 50 value of 5.08 µM, compared with 4.94 µM for sorafenib, and poor cytotoxicity against A549 cells.
items.author: Yassen ASA, Nafie MS, Kishk SM, Simons C, Elrayess R.

items.title: Hepatic sinusoidal obstruction syndrome and the search for a modifiable endothelial state.
items.summary: Pyrrolizidine alkaloid (PA) exposure, haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), and repeated oxaliplatin treatment provide distinct contexts for sinusoidal endothelial injury, with differing mechanisms and courses. Oxaliplatin-associated abnormalities may resolve or persist. Illustrated features are conceptual, not validated clinical stages or a shared temporal sequence. Recognition varies by setting and age; the proposed gap remains unvalidated. Current biomarkers and imaging do not establish the reversibility of liver sinusoidal endothelial cell (LSEC) injury. Clinical care remains etiology-specific. Testing whether an endothelial profile can guide treatment selection requires endothelial-associated measures, independent vascular assessment, and prospective evidence of differential treatment benefit. No endothelial-state-based treatment threshold has been validated.
items.author: Zhao Z, Zhang Z, Liu F, Wang H, Yu D, Xu C, Chen X, Xiao Y, Yu Q, Xiong Q, Lai ECH, Tong Q, Chen X, Zhang Y.

items.title: Simultaneous determination of binary diffusion coefficients of hydrogen and methane in water and water-saturated porous media using a pressure decay method: experiments and modeling.
items.summary: Accurate measurement of gas diffusion coefficients in liquid-saturated porous media is essential for evaluating the performance and containment of underground gas storage systems, particularly for emerging underground hydrogen storage applications. However, experimental techniques that can directly determine these coefficients are scarce, and available data remain limited. This study introduces a novel model that simultaneously determines diffusion coefficients in bulk liquids and liquid-saturated porous media from a single pressure-decay experiment. By explicitly separating the pressure responses of the bulk liquid and porous-medium regions, the model estimates the bulk-liquid diffusion coefficient D b and the porous-medium parameter β , from which it estimates the effective diffusion coefficient D eff .
items.author: Aldalawy A, Abdi M, Hassanzadeh H.

items.title: Correction: A cluster randomised feasibility trial assessing an interactive film intervention to improve wellbeing of young people in school settings in the North of England.
items.author: Christie-de Jong F, Walker E, Corlett H, Hardacre C, Soulsby E, Arnott B, Franks K, Ling J, Stephenson J, Azevedo LB.

items.title: Prospective associations between diet quality, frailty and incident cognitive impairment in the health and retirement study.
items.summary: Background Diet quality is a modifiable determinant of healthy aging, potentially influencing physical and cognitive functioning through inflammatory and metabolic pathways. Although healthier dietary patterns have been linked to reduced frailty and cognitive decline, findings remain inconsistent. The interrelationships among diet quality, physical frailty, and incident cognitive impairment, including potential modification by specific dietary components, remain poorly understood. Methods We analyzed 1,636 cognitively normal participants in 2016 from the Health and Retirement Study, a longitudinal study of adults in the United States (U.S.), with diet assessed in 2013, frailty in 2016, and cognitive follow-up through 2022. Cognitive impairment was assessed with cognitive tests and used the Langa-Weir classification; diet quality was measured using the Healthy Eating Index-2015 (HEI-2015); and physical frailty used a modified Fried phenotype.
items.author: Beydoun MA, Wei C, Weiss J, Beydoun HA, Noren Hooten N, Meirelles O, Tsai J, Huang T, Evans MK, Zonderman AB.

items.title: A non-IMiD multi-target degrader reactivates fetal hemoglobin.
items.summary: Reactivation of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) is a validated therapeutic strategy for sickle cell disease (SCD) and β-thalassemia. Cereblon (CRBN)-dependent molecular-glue degraders of HbF repressors are advancing clinically, but all share an immunomodulatory imide drug (IMiD) backbone and its class liabilities. We show that SH6, a non-IMiD small-molecule degrader, consistently induces HbF in erythroid cell lines, primary healthy-donor, SCD, and β-thalassemia CD34⁺-derived erythroid cells, and humanized NBSGW mice, at nanomolar to low-micromolar concentrations. When all compounds were tested at a matched 0.25µM concentration, HbF induction by SH6 was comparable to that of decitabine and greater than that of hydroxyurea, pomalidomide or thalidomide.
items.author: Liu J, Shen Z, Park SY, Dong Y, Yu N, Zeng J, Lee H, Pate B, Adamia S, Vanuytsel K, Zhang J, Wu SC, Herman A, Moein S, Li W, Liu M, Gao C, Tian X, Liu Z, Kwon J, Qin K, Budjan C, Shao C, Li J, Lee E, Arji S, Liu BH, Stowell S, Manis JP, Justus D, Blobel GA, Luo HR, Belizaire R, Zheng Y, Hormoz S, Bassal MA, Nikiforow S, Cancelas JA, Bauer DE, Tenen DG, Chai L.

items.title: Dismantling the immune-metabolic barrier in TP53-mutant hematologic malignancies.
items.summary: Tumor protein 53 (TP53) mutations, long recognized as harbingers of poor prognosis, drive treatment failure in hematologic malignancies by erecting two mutually reinforcing defense systems. Immune evasion is effected through silencing of death-receptor signaling, crippled antigen presentation, and establishment of a T-cell-exclusionary microenvironment, while a parallel metabolic shield fortifies cells against oxidative, proteotoxic, and replicative stress. Here, we propose that immune evasion and metabolic fortification do not operate in complete isolation, but rather as an integrated defense network with emergent crosstalk nodes. We dissect how the spectrum of TP53 mutations dictates the configuration of this barrier, analyze why mono-modal therapies, from chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells and bispecific antibodies to chemotherapy and BCL-2 homology 3 (BH3) mimetics, have shown limited efficacy to date, and outline a roadmap for rationally designed, multi-node therapeutic combinations that may convert these integrated defenses into selective vulnerabilities.
items.author: Su J, Zeng Y, Liu Y, Liu S, Ou K, Peng B, Li S, Li Y, Tu S.

items.title: Monitoring that follows the patient: from the extended recovery room to a continuous, surgery-specific postoperative pathway.
items.author: Bignami EG, Panizzi M, Macagno F, Bellini V.
