items.title: Air pollution exposure during urban running in Frankfurt, Germany: a randomized crossover comparison of particulate matter levels on park, roadside, and residential routes across morning and early afternoon hours.
items.summary: Background In urban environments, physical activity-induced health effects may be diminished by exposure to air pollution. Typical avoidance strategies, such as running through green spaces or avoiding major roads and rush hours, have not yet been adequately validated. This study quantified particulate matter exposure during running across three adjacent urban microenvironments: a major roadside, a residential area, and an urban park, accounting for diurnal variation. Methods Mobile measurements of particulate matter with aerodynamic diameters ≤ 10 μm (PM 10 ), ≤ 2.5 μm (PM 2.5 ), and ≤ 1 μm (PM 1 ) as well as local urban background concentrations of PM 2.5 and PM 10 were collected during 2 km runs (n = 60, pace 8:02-4:31 min/km).
items.author: Engeroff T, Delp F, Niederer D, Groneberg D.

items.title: Correction: Why should more than two reliability coefficients be reported in triage studies?
items.author: Mirhaghi A.

items.title: Model cards are not primary artifacts: stereochemistry in the MoLFormer and SMI-TED chemical foundation models.
items.summary: Pretrained chemical language models are selected, embedded with, and fine tuned on the basis of what their documentation says they are. We report that the released model card for MoLFormer, one of the most widely used chemical foundation models, states that isomeric information was removed from its training data, and that this statement is contradicted by artifacts distributed in the model's own repository. The shipped token frequency table records the tetrahedral stereocentre token [C@H] occurring 669,642,207 times, making it the twelfth most frequent token in a corpus of 47.2 billion tokens, ahead of fluorine, and stereochemical tokens account for 3.17% of all token occurrences.
items.author: Kaplan N.

items.title: Distinct asciminib sensitivity profiles between BCR::ABL1 p190 and p210 isoforms.
items.summary: BCR::ABL1 is the oncogenic driver of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) and Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph + ) acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), with BCR::ABL1 p210 and p190 being the predominant isoforms. Asciminib, an inhibitor that specifically targets the ABL myristate pocket (STAMP), has demonstrated efficacy in both pre-clinical and clinical studies against p210-driven CML, including cases where resistance mediated by ATP-pocket mutations has developed during prior tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. The resistant mutation profile of asciminib is currently considered largely distinct from that of ATP-competitive TKIs. In our study, we demonstrate that several ATP-pocket mutations, including the V299L, F311I, T315I, and F317C/L, confer high levels of resistance to asciminib in the p190 isoform (> 1000-fold increase in LD 50 asciminib values compared to non-mutated BCR::ABL1 p190), but remain sensitive when occurring in the p210 isoform.
items.author: Lagonik E, Quinlan LJ, Page EC, McDougal DP, Eadie LN, Bruning JB, Yeung DT, Hughes TP, White DL.

items.title: Cardioversion and stroke volume index rather than heart rate alone define haemodynamic success of rate control in septic shock-associated atrial fibrillation.
items.author: Balik M, Slama M, Levy B, Fries M, Joannidis M, Makris D, Rehberg S, Guarracino F.

items.title: Subtype-resolved tumor-intrinsic programs in immune-cold breast cancer: mechanistic interactions, evidence gaps, and translational priorities.
items.summary: Most breast cancers respond poorly to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB), and hormone receptor-positive (HR +) tumors, which constitute most diagnoses, are particularly refractory. This review synthesizes evidence on tumor-intrinsic determinants of the immune-cold phenotype in breast cancer under an operational framework designated ICE, comprising three functionally defined domains: Invisibility (failure of antigen generation, presentation, and innate sensing), Coercion (active exclusion and post-infiltration suppression of effector cells), and Exhaustion-by-Metabolism (metabolic attrition of infiltrating lymphocytes). ICE is not proposed as a newly discovered taxonomy of immune evasion; its added value lies in integrating breast-cancer subtype resolution, evidence provenance, systems-level interactions, negative clinical evidence, and mechanism-biomarker-intervention matching within a single operational framework.
items.author: Lin HY, Wang SM, Chu PY.

items.title: Oxytocinergic neurons in the paraventricular nucleus mediate the analgesic effect of electroacupuncture in inflammatory pain.
items.summary: Background Electroacupuncture (EA) is a well-established and effective analgesic intervention, particularly for inflammatory pain; however, the analgesic effect of EA is closely related to the stimulation frequency, amplitude, and acupoint. The underlying neural mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify the central neural projections responsible for EA-induced analgesia and to investigate the mechanisms underlying its frequency-specific effects. Methods In this study, we utilized a mouse model of carrageenan (CGN)-induced inflammatory pain to explore the analgesic effects of EA. In vivo fiber photometry and immunofluorescence were employed to monitor the activity of oxytocinergic neurons in the paraventricular nucleus (PVN).
items.author: Liu J, Wang X, Han Q, Chen Y, Zheng B, Yang W, Wang B, Ma Y, Sun J, Zheng Y.

items.title: An exploratory study on the influence of CT slice spacing on the positioning accuracy of 3D-printed patient-specific instruments designed for a distal radius osteotomy.
items.summary: Background Computed tomography (CT) images with slice spacing up to 3 mm are generally sufficient for accurate 3D reconstructions of patient anatomy. For designing patient-specific instruments, particularly for forearm and wrist osteotomies, higher-resolution imaging (slice spacing of 0.4-1.25 mm) is commonly used. However, it remains unclear whether CT slice spacing meaningfully affects the surface fit of 3D-printed patient-specific instruments. This in-vitro study quantified the impact of CT slice spacing on the positional accuracy of instruments for the distal radius. Methods Data from 12 patients were analysed. Each had a high-resolution CT image (0.625 mm slice spacing), from which a reference 3D radius model and a patient-specific instrument were designed.
items.author: Gryska E, Axelsson P, Libberecht K, Stor Swinkels C, Björkman A.

items.title: RNA splicing factors and long noncoding RNA reciprocally regulate EGFRvIII expression in human cancer cells.
items.summary: Background Dysregulated epidermal growth factor receptor variant III (EGFRvIII) contributes to tumor progression in several human cancers, including oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and glioblastoma multiforme. Although genomic alterations are frequently associated with EGFRvIII expression, the contribution of environmental carcinogens and RNA-based regulatory mechanisms to its expression remains poorly understood and was investigated in this study. Methods Chronic exposure models of the tobacco-specific nitrosamine nicotine-derived nitrosamine ketone (NNK) and the areca nut alkaloid arecoline were established in dysplastic oral keratinocytes. Expression and splicing patterns of EGFR isoforms were analyzed using molecular assays and long-read sequencing. Functional assays, RNA pull-down, AGO2 immunoprecipitation, MS2-based RNA affinity purification, and reporter assays were performed to investigate the roles of splicing factors, long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), and microRNAs in EGFRvIII regulation.
items.author: Peng HY, Chang JY.

items.title: From technique to sensitivity: the transformation of clinical and ethical reasoning in physiotherapy students in the context of chronic neurodegenerative diseases.
items.summary: Background The evolution of Physiotherapy requires a shift from the biomedical model towards bioethical and humanistic approaches. This study explores how final-year students perceive their professional role when dealing with patients with complex neurodegenerative conditions, where traditional technical success is challenged by the irreversibility of the deterioration. Methods Qualitative research based on interpretative description. Thirty final-year students from the University of Almería (Spain) took part, divided into five working groups. Three training sessions and discussions were held on Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), Alzheimer's disease, stroke and Rett syndrome. The data were analysed using thematic analysis and triangulation by researchers external to the study, with reflexivity ensured through logbooks.
items.author: Pérez-de la Cruz S.

items.title: Suicide in youth and its prevention: a public health priority.
items.summary: Suicide is a major public mental health problem in young people. Effective suicide prevention requires a public health approach that address both individual and social determinants. The articles published in this collection sought to better understand the factors that contribute to youth suicide and potential preventative approaches. Four studies reported on either the development or evaluation of suicide prevention approaches, including school-based mental health promotion, risk factor identification, multi-modal strategies comprising assessment, referral, and intervention, gate-keeper training. Development of suicide prevention approaches that can be tested and implemented at scale, and importantly, in low- or middle-income countries is necessary in the future.
items.author: Robinson J, Tong Y.

items.title: Multimodal imaging features of atypical multifocal torpedo maculopathy: a case report.
items.summary: Background Torpedo maculopathy (TM) is a rare congenital retinal abnormality, typically presenting as a solitary, torpedo-shaped hypopigmented lesion located temporal to the fovea with its apex pointing toward the fovea. Multifocal TM is exceedingly uncommon, and its multimodal imaging characteristics and lesion distribution remain incompletely understood. Case presentation A 32-year-old man was referred after an incidental abnormality was detected in the fundus of his right eye. He was asymptomatic, with uncorrected visual acuity of 20/20 in both eyes. Color fundus photography revealed a typical torpedo-shaped lesion temporal to the macula and additional elongated temporal lesions with indistinct borders. OCT demonstrated focal RPE attenuation or loss, increased choroidal hypertransmission, and outer retinal involvement, with a slit-like subretinal cleft in one lesion.
items.author: Lu J, Zeng Y, Xu B, Guo T, Wang J.

items.title: Early warnings about the Galleri test were disregarded.
items.author: Diamandis EP.

items.title: Body composition and blood pressure: Haemodynamic links in young men and women.
items.summary: The aim of this study was to explore the sex-specific haemodynamic links between body composition parameters and systolic and diastolic blood pressure (SBP and DBP, respectively) in adults free of cardiovascular disease and not receiving cardiovascular medications. Body mass index (BMI), fat mass (FM), fat-free mass (FFM), SBP and DBP, cardiac output (CO), peripheral vascular resistance (PVR) and aortic pulse wave velocity (PWV) were determined in 235 men and 192 women aged 18-40 years. Multivariable linear regression and single- as well as multiple-mediator models were used to assess haemodynamic mechanisms underlying the associations between body composition and blood pressure. BMI showed positive associations with SBP and DBP in both sexes (P < 0.001 for all).
items.author: Cseh D, Middlemiss JE, Yu S, Bentley GJ, Williams AR, Yasmin, McDonnell BJ, Pugh CJA, Wilkinson IB, McEniery CM.

items.title: SNRPC-DHX9-RelA Complex Drives Cell-Cycle Signaling and CDK4/6 Inhibitor Sensitivity in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.summary: SNRPC is a core spliceosomal protein, but its oncogenic function and therapeutic relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain incompletely defined. Here, we found that SNRPC was upregulated in HCC tissues and was associated with adverse clinicopathological features and poor survival. In the TCGA-LIHC cohort, high SNRPC expression remained associated with poorer overall survival after multivariable adjustment. Gain- and loss-of-function studies showed that SNRPC promoted HCC cell proliferation and migration in vitro and tumor growth in vivo. Mechanistically, SNRPC interacted with DHX9 and RelA/p65 to form a functional complex that enhanced NF-κB signaling and downstream CDK4/6-E2F1 signaling. Mutational analysis showed that the ATP-binding residue K417 of DHX9 contributed to RelA/p65 Ser536 phosphorylation, supporting a functional role for DHX9 in this signaling complex.
items.author: Xie J, Wu Y, Qian X, Huang J, Jia T, Bian S, Ni R, Zhao X, Huang X.

items.title: Comparison of Wiltse Approach-Based Invasion-Controlled Surgery With Traditional Open Surgery for Thoracolumbar Spinal Metastases Within the NOMS Framework.
items.summary: Objectives To compare Wiltse approach-based invasion-controlled surgery (ICS) with traditional open surgery (TOS) for symptomatic thoracolumbar spinal metastases within the Neurologic, Oncologic, Mechanical, and Systemic (NOMS) framework, focusing on perioperative burden, postoperative recovery, neurological outcomes, pain, and QLQ-BM22 domains. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 30 patients undergoing ICS and 60 patients undergoing TOS from January 25, 2019, to January 25, 2022. Perioperative, neurological, and patient-reported outcomes were compared, including operative burden, postoperative recovery, complications, ASIA grade, VAS score, and QLQ-BM22 domains. Continuous variables were assessed with Shapiro-Wilk tests and compared using two-sided Welch independent-samples t-tests; categorical variables were analyzed using Pearson's χ 2 or exact tests, and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for sensitivity analyses when patient-level data were available.
items.author: Wang P, Shen Z, Zhou J, Xu G, Yuan H, Xu M, Xiao J, Xu W.

items.title: Forecasting Next-Day Alcohol Craving in Individuals With Problematic Alcohol Use With Multimodal Data and a Tiny Recurrent Neural Network: Prospective Longitudinal Study.
items.summary: Background Alcohol craving is associated with drinking behaviors despite negative consequences and relapse following periods of abstinence or treatment. Accurately forecasting alcohol craving is crucial for preventing alcohol consumption and relapse, thereby mitigating alcohol-related problems. Previous studies have assessed alcohol craving using diverse modalities such as psychological assessments, neurophysiological measures including electroencephalography (EEG) or heart rate variability (HRV) at a single time point, and digital phenotypes collected longitudinally via smartphone apps. However, alcohol craving is inherently heterogeneous and multidimensional across individuals and over time, making it difficult to capture using any single modality alone. In contrast, multimodal AI enables the prediction of alcohol craving by integrating complementary behavioral and neurophysiological features.
items.author: Lee D, Lee JY, Lee H, Kwon M, Song S, Yoon J, Jung YC, Ahn WY, Choi JS.

items.title: Robotic Rollator Assistance for Sit-to-Stand Transfers in Older Adults with Mobility Challenges: Within-Participant Feasibility Study.
items.summary: Background Robotic mobility aids with sit-to-stand (STS) support may help older adults reduce physical effort during a demanding, fall-prone daily task. Objective This paper reports a feasibility evaluation of the "SkyWalker" robotic walker, which provides powered STS assistance via actuated lower handles. The 2 trajectories (linear and S-shape) were selected to examine how assistance profile shape influences feasibility, biomechanics, and user experience. Methods Seven older adult patients with mobility challenges were enrolled from a rehabilitation hospital. One withdrew during the robot familiarization (unable to stand up) without attempting any study trial, and 6 completers (4 women, 2 men; aged 70-84 years) form the analyzed sample.
items.author: Mahdi A, Buchner T, Werner C, Hu Y, Mombaur K.

items.title: A Co-Designed and Bilingual WhatsApp-Based Chatbot Intervention (PflegeBot) for Informal Caregivers in Germany: Single-Arm Nonrandomized Feasibility Study.
items.summary: Background Informal caregivers play a central role in long-term care but experience elevated risks of stress, depressive symptoms, and caregiver burden, alongside barriers to accessing preventive support. Low-threshold digital public health interventions may offer scalable support; however, evidence on their feasibility, usability, and contextual fit remains limited, particularly for heterogeneous caregiver populations. Objective This study describes the development and implementation of PflegeBot, an intersectionality-informed WhatsApp-based chatbot intervention, and evaluates its feasibility, usability, and acceptability among informal caregivers in Germany. Methods A single-arm, nonrandomized feasibility study with pre-post assessments was conducted between December 2023 and March 2024. Informal caregivers aged 18 years and older were recruited via community-based, institutional, and online channels.
items.author: Gencer H, Mena E, Freund T, Budde S, Zeeb H, Schüz B, Brand T.

items.title: Healthy Lifestyle Score and the Risk of Cardiovascular Disease, Cancer, and Mortality in an Asian Population: Prospective Cohort Study.
items.summary: Background Healthy lifestyle behaviors are key modifiable factors for the prevention of chronic diseases and premature mortality. Composite lifestyle scores provide a practical framework for capturing the combined impact of multiple health behaviors, but prospective evidence from multiethnic Asian populations remains limited. Objective This study examined the associations between a composite healthy lifestyle score and the risk of cardiovascular diseases, cancer, and all-cause mortality in a multiethnic Asian population. Methods We analyzed prospective data from 9920 participants of the Singapore Multi-Ethnic Cohort who were free of major chronic diseases at baseline. A healthy lifestyle score was constructed from 5 components: BMI, smoking, physical activity, diet quality, and screen time.
items.author: Park SH, Ho PJ, Liang X, van Dam R, Chong MF, Lim CGY, Sim X, Chia A.

items.title: Anticipated Effects of Using a Poststroke Patient Portal for Stroke Survivors and Carers: Semistructured Interview Study.
items.summary: Background Digital technologies are increasingly incorporated into long-term self-management of health conditions, yet their social impact on stroke survivors and carers remains limited. Objective This study explores how stroke survivors and carers view a prototype web-based application ("portal") that allows patients to access and contribute up-to-date information about their health and care poststroke and how this might impact their self-management practices. Methods Through 27 semistructured interviews with 21 stroke survivors and 6 informal carers (performing unpaid care work), we explore the enablers of and barriers to the adoption and use of a portal for stroke survivors. To support discussions, participants were shown images of the portal prototype that displayed various features, including a self-living ability assessment, blood pressure monitoring, and an overview of exemplar personal data.
items.author: Rowland-Coomber S, Huo Z, Mustafa M, Stevens E, McKevitt C, Neate T, Chapman M, O'Connell MD, Emmett ES, Bhalla A, Curcin V, Wolfe CDA, Marshall IJ, Wyatt D.

items.title: Horizon-Aware Forecasting of Hypertension Prevalence and Mean Total Cholesterol in Chinese Men: Retrospective Leakage-Controlled Benchmark Study Comparing Statistical, Machine-Learning, and Neural Models.
items.summary: Background Forecasts of population-level cardiovascular risk factors can support surveillance and planning, but annual country-level health series are often short. With only 30 or 39 annual values per target, model flexibility can outpace the information available for training, making leakage control, repeated temporal evaluation, and comparison with simple baselines essential. Objective The aim of this study is to compare statistical, classical machine-learning, and neural forecasting models for age-standardized prevalence of hypertension (ASPH) and mean total cholesterol (MTC) in Chinese men and to test whether attention or substantially greater neural capacity provides consistent predictive benefit. Methods The authors analyzed 2 officially sourced annual series: ASPH for Chinese men aged 30 to 79 years (1990-2019; 30 observations) and MTC for Chinese men aged 18 years or older (1980-2018; 39 observations).
items.author: Lai W, Subhan F, Zhou N, Khan J.

items.title: Information Processing Mechanisms Associated With Intention to Use Public Reporting Systems: Cross-Sectional Study.
items.summary: Background Health care public reporting (PR) systems are intended to reduce information asymmetry and support informed health care decision-making. However, their adoption remains limited, partly because health care information is complex, difficult to interpret, and may evoke cognitive and emotional responses. Existing research has focused largely on system design and development, with limited attention to how users' central and peripheral-route information-processing mechanisms shape PR system adoption. Objective This study aims to identify the factors influencing users' intentions to use health care PR systems by integrating sociotechnical and information-processing perspectives. It specifically examines how perceived information accessibility (PIA), visual information presentation (VIP), health information comprehension (HIC), information credibility (IC), heuristic trust (HT), and negative emotional response (NER) contribute to system adoption.
items.author: Du L.

items.title: Correction: Effectiveness of a Home-Based and Group-Based Tele-Exercise Program for Breast Cancer Survivors: Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.author: Gao Y, Sun Y, Wang X, Chun OK, Fung BKY, Fung WWS.

items.title: The Myth of Effortless Clinical Documentation Automation: A Critical Sociotechnical Commentary on Ambient Digital Scribes.
items.summary: Unlabelled Ambient digital scribes (ADSs) are promoted to reduce clinical documentation burden, improve efficiency, and allow clinicians to focus on patients. This viewpoint examines the sociotechnical assumptions underlying these claims and argues that safe integration of ADSs requires consideration of how documentation work and clinician oversight are transformed within the wider clinical work system. Their appeal rests on 2 reassuring assumptions: that documentation work can be cleanly automated and that residual risks can be controlled because clinicians remain responsible for reviewing and correcting the output. This viewpoint argues that both assumptions can be challenged from a sociotechnical perspective. Automating the draft note does not eliminate documentation work.
items.author: Preston K, Habli I, Lawton T, Hayat Y, Cunningham A, Sujan M.

items.title: Potential Impact of Breathing Practice on Brain and Mental Health in Rural Adolescents With Psychiatric Symptoms: Protocol for a Single-Arm Pilot Feasibility Trial.
items.summary: Background Mental health conditions (MHC), particularly depression and anxiety, are the leading contributors to youth disability globally. In the United States, there has been a steep increase in diagnosed MHC cases over the last decade. Adolescents in rural areas are disproportionately affected by the combination of limited access to mental health professionals and stigma around seeking care. Current treatment options, mainly psychotherapy and psychopharmacology, have shown modest effects. Prior research suggests associations between slow-paced deep breathing and autonomic function, cerebral perfusion, and stress regulation, supporting further investigation of structured breathing as a potential adjunctive approach for MHC management. Objective This study aims to evaluate the feasibility, acceptability, implementation appropriateness, and participant satisfaction of a digitally supported, breathing-based intervention for adolescents with mild-to-moderate anxiety and depressive symptoms.
items.author: Sharma P, Imsande K, Boos D, Bormann NL, Osman R, Nycklemoe M, Lim S, Arndt S, Kainerstorfer J, Min PH.

items.title: Development and internal validation of a multimodal deep learning model for screening-level lower-limb alignment using plantar 3D foot scans.
items.summary: Lower-limb alignment is a key determinant of musculoskeletal loading and is associated with biomechanical risk pathways for conditions such as knee osteoarthritis and plantar fasciitis. However, routine alignment assessment still relies on radiography or specialist clinical examination, limiting scalability for early screening. Here, we investigated whether plantar foot morphology captured by weight-bearing 3D scanning can serve as a computational screening feature for proximal lower-limb alignment, and we developed a multimodal deep learning framework to support scalable alignment screening. We established a cross-sectional dataset of 167 participants (adults and children aged 6-60 years) with standardised plantar 3D foot scans and clinical labels for arch type, hindfoot alignment, and frontal-plane knee alignment.
items.author: Ni S, Chen Y, Wang C, Zhou D, Liu J, Zhou M, Leong J, Hu Y, Huang J, Wang J, Liu C.

items.title: Integrating the RE-AIM Framework and Theory of Change in the Evaluation of Health Interventions: Scoping Review.
items.summary: Background Frameworks for implementation evaluation and program theory have been increasingly used to support the design, implementation, and assessment of complex health interventions. The reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and maintenance (RE-AIM) framework provides a structured approach to evaluating reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, and maintenance, while the theory of change and logic models explicitly articulate causal mechanisms and pathways of impact. Despite their conceptual complementarity, how these approaches have been jointly applied in empirical studies, particularly in digital health and telehealth contexts, remains insufficiently mapped. Objective This scoping review aimed to map and characterize how empirical studies have integrated the RE-AIM framework with theory of change or logic models in the design, implementation, and evaluation of health interventions; identify levels and patterns of integration; and examine how this combined use has been applied in digital health and telehealth interventions.
items.author: Leite DB, de Carvalho GB, Buto MSS, Garcia ML, de Jesus AM, de Albuquerque E Silva R, de Lima RR, de Andrade MCCLB, Cerri GG, de Carvalho CRR, Schor P.

items.title: Sports App Involvement and Core Literacy in Physical Education and Health Among University Students: Randomized Experiment and Cross-Sectional Study.
items.summary: Background Sports apps can support physical activity through self-monitoring, feedback, and engagement features; however, evidence regarding their broader health-related outcomes remains mixed. The roles of digitalization and gamification in the association between sports app involvement and core literacy in physical education and health also remain unclear. Objective This study aimed to evaluate a multicomponent app-supported physical activity intervention and examine the cross-sectional associations between sports app involvement and core literacy in physical education and health, including indirect statistical associations through digitalization and gamification. Methods This study comprised 2 quantitative studies with independent samples. Study 1 used a Solomon 4-group randomized design in which 120 university students were allocated equally to the pretested experimental, pretested control, unpretested experimental, or unpretested control groups.
items.author: Guo R, Geng W.

items.title: Classroom Integration of AI-Simulated Patients and Automated Feedback in Doctoral Psychotherapy Training: Longitudinal Mixed Methods Study.
items.summary: Background Psychotherapy education increasingly emphasizes technology-assisted methods that extend deliberate practice beyond human supervision. AI has enabled automated skill assessment and patient simulations, yet few studies have examined how students experience such tools in real-world settings alongside established practice modalities. Objective We aimed to evaluate students' experiences with AI-augmented deliberate practice embedded in an existing psychotherapy course sequence. Secondary aims included identifying implementation barriers, ethical and pedagogical considerations, and factors influencing students' acceptance of AI-assisted learning. Methods Participants were 29 first-year clinical psychology doctoral students in a 2-quarter psychotherapy sequence at an American Psychological Association-accredited program. In the fall course, students completed weekly peer role-plays and could optionally submit transcripts to CARE for AI feedback to supplement peer feedback.
items.author: Converse E, Louie R, Safer D, Pacheco JP, Fang W, Kent J, Arnow B, Yang D.

items.title: Climate-Driven Perturbations in Influenza Subtype Positivity Before and After the COVID-19 Pandemic: Observational Study.
items.summary: Background The COVID-19 pandemic significantly altered global influenza transmission patterns. Whether the associations among meteorological conditions, visibility, and influenza subtype (A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria) positivity changed after the pandemic remains unclear. We compared these associations before and after the COVID-19 pandemic in northern China. Objective This study aimed to characterize changes in the associations of meteorological variables and visibility with influenza subtype positivity before and after the COVID-19 pandemic and to identify subtype-specific nonlinear patterns and thresholds. Methods Using 13 years of influenza surveillance and environmental data, we applied Extreme Gradient Boosting enhanced with Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to characterize the relative importance and direction of associations between environmental variables and influenza subtype positivity.
items.author: Lin J, Li C, Zhang L, Zheng J, Niu Y, Lin D, Che Y, Cao Z.

items.title: Imaging-Based AI for Predicting Pathological Complete Response in Esophageal Cancer After Neoadjuvant Therapy: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.summary: Background Imaging-based AI may help predict pathological complete response (pCR) after neoadjuvant therapy for esophageal cancer. However, an encouraging average diagnostic performance does not establish reliable performance across clinical settings or justify treatment decisions without further validation. Objective We aimed to assess the predictive performance of imaging-based AI across neoadjuvant strategies, distinguish internal from external validation, and examine limitations affecting interpretation. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through August 7, 2026. Eligible English-language studies evaluated imaging-based AI against pathological assessment of pCR. PROBAST+AI (Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool plus Artificial Intelligence) assessed study quality and risk of bias; GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) assessed certainty for sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR).
items.author: Li Z, Gao X, Zhou J, Wang L, Ren F.

items.title: Depression Screening Positivity, Treatment-Seeking Intention, and Willingness to Take Antidepressants in a Self-Selected Online Sample of Korean Adults: Cross-Sectional Questionnaire Study.
items.summary: Background Depression is a prevalent psychiatric condition with functional and socioeconomic consequences. Understanding the barriers to professional help-seeking and treatment acceptance among individuals with depressive symptoms is important. Objective This study aimed to quantify depression screening positivity and examine treatment-seeking intention, willingness to use antidepressants, and perceived barriers among Korean adults, with attention to prior depression-related health care experiences. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was conducted in South Korea (March 16-April 5, 2024) via paid social media advertising and messaging app invitations. A total of 1053 adults aged 20 years and older participated in this study. Depression screening was conducted using 2 Primary Care Evaluation of Mental Disorders-derived items, with the endorsement of either item defining a positive screen.
items.author: Kim HN, Kim CM, Park YK, Lee K, Huh Y, Kim W, Kim YS.

items.title: Digital Behavioral Risk Stratification Tool Integrated With HIV Online Self-Testing for HIV Positivity Among Men Who Have Sex With Men: Retrospective Observational Study.
items.summary: Background Due to concerns about privacy breaches and the fear of social stigma, some individuals engaging in high-risk behaviors-particularly men who have sex with men (MSM)-may avoid in-person HIV testing services and instead choose to purchase HIV self-test kits online. Unlike traditional e-commerce platforms that provide self-test kits directly without conducting risk assessments, the "Easy Test Know" platform integrates a structured behavioral risk assessment prior to purchasing an HIV self-test kit, allowing users to be categorized into different HIV risk groups. Objective This study aimed to evaluate the performance of a digital HIV behavioral risk stratification tool integrated with online self-testing among MSM and to determine whether incorporating multidimensional behavioral indicators-particularly the high-risk venue diversity score-could improve the prediction of HIV positivity compared with the platform's existing rule-based risk-scoring algorithm.
items.author: Liu W, Jiang Y, Zhang G, Lv Y.

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Fine-Grained Image-Interpretation Performance of Multimodal Large Language Models on Bilingual Radiology Questions: Cross-Sectional Benchmark Study.
items.summary: Background Multimodal large language models (LLMs) are rapidly expanding in radiology and digital health; however, their diagnostic performance across diverse clinical scenarios and fine-grained visual reasoning tasks requires systematic evaluation. Objective The study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and fine-grained visual reasoning performance of 5 multimodal LLMs with bilingual medical imaging questions. Methods This cross-sectional benchmark study evaluated bilingual medical imaging questions using zero-shot prompting on 5 LLMs: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro, Doubao, Yuanbao, and Llama 4 Maverick. Subgroup analyses by language (English/Chinese), question type (image/text), imaging modality (computed tomography, radiography, magnetic resonance imaging, ultrasound, and nuclear medicine), and anatomical system (neurologic, respiratory, cardiovascular, digestive, genitourinary, and musculoskeletal) evaluated intermodel accuracy and intramodel consistency.
items.author: Liu Y, Zhang X, Xu J, Huang M, Xiong Y, Wu W.

items.title: Identifying Metabolic Pathways That Drive Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Protocol for a Prospective Observational Study.
items.summary: Background Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a disorder characterized by hyperglycemia that is first recognized during pregnancy due to a mismatch between placental insulin production and increased maternal need, exacerbating insulin resistance. Few studies have systematically examined the metabolic markers and pathways underlying GDM from diagnosis through the postnatal period, including placental metabolic changes through metabolomics studies. Objective This study aims to evaluate the metabolite profiles identified through metabolomics, as well as the associated pathways responsible for hyperglycemia during pregnancy and the postpartum period, in mothers with GDM compared with mothers without diabetes during pregnancy. Methods We plan to recruit an equal number of patients with GDM and age- and BMI-matched mothers without GDM.
items.author: Jebasingh F, Harika LM, Anoop S, Christian M, Daniel S, Benjamin SJ, Rathore S, Selvi RV, Beck MM, Abraham A, Preethi RN, Kolthur-Seetharam U, Sonawane M, Price S, Ilhan Ekinci E, Thomas N.

items.title: Comparative connectomics reveals stage-specific gap junction rewiring that reshapes avoidance behavior
items.summary: Environmental stress can remodel neural circuits, yet how such rewiring generates behavioral adaptation remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how dauer-specific circuit remodeling alters nociceptive behavior. We discovered that dauers exhibit significantly shorter avoidance durations than adults. Through comparative connectomics, we observed a substantial expansion of gap junctions within the dauer nociceptive circuit and found that dauer neurons exhibit more transient activity dynamics as a result of this rewiring. Modeling neuronal activity demonstrated that removing dauer-specific connectivity constraints failed to reproduce transient characteristics, validating the functional role of dauer-specific gap junctions. Furthermore, introducing synthetic dauer-specific gap junctions into adults was sufficient to recapitulate dauer-like activity patterns and shorten avoidance duration.
items.author: Choe, D. T., Hall, D. H., Nguyen, K. C. Q. et al.

items.title: Repurposing clofarabine against enteric pathogens via metabolic starvation
items.summary: Enteropathogenic and enterohaemorrhagic Escherichia coli (EPEC/EHEC) cause severe global diarrhoeal disease, exacerbated by rising antimicrobial resistance. Pathogenesis relies on attaching and effacing lesions, where bacteria generate actin pedestals to adhere, replicate, and destroy intestinal microvilli. To identify novel anti-virulence candidates targeting this process, we conducted a high-throughput phenotypic screen quantifying pedestal formation via high-content fluorescence microscopy. We identified the anticancer nucleotide analogue clofarabine as a potent inhibitor of EPEC growth and pathogenesis. Distinct from its oncology mechanism - inducing DNA chain termination and apoptosis - clofarabine competes with bacterial ATP-dependent processes to impede gene transcription, protein synthesis, and Type III Secretion System (T3SS) function.
items.author: Deans, N. D., Naylor, K. L., Srour, S. et al.

items.title: The nucleus spatially partitions mechanoprotection and mechanosensing
items.summary: Mechanical forces shape cell behavior, but how the nucleus integrates its roles as genome protector and mechanosensor remains unresolved. Here, we dissect the spatiotemporal control of transcriptional response to forces during epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). By combining genome-wide approaches, in vivo nuclear micromanipulation, and quantitative live imaging, we uncover two key properties of nuclear mechanosensing. First, mechanically induced changes in chromatin accessibility and transcription are spatially patterned within the nucleus: genes closest to deformations appear protected, revealing a local shielding mechanism associated with chromatin closure. Second, relocating a gene between chromatin environments is sufficient to alter its mechanosensitivity, challenging the concept of inherently force-sensitive genes.
items.author: Bouzignac, R., Palandri, A., Fritsch, L. et al.

items.title: Integrating Long-Read Structural Variant Analysis with single-nucleus RNA-seq to Elucidate Gene Expression Effects in Disease
items.summary: Structural variants (SVs) are a major source of genetic diversity, yet how they impact cell types in complex brain diseases remains largely unexplored, partially due to limitations of short-read sequencing. Here, we addressed this fundamental question in Parkinson's disease (PD). generating long-read whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data for 100 post-mortem brain samples from a PD cohort, constructing a high-confidence catalog of 74,552 SVs. To resolve their functional impact, we integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data from two brain regions from the same samples and focused functional analyses on SVs proximal to genes previously nominated as cis-regulated, potential causal targets of PD-associated GWAS loci.
items.author: Kim, K., Lin, Z., Simmons, S. K. et al.

items.title: Multimodal imaging links molecular identity with nanoscale-resolved 3D cell morphology in opossum cortical cultures
items.summary: In the mammalian central nervous system (CNS), the ability to regenerate after injury drops sharply in the first weeks after birth, but how this change is reflected in cell morphology and organization is still not fully understood. Here we cultivated cortical cell cultures from the gray short-tailed opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and compared cells derived from early postnatal pups (postnatal day 3-6, "Pyoung") with those from older pups (postnatal day 16-18, "Pold"), which differ in their capacity to regenerate after injury. For each culture, we assessed marker-defined cellular composition using fluorescently labeled markers for neurons, glia, and immature/progenitor cells, and characterized their nanoscale-resolved three-dimensional morphology using label-free scanning ion conductance microscopy (SICM).
items.author: Ayar, Z., Pongrac, M., Mladinic, M. et al.

items.title: Functional Performance of Electrospun Tissue-Engineered Heart Valve Scaffolds Across Geometries Under Aortic Conditions
items.summary: Electrospun, bioresorbable polymer scaffolds are a promising platform for tissue-engineered heart valves (TEHVs) owing to their fibrous microstructure, tunable mechanics and capacity to support host-cell infiltration and remodeling. Recent in-vitro parametric studies of bioprosthetic heart valve (BHV) geometry have used silicone cast valves to link design parameters to hemodynamic performance and leaflet strain, but the functional behavior of electrospun whole-valve TEHV scaffolds across distinct leaflet geometries and clinically relevant aortic conditions remains poorly characterized. Here, we present an end-to-end workflow in which polycaprolactone (PCL) is electrospun directly onto parametrized, 3D-printed mandrels derived from two established analytical leaflet geometry models, yielding 21 whole-valve scaffolds across four geometries without cutting and assembling flat fiber sheets or suturing of flat fiber sheets.
items.author: Dillinger, H., Saberi, A., Manenti, M. et al.

items.title: A reformulation of the t-test in single-cell transcriptomics dramatically reduces false positives
items.summary: The default differential expression tests in single-cell analysis software provide fast and simple approaches that help practitioners annotate cell populations identified through clustering algorithms. Here, we use theoretical arguments and empirical studies to show that these tests suffer from inflated false positive rates that affect the resulting annotations. We introduce LN's t-test, which tests a novel, asymptotically unbiased log-fold change estimator and avoids these false positives, without compromising speed.
items.author: Kviman, O., Ferreira, P. F., Jun, S.-H. et al.

items.title: Modulating inter-mitochondrial contacts to increase membrane potential for mitigating blue light damage
items.summary: Mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) is essential for mitochondrial functions, yet current methods for modulating MMP lack precise spatial and temporal control. Here, we developed an optogenetic mitochondrial tethering system, termed OptoMitoTether, that enables reversible control of inter-mitochondrial proximity with high spatiotemporal precision. Blue light activation induced CRY2PHR oligomerization between adjacent mitochondrial outer membranes, reduced mitochondrial nearest-neighbor distances, and promoted inter-mitochondrial tethering. OptoMitoTether activation was associated with elevated MMP and was associated with lower reactive oxygen species (ROS) and preserved ATP production during prolonged blue light stress. Moreover, OptoMitoTether expression preserved mitochondrial bioenergetic function in human retinal cells and extended lifespan in C.
items.author: Wang, Y., Qiu, K., Zou, W. et al.

items.title: Systematic comparison of gliflozins identifies a selective anti-calcifying effect of canagliflozin beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition
items.summary: Background: Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) provide important cardiorenal benefits in chronic kidney disease (CKD), but their effects on vascular calcification remain conflicting. Whether potential anti-calcifying effects are shared across gliflozins or involve mechanisms beyond canonical SGLT2 inhibition is unknown. Methods: We systematically compared canagliflozin, dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in a high-phosphate diet-induced mouse model of vascular calcification and complementary ex vivo and in vitro models, including rodent and human vascular tissues and vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). Aortic transcriptional response was investigated by RNA sequencing. VSMC calcification, proliferation, migration, viability, glucose uptake and bioenergetics were investigated using complementary cellular assays, including OsteoSense staining, Annexin V/propidium iodide staining, radiolabeled 2-deoxyglucose uptake and Seahorse ATP rate analysis.
items.author: Fernandez, L., Brunet, M., Ballongue, E. et al.

items.title: A Double Challenge: Cerebral Blood Flow During Concurrent Breath-Hold and Motor Task
items.summary: Motor activation and breath-holding probe complementary aspects of cerebrovascular function: the response to local neuronal demand and to a global vascular challenge. Combining them tests whether local perfusion responses remain supported when the cerebral circulation must also accommodate a systemic perturbation, potentially revealing constraints that either challenge alone would miss. We used arterial spin labelling (ASL) MRI to investigate whether concurrent breath-holding modifies the regional cerebral blood flow (CBF) response to motor activation. Fourteen healthy volunteers underwent pseudo-continuous ASL at 3T during sequential finger tapping with normal breathing, finger tapping during breath-holding, and breath-holding alone. Each condition included a resting baseline followed by eight 25-second task blocks interleaved with recovery.
items.author: Jakobsen, K., Daiu, M., Critchley, H. et al.

items.title: Higher stomatal density and smaller stomatal size associate with higher grain yield in winter wheat
items.summary: In wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), flag leaf is crucial in determining grain-filling rate and final grain yield. Stomata, microscopic pores on plant surfaces, balance CO2 uptake and evaporative water loss; their numbers and aperture sizes depend on environmental factors. Previous studies have reported associations between stomatal traits and grain yield; mostly under controlled conditions. Our study aimed to investigate flag leaf stomatal anatomical and physiological traits, and their relationships with winter wheat grain yield under field conditions. We measured stomatal density and size, and stomatal conductance on adaxial and abaxial flag leaf surfaces in a three-year field study with twenty-five winter wheat varieties.
items.author: Ivandi, E., Jalakas, P., Tulva, I. et al.

items.title: Time-Resolved Proteomics of a Polyglutamine-Expanded Huntingtin in vitro Cell Model Reveals Early RNA-Regulatory Compensation and Late Respiratory-Chain Remodeling
items.summary: Huntington disease (HD) is caused by a polyglutamine-expanded huntingtin protein that exerts progressive cellular toxicity. However, the temporal order of pathogenic events, and in particular which changes arise early and which emerge late, remains incompletely defined, despite their distinct therapeutic implications. To examine this trajectory, we profiled the proteome of a huntingtin-expressing cell model at early (72 h) and late (144 h) stages. Rather than a linear progression, the proteome changed in two distinct stages. At the early stage, cells showed increased abundance of RNA-processing, splicing, and protein-synthesis proteins, which may reflect an adaptive response to preserve gene-expression fidelity under stress.
items.author: Sonmez, E., Mutlu, P., Ozlevent, C. et al.

items.title: Temporal Dynamics of Multi-Item Working Memory Maintenance in Human Gaze Patterns and EEG
items.summary: Maintaining multiple items in working memory (WM) requires the allocation of limited resources, which may involve prioritizing individual items over others. Previous work has suggested that attentional prioritization can vary rhythmically between WM samples, but direct empirical evidence for such temporal fluctuations remains scarce. Here, we recorded eye-tracking and EEG to track the temporal dynamics of multi-item processing while participants maintained up to three object orientations in WM. Whereas EEG encoding was only short-lived, miniature gaze patterns reflected the orientations of all three items throughout the entire WM delay and showed systematic load and serial position effects. Contrary to rhythmic sampling accounts, however, we found no evidence that eye movements alternated between the concurrently maintained items.
items.author: Broehl, F., Bielefeldt, A. A., Linde-Domingo, J. et al.

items.title: OpenDrive: An Open-Source Microdrive for Large-Scale Neurophysiology
items.summary: Neuropixels-NHP probes have ushered in a new era of high-density neurophysiology recording in large animal models. Here, we present OpenDrive, an open-source microdrive system designed specifically for acute insertion of Neuropixels-NHPs. OpenDrive combines a custom motorized microdrive, six-drive control console, and software platform. Compared with commercially available options, OpenDrive offers (1) low cost, (2) precise, accurate, and stable probe movement, (3) scalability to many-probe recording, and (4) open-source hardware designs and software. In our experiments, OpenDrive has already supported recordings from thousands of neurons across a variety of cortical and subcortical structures. By lowering technical barriers and enabling community-driven development with OpenDrive, we aim to accelerate Neuropixels recording in large animal models.
items.author: Stine, G. M., Gabel, J., Watters, N. et al.

items.title: A nanoscale atlas of extracellular vesicles and particles in Drosophila olfactory sensilla
items.summary: Extracellular particles, including non-vesicular extracellular particles (NVEPs) and extracellular vesicles (EVs), are emerging as key contributors to sensory signaling, yet their ultrastructural organization within native tissues remains underexplored. Native tissues preserve extracellular particle organization and heterogeneity that are often lost during dissociation. Using cryofixation-based serial block-face scanning electron microscopy, we generated a nanoscale atlas of NVEPs and EVs across 352 Drosophila antennal olfactory sensilla ([~]70% coverage). Segmentation of more than 7,800 extracellular particles revealed distinct populations differing in morphology, size, electron density, and sensillum-class distribution. Analyses of EV biogenesis identified multivesicular bodies and membrane budding in auxiliary cells. Furthermore, sensilla housing degenerating neurons exhibited marked accumulation of EVs and NVEPs, accompanied by increased auxiliary-cell EV biogenesis.
items.author: Vijayakumar, P., Cauwenberghs, K., Garg, M. et al.

items.title: The MarR-family regulator TilR links biosynthesis of enterotoxin tilimycin with physiologic adaptation in Klebsiella oxytoca
items.summary: Members of the Klebsiella oxytoca species complex (KoSC) are ubiquitous gut colonizers that produce the DNA-damaging enterotoxin tilimycin (TM) as part of their virulence-related program. A MarR-like transcriptional regulator, herein designated TilR, controls expression of the divergently transcribed aroX- and NRPS-operons responsible for TM production. Deletion of tilR resulted in pronounced induction of both operons, elevated toxin production, and increased cytotoxicity - establishing TilR as the key repressor of TM biosynthesis. TilR is encoded downstream of the NRPS operon and binds a 20 bp motif within the aroX-NRPS intergenic region, spatially separated from the predicted promoters driving toxin gene expression.
items.author: Unterhauser, K., Grassmann, A. A., Balachandran, P. et al.

items.title: Detection of bifidobacterial lipoproteins with anti-viral potential in donor human milk
items.summary: Background: Group B coxsackieviruses (CVBs) are involved in triggering type 1 diabetes. Free bifidobacterial lipoproteins (BLps) prevent CVBs cell infection. Our objective is to isolate free BLps potentially released by bifidobacteria in breastmilk and document their bioavailability. Methods: Bifidobacterium breve and B. longum were quantified by qPCR in samples donated to the hospitals biobank (DHM) within two weeks following delivery. BLps were captured onto CV B4, analyzed by SDS-PAGE and competitive ELISA. BLps transport through Caco-2 monolayers was monitored after DHM contact. Titration of anti-CV B IgA was carried out by ELISA. Results: Among the 90 enrolled donors, seven were excluded, 68 donated a unique sample and 15 donated multiple specimens (2 to 12).
items.author: AYARI, S., Sane, F., Piva, F. et al.

items.title: Chemotaxis and motility of Achromatium oxaliferum in response to oxygen, sulfide, and nitrate
items.summary: Bacteria of the genus Achromatium are known for their large cell sizes and intracellular calcium carbonate deposits. Achromatium cells inhabit freshwater, brackish, and marine sediments where they accumulate to high abundances at the oxic-anoxic interface. These bacteria alter their vertical position in the sediment along with daily fluctuations in oxygen concentrations. Yet, the mechanism behind their migration in the sediment remains unknown. In this study, we used chemotaxis assays and time-lapse microphotography to analyze the motility and chemotactic behavior of Achromatium oxaliferum. Microscopic observations revealed that rolling and gliding were the main forms of locomotion exhibited by Achromatium. In absence of any stimulant, the movement appeared to be mostly random and changes in direction frequently occurred.
items.author: Schorn, S., Ionescu, D., grossart, H.-P. et al.

items.title: WHaloForce enables chemigenetic imaging of molecular tension in living cells and animals
items.summary: Piconewton forces borne by individual proteins within complex assemblies underlie cell adhesion, migration, and tissue morphogenesis, yet remain difficult to image in living systems. Here, we introduce WHaloForce, a chemigenetic HaloTag-based tension sensor that converts force-dependent relief of tryptophan-mediated dye quenching into a fluorescence lifetime change. Optical tweezers revealed a switch-like unquenching transition near 5 pN, and cellular measurements demonstrated dynamic responses to actomyosin activity. WHaloForce enabled quantitative tension imaging of diverse force-bearing proteins (vinculin, E-cadherin, -catenin, and laminin) in mammalian cells, mouse tissue, and C. elegans. Bright synthetic dyes made tension measurements possible at endogenous expression levels. In C.
items.author: Wu, D., Morales, E. A., Lee, J. et al.

items.title: Endogenous Mechanical Reporters Encode the Global Mechanical Landscape of Morphogenesis
items.summary: Developmental systems usually comprise multiple genetically programmed morphogenetic events within a mechanically continuous environment, yet how individual processes interact and contribute to the overall mechanical landscape remains unknown. Here, we introduce the concept of mechanical reporter: endogenous tissues function as in situ probes of the embedded mechanical landscape. We exemplified cephalic furrow (CF) migration as a mechanical reporter in gastrulating Drosophila. Using optogenetics and genetics, we revealed that CF displacement reflects the combined effect of both force and tissue mechanical properties. By incorporating condition-specific mechanical landscape into a continuum minimal-response model, we developed a framework to quantitatively predict the reporter dynamics.
items.author: Xu, R., Gao, H., Li, F. et al.

items.title: Shared landscape, divergent genomes: Comparative population genomics of co-occurring flora in an isolated Australian mountain range
items.summary: Understanding how landscape heterogeneity shapes genomic variation is key to conserving biodiversity and evolutionary potential. Yet conservation genomics is typically conducted at the single species level, limiting our ability to identify shared genomic patterns or understand how co-occurring taxa differ in their response to common environmental gradients. We assessed spatial patterns of genomic variation and their associations with geographic and environmental features among populations of nine co-existing plant species with contrasting life-histories and ecological traits across Gariwerd, a threatened biodiversity hotspot in south-eastern Australia. All species exhibited weak overall genetic structure, although the magnitude and spatial distribution of differentiation varied among species.
items.author: Lobos, S. E., Ahrens, C. W., Rymer, P. D. et al.

items.title: NASA Celebrates Voyager 1 Reaching One Light-Day Distance
items.summary: NASA is marking a major milestone as Voyager 1 reaches a distance of one light-day from Earth, equivalent to over 16 billion miles, nearly 50 years after its launch in 1977. To honor the event, NASA has organized public participation through a global digital light wave using smartphones to flash Voyager's call sign in Morse code. Additionally, the Jet Propulsion Laboratory will host a moderated panel discussion featuring mission members and leadership to discuss the historic journey, current status, and unique interstellar science gathered by both Voyager 1 and Voyager 2, alongside a preview of an upcoming documentary.
items.author: Gerelle Q. Dodson
items.original_title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
items.original_summary: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]

items.title: Foundation Model Adaptation Outperforms Task-Specific Training Across Medical Imaging Sites
items.summary: Researchers investigated whether pretrained foundation models can replace task-specific training for medical image segmentation by adapting the DINOv2 model and comparing it against U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Testing across colonoscopy, breast ultrasound, and dermoscopy datasets demonstrated that the adapted foundation model generalized better on every independent external dataset from other institutions. Within the original training distribution, traditional task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant and delineated boundaries more accurately, whereas the foundation model occasionally missed smaller lesions. The experiments also revealed that only a small portion of the foundation model needs tuning, with the required capacity dictated by the imaging domain rather than the adaptation strategy.
items.author: Emre Kutlusan, Yongmin Li
items.original_title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.original_summary: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch.
items.ai_title: Foundation Model Adaptation Outperforms Task-Specific Training Across Medical Imaging Sites

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning.
items.author: Sheethal Bhat, Bogdan Georgescu, Awais Mansoor et al.

items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.summary: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes.
items.author: Alex Shtoff

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns.
items.author: Zijian Zhang, Rizhen Hu, Jiangweizhi Peng et al.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation.
items.author: Ziang Liu, James J. Kim, Yijia Dai et al.

items.title: Solving the SU(2) BFSS model
items.summary: We numerically solve the ground state wavefunction of SU(2) BFSS matrix quantum mechanics. We compare ground correlators against islands obtained using the matrix bootstrap and find agreement up to five significant figures. The power law tail of this wavefunction determines the three-point amplitude, which agrees with the computation of Herderschee and Maldacena. Beyond the ground state, we extract the non-perturbative four-point scattering amplitude using Lüscher's method. In the appropriate regime, we find agreement with the Born-Oppenheimer approximation that yields the well-known $v^4/r^7$ interaction. We also find explicit bound states with positive energies in various SO(9) irreps. These are closely related to the bound states whose existence was recently discovered by OpenAI.
items.author: Kabir Bajaj, Henry W. Lin

items.title: Pyrite Benchmark Evaluates AI Agents in Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking
items.summary: Predicting how a ligand binds to a target remains a major challenge in small-molecule drug discovery. To address this, researchers developed Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark containing 1,500 pose pairs across various protein-ligand complexes. Tests showed that expert chemists using 3D tools and physics-based scores perform close to random chance. To test automated solutions, the authors introduced PyriteRep, a structured representation of chemical and geometric signals, alongside two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner and PyriteFeaturizer. The agents achieved up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, outperforming human experts. Furthermore, LLM-guided feature discovery surpassed direct reasoning, while optimization techniques allowed open-weight models to match or exceed closed-source alternatives.
items.author: Megha Srivastava, Michael H. Lim, Allison M. Keys et al.
items.original_title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.original_summary: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls.

items.title: Assessing Connectome Structure-Function Claims Against Unmeasured Physiology
items.summary: Connectome-constrained models are frequently used to claim that a measured biological wiring diagram dictates function, though such models often confound wiring patterns with tuning choices like excitability or plasticity. Researchers tested three distinct estimands using synthetic ground truths, placebo nulls, and three Drosophila circuit models to evaluate these claims. While certain biological conclusions proved robust across protocols, others shifted significantly depending on physiological constraints and model parameters. For instance, models of the fly mushroom body showed that real wiring could either outperform or lose to shuffled alternatives depending on active cell shares, highlighting underlying model inadequacies rather than wiring deficits. The study concludes that validating structural claims requires properly matched optimization alongside data-constrained physiology.
items.author: Yeyuan Liu
items.original_title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.original_summary: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models.

items.title: Continual-ARC Benchmark Measures Lifelong Skill Acquisition in AI Agents
items.summary: Evaluating continual learning in AI agents has historically been hindered by single-domain limits and inconsistent comparison scales between memory-based and weight-based systems. Continual-ARC addresses this by introducing a lifelong stream built from ARC-AGI task editions that require no prior domain knowledge, featuring recurring tasks with fresh instances and incoming new tasks. The framework scores learners based on feedback consumption budgets and tests both memorization of seen tasks and generalization to unseen tasks. Testing models like Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash revealed that harness persistence generally fails to improve memorization without explicit expert guidance, and harness methods typically underperform simple demonstration caching. However, weight-based learning demonstrated substantial gains on unseen tasks, pointing toward future continual learning applications.
items.author: Daniel Lenton
items.original_title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.original_summary: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for.

items.title: Bonbon Foundation Model Exhibits Emergent Capabilities in Molecular Interactions
items.summary: Trained on roughly 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences without task-specific supervision or structural coordinates, Bonbon is a multimodal foundation model for molecular interactions. From a single representation space, the model displays zero-shot emergent capabilities across functional, residue, and bond resolution levels that generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Controlled scaling experiments revealed sharp performance jumps at the largest model scale of 1.6 billion parameters, demonstrating that standard pretraining loss curves do not predict these sudden capabilities. Achieving state-of-the-art binding prediction speeds, prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets yielded a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, successfully discovering structurally novel inhibitory molecules.
items.author: Adi Mashiach
items.original_title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.original_summary: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly.

items.title: Comparing Evaluation Frameworks for Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.summary: Deploying LLM analytics agents in enterprise environments requires robust evaluation methods to detect failures across multi-tool workflows. A three-phase study compared three frameworks—trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics—using frozen execution traces and two analytics agents. Phase 1 showed high evaluation harness stability across 97% of configurations. Phase 2 found that trace-based judging achieved the best precision-recall balance on known risks, whereas text-only evaluation produced five times more false alarms. Phase 3 uncovered 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. The findings indicate that evaluation quality depends heavily on available harness information, and recommend combining trace-based functional assessment with adversarial red-teaming for security validation.
items.author: Howard Zhang, Chuck Arvin, Logan Brown et al.
items.original_title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.original_summary: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms.
